exercises.explanation: After the preposition у, его́ becomes него́.
exercises.promptTranslation: He has a sister.
She has a family.
We have a house.
They have children.

exercises.explanation: The thing you have stays nominative.
exercises.promptTranslation: I have a big family.
We had a car.

exercises.prompt: Why is there no есть in “У него́ но́вая маши́на”?
options: The sentence describes the car, not the fact of having one
exercises.explanation: You can drop есть when the focus is a description.

exercises.prompt: How do you ask a polite “Do you have a family?”

lessons.title: 47. Liking things: мне нра́вится
lessons.subtitle: Мне нра́вится го́род, мне нра́вятся фи́льмы

explanations.title: The thing pleases you
explanations.body: Russian does not say “I like the city”. It says “the city is pleasing to me”: Мне нра́вится го́род. The person is in a special form (мне, тебе́, ему́, ей, нам, вам, им), the thing liked is the subject, and the verb agrees with it: нра́вится for one thing or an activity, нра́вятся for several. After нра́вится you can also use an infinitive.

explanations.title: Нра́виться or люби́ть?
explanations.body: Нра́виться is a lighter feeling: a preference, a taste, a first impression, or a compliment. Люби́ть is for deep, lasting feelings: family, your country, a long-time favourite. To compliment someone's dress say Мне нра́вится ва́ше пла́тье!, not Я люблю́ ва́ше пла́тье. When you see a film for the first time and enjoy it, you say Мне понра́вился э́тот фильм, using the past tense and the perfective verb понра́виться.

examples.translation: I love my family.
I like this film.
I really liked this film.

exercises.explanation: The person who likes is in the form мне.
exercises.promptTranslation: I like this city.
She likes this book.
We like new films.
I like walking in the park.
Do you like this film?
They like this city.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means “I like these books”?
What is the grammatical subject in “Мне нра́вится го́род”?
exercises.explanation: The thing liked is the subject; it is in the nominative.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is the natural compliment about a dress?
exercises.explanation: Use нра́виться for taste and compliments.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence expresses a deep, long-held feeling?

lessons.title: 48. Both of us: о́ба, о́бе; и … и …, ни … ни …
lessons.subtitle: Мы о́ба студе́нты, они́ о́бе врачи́

explanations.title: О́ба or о́бе
explanations.body: О́ба and о́бе mean “both”. They have two forms: о́бе for two women (or two feminine nouns) and о́ба for everything else: two men, or a man and a woman together. In the plural pronouns they follow the pronoun.

tables.note: “Anything else” = two men, or a man and a woman.

examples.text: Я студе́нт, и мой друг студе́нт. Мы о́ба студе́нты.
examples.translation: I'm a student and my friend is a student. We are both students.

examples.text: Ма́ма и сестра́ — врачи́. Они́ о́бе врачи́.
examples.translation: Mom and my sister are doctors. They are both doctors.

examples.text: Муж и жена́ до́ма. Они́ о́ба до́ма.
examples.translation: The husband and wife are at home. They are both at home.

explanations.title: Both … and, neither … nor
explanations.body: To translate “both A and B”, do not use о́ба: say и … и …. “Neither A nor B” is ни … ни …, and the verb must still be negated with не.

examples.text: И мой брат, и его́ друг — студе́нты.
examples.translation: Both my brother and his friend are students.

examples.text: Ни она́, ни её сестра́ не иду́т в кино́.
examples.translation: Neither she nor her sister is going to the movies.

exercises.prompt: Мой брат и я — студе́нты. Мы ___ студе́нты.
exercises.promptTranslation: My brother and I are students. We are both students.

exercises.prompt: Ма́ма и сестра́ — врачи́. Они́ ___ врачи́.
exercises.promptTranslation: Mom and my sister are doctors. They are both doctors.

exercises.prompt: Па́па и ма́ма до́ма. Они́ ___ до́ма.
exercises.explanation: A man and a woman: о́ба.
exercises.promptTranslation: Dad and mom are at home. They are both at home.
You are both my friends.

exercises.prompt: ___ мой брат, и его́ друг — студе́нты.
exercises.explanation: Both … and is и … и …, not о́ба.
exercises.promptTranslation: Both my brother and his friend are students.

exercises.prompt: Ни она́, ни её сестра́ ___ иду́т в кино́.
exercises.explanation: After ни … ни … the verb takes не.
exercises.promptTranslation: Neither she nor her sister is going to the movies.

exercises.prompt: Which word do you use for two women?
What happens to the verb after ни … ни …?
options: It must be negated with не

exercises.prompt: A man and his wife are doctors. “They are both doctors.” Which is right?

lessons.title: 49. Such and so: тако́й and так
lessons.subtitle: Тако́й интере́сный фильм! Он так бы́стро чита́ет.

explanations.title: Two words, two jobs
explanations.body: Both words mean “so” or “such”, but they attach to different things. Тако́й is an adjective: it goes with a noun, or with an adjective that describes one, and it agrees with the noun in gender, number and case (тако́й, така́я, тако́е, таки́е). Так is an adverb: it goes with a verb or another adverb and never changes.

examples.translation: Your car is so beautiful!

examples.text: У меня́ уже́ есть така́я кни́га.
examples.translation: I already have such a book.
It's so beautiful here.
He speaks English so badly.

exercises.promptTranslation: This is such an interesting book.
He reads so fast.

exercises.explanation: Краси́во is an adverb, so так.
exercises.promptTranslation: It's so beautiful here.
This is such a big house!
I already have such a car.
Your books are so interesting!

exercises.prompt: Which word modifies a verb or an adverb?

exercises.explanation: Gender, number and case of the noun.

units.title: Unit 8: Getting around town

lessons.title: 50. Going by vehicle: е́хать and е́здить
lessons.subtitle: Еду́ сейча́с, е́зжу ка́ждый день

explanations.title: The vehicle twins of идти́ and ходи́ть
explanations.body: When you travel by car, bus, train or any vehicle, Russian uses е́хать (one trip in one direction, right now, with a destination, or a planned trip) and е́здить (habits, round trips, general ability, liking, negative commands). They work exactly like идти́ and ходи́ть. To stress that you go on foot, add пешко́м: Я хожу́ на рабо́ту пешко́м.

tables.note: Past: е́хал, е́хала, е́хали · е́здил, е́здила, е́здили. Е́здить has the д → ж change in the я-form.

explanations.title: Which one?
explanations.body: Same logic as for walking. Сейча́с, куда́?, за́втра (a planned trip) point to е́хать; ка́ждый день, ча́сто, люблю́ point to е́здить. In the past е́здил means a round trip, so Вчера́ я е́здил на ры́нок means I went there and came back. For a positive command to go by vehicle use поезжа́й(те); for a negative one, не е́зди(те).

examples.translation: Right now I'm driving home.

examples.text: Ка́ждую суббо́ту я е́зжу на ры́нок.
examples.translation: Every Saturday I go to the market.
Tomorrow we are going to the airport.
Yesterday he went to the market (and came back).
Go by subway!

exercises.prompt: Ка́ждую суббо́ту я ___ на ры́нок на авто́бусе.
exercises.explanation: A weekly habit by bus: е́здить.
exercises.promptTranslation: Every Saturday I go to the market by bus.

exercises.prompt: Сейча́с мы ___ в аэропо́рт на такси́.
exercises.explanation: Right now, one direction, by vehicle: е́хать.
exercises.promptTranslation: Right now we're going to the airport by taxi.
I don't like driving.
Tomorrow they are going to Moscow.

exercises.explanation: A positive command to go by vehicle: поезжа́й.
exercises.promptTranslation: Go by subway!
I go to the institute on foot.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means “Yesterday he went to the market (and came back)”?
exercises.explanation: Past е́здил = a completed round trip.

exercises.prompt: Which verb fits “Every day I go to work by car”?
What do you add to ходи́ть/идти́ to stress that you go on foot?

lessons.title: 51. By bus, on the bus: на and в with transport
lessons.subtitle: На авто́бусе, в авто́бусе

explanations.title: How you travel vs where you are
explanations.body: To say how you travel use на plus the prepositional case: е́хать на авто́бусе, на по́езде, на маши́не. To say where you are, inside the vehicle, use в plus the prepositional: в авто́бусе, в по́езде. Two nouns never change: метро́ and такси́. Because they do not decline, only на or в (and the context) shows the difference.

examples.translation: I go there by bus.
On the bus I read the paper.
We are traveling by train.
You may not smoke on a train.

exercises.promptTranslation: I go to work by bus.
On the bus I read the paper.
We're going home by train.
You can't smoke on a train.
We're going to the airport by taxi.
I like to ride a bicycle.

exercises.prompt: What is special about метро́ and такси́?
exercises.explanation: Indeclinable nouns look the same in every case.

lessons.title: 52. In the forest, on the bridge: the second prepositional
lessons.subtitle: В лесу́, на мосту́, в саду́

explanations.title: Place: stressed -у́
explanations.body: A small group of masculine nouns, mostly one-syllable, has two prepositional forms. To say where something is after в or на, they take a stressed -у́ (or -ю́): в лесу́, в саду́, на мосту́. To say what you are talking about after о, they use the ordinary -е: о ле́се, о са́де, о мосте́. Learn them as pairs, because the stress changes too.

examples.translation: My uncle works in the garden.
He often talks about the garden.
The car is standing on the bridge.
All my things are in the wardrobe.

exercises.promptTranslation: We're walking in the forest.
He's talking about the forest.
My uncle works in the garden.
I see a car on the bridge.
The book is on the floor.
All my things are in the wardrobe.

exercises.explanation: Place: the о drops out too: у́гол → углу́.
exercises.promptTranslation: He's waiting on the corner.

exercises.prompt: Which ending marks the “place” form of лес?
Which form is used for “about the forest”?

lessons.title: 53. About me, about him: pronouns in the prepositional
lessons.subtitle: Обо мне́, о нём, о ней

explanations.title: Seven forms
explanations.body: Personal pronouns have a prepositional case, used after о, в, на and other prepositions that take it. The forms for он, она́ and они́ always start with н because a preposition always stands in front of them. With мне, о becomes обо and в becomes во.

examples.translation: What do you see in me?
I'm thinking about you.
We're talking about him.

exercises.promptTranslation: I'm thinking about him.
We're talking about her.
They're talking about us.
He's thinking about me.
What do you see in me?
We're telling about them.
I'm thinking about you.

exercises.explanation: Prepositional of я: мне, with обо.

exercises.prompt: Why is it о нём and not о него́?
options: The prepositional of он is нём
exercises.explanation: Он → нём, она́ → ней, они́ → них.

exercises.prompt: Which pronoun has ней in the prepositional?

lessons.title: 54. Nobody, nothing, never: ни- words
lessons.subtitle: Никто́, ничего́, никогда́, нигде́, никуда́

explanations.title: Add ни- to a question word
explanations.body: Negative pronouns and adverbs are made by putting ни- in front of a question word. The key rule: the verb must still carry не. Russian does not mind a double (or triple) negative; it requires it. Ничто́ (nothing) is only used as a subject; the usual form after a negated verb is ничего́.

explanations.title: In sentences
explanations.body: Put не right before the verb, and the ни- word wherever it fits. Remember: нигде́ is for where something is, никуда́ is for where someone goes. The particle не can also negate a single word other than the verb: Я рабо́таю не здесь, а там.

examples.translation: He never works.
I don't know anything.
They aren't going anywhere.
I didn't see anyone.
No one knows.

exercises.promptTranslation: I don't know anything.
He never works.
We're not going anywhere.
My friend doesn't work anywhere.

exercises.explanation: Not anyone, as an object: никого́.
exercises.promptTranslation: I don't know anyone here.

exercises.explanation: No one, as a subject: никто́.
exercises.promptTranslation: No one knows this.

exercises.prompt: What must a sentence with никогда́ also have?
How do you say “I didn't see anyone”?

lessons.title: 55. Can and want: мочь and хоте́ть
lessons.subtitle: Могу́, хочу́

explanations.title: Two irregular verbs
explanations.body: Мочь (can, to be able to) and хоте́ть (to want) are irregular, and both are followed by an infinitive. Мочь has a changing stem (мог-/мож-). Хоте́ть is a mix: its singular forms follow the first family and its plural forms the second.

tables.note: Past: мог, могла́, могло́, могли́ · хоте́л, хоте́ла, хоте́ло, хоте́ли.

examples.translation: I can read Russian.
Can you speak slowly?

examples.text: Он хо́чет купи́ть маши́ну, но не мо́жет.
examples.translation: He wants to buy a car, but he can't.
We want to go home.

explanations.title: Can vs. may
explanations.body: You already know мо́жно (it is allowed) and нельзя́ (it is not allowed). They describe permission with no subject. Мочь with a person says that someone is able, or has the opportunity, to do something: Здесь мо́жно кури́ть (it is allowed), but Я не могу́ кури́ть (I can't, perhaps because I'm ill).

exercises.promptTranslation: I can read Russian.
Can you speak slowly?

exercises.explanation: Plural forms of хоте́ть follow the second family: хоти́м.
exercises.promptTranslation: We want to buy this car.
They want to go home.
Yesterday she couldn't talk.

exercises.prompt: Он ___ купи́ть маши́ну, но не мо́жет.
exercises.promptTranslation: He wants to buy a car, but he can't.

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between мо́жно and я могу́?
options: Мо́жно says it is allowed; я могу́ says I am able

lessons.title: 56. Asking the way
lessons.subtitle: Извини́те, как попа́сть на вокза́л?

explanations.title: Useful questions
explanations.body: Start with Извини́те (excuse me). Then ask where something is, or how to get there. Нахо́дится (is located) agrees with what you ask about: нахо́дится for one thing, нахо́дятся for several. Как попа́сть в … / на … ? takes the accusative, so use the same в or на that the place takes.

rows: How do I get to the museum?
How do I get to the station?

explanations.title: Answers
explanations.body: Directions use commands (иди́те, поезжа́йте) and a few small words: пря́мо (straight on), напра́во (to the right), нале́во (to the left), далеко́ (far), недалеко́ (not far), ря́дом (nearby). A distance can be one block: оди́н кварта́л.

examples.translation: Go straight, then left.
The station isn't far.
Is the square far?
Go one block straight ahead.
The subway is nearby.

exercises.explanation: Музе́й takes в; Как попа́сть + accusative.
exercises.promptTranslation: How do I get to the museum?
How do I get to the station?
Go straight, then left.
Excuse me, where is the station located?
Where are the stops located?

exercises.prompt: What case follows Как попа́сть в …?
How do you ask “Where is the museum located?”

lessons.title: 57. Review: walking, riding, having, liking
lessons.subtitle: Putting lessons 42 to 56 together

explanations.title: What do I need?
explanations.body: A map of what you have learned since lesson 42. Use it to choose a form before you speak.

lessons.title: 58. Adjectives in the prepositional: -ом and -ой
lessons.subtitle: В краси́вом го́роде, в но́вой кни́ге

explanations.title: The adjective changes with its noun
explanations.body: In lesson 16 you learned that a noun takes the prepositional ending after в, на or о. A describing word in front of that noun changes too, because adjectives always agree with their noun in gender, number and case. In the singular, a masculine or neuter adjective ends in -ом, and a feminine one ends in -ой. Masculine and neuter match, just as they matched for nouns.

tables.note: Both words change, and the adjective ending is the one you hear first. This lesson covers the regular hard-stem endings. Soft stems and the spelling rules come next.

explanations.title: Using it
explanations.body: Everything you know about в and на still applies. Only the adjective is new. When the adjective stands after о, remember to use об before a vowel: об интере́сной кни́ге.

lessons.title: 59. Soft stems and spelling: -ем, -ей and the spelling rules
lessons.subtitle: В си́нем пла́тье, в ру́сском словаре́, в хоро́шей кни́ге

explanations.title: Soft stems: -ем and -ей
explanations.body: Adjectives that end in -ий, -яя or -ее in the nominative are soft-stem adjectives. In the prepositional they take -ем for masculine and neuter, and -ей for feminine, instead of -ом and -ой. Look at the dictionary form to decide which set you need.

explanations.title: The spelling rules still apply
explanations.body: The two spelling rules from lesson 25 decide what happens after certain letters. After г, к, х you always write -ом and -ой, whatever the stress. After ж, ч, ш, щ you write -ем and -ей when the ending is unstressed, but -ом and -ой when it is stressed. That is why a stressed ending still sounds like -ой: большо́й, большо́м.

tables.note: Ру́сский and ма́ленький follow the г/к/х rule. Хоро́ший has an unstressed ending, so it keeps -ем/-ей. Большо́й has a stressed ending, so it takes -ом/-ой.

lessons.title: 60. My, this, which, first: pronouns and ordinals in the prepositional
lessons.subtitle: О моём бра́те, об э́той кни́ге, на тре́тьем этаже́

explanations.title: Same pattern, a few special forms
explanations.body: Possessives, demonstratives, question words and ordinal numbers follow the same rule as adjectives: one ending for masculine and neuter, another for feminine. The only surprises are that мой, твой and чей take the stressed ending -ём in the masculine and neuter. Его́, её and их never change. Remember the spelling rule: after ш the ending is -ем/-ей, since it is unstressed.

explanations.title: Ordinal numbers
explanations.body: Ordinals are adjectives, so they work the same way. They are what you use for floors: на пе́рвом этаже́, на второ́м этаже́, на тре́тьем этаже́. Тре́тий is a soft-stem adjective, so it takes -ьем and -ьей.

lessons.title: 61. Flying and swimming: лета́ть, лете́ть, пла́вать, плыть
lessons.subtitle: Лета́ю ча́сто, лечу́ сейча́с

explanations.title: Two more pairs of motion verbs
explanations.body: Flying and swimming work exactly like walking (идти́/ходи́ть) and riding (е́хать/е́здить). The multidirectional verbs лета́ть and пла́вать describe habits, round trips, general ability, motion with no fixed direction, and negative commands. The unidirectional verbs лете́ть and плыть describe one trip in one direction: right now, with a destination, a planned trip, or a step in a sequence. Плыть is used for swimming, for sailing and for what a ship does.

tables.note: Лете́ть belongs to the second family, and the я-form has the т → ч change. Past: лета́л, лета́ла · лете́л, лете́ла.
Past: пла́вал, пла́вала · плыл, плыла́, плы́ли.

explanations.title: Which one?
explanations.body: Use лета́ть and пла́вать for what you do often, for a trip you have already completed and returned from, for ability (Я не уме́ю пла́вать), and for negative commands (Не пла́вайте здесь!). Use лете́ть and плыть for now, for a destination, for a planned trip, and for a positive command (Плыви́ сюда́!). Like идти́, лете́ть also works figuratively for moving very fast: Вре́мя лети́т!

lessons.title: 62. What time is it? Hours and minutes
lessons.subtitle: Сейча́с пять часо́в двадцать мину́т

explanations.title: Hour: час, часа́, часо́в
explanations.body: To ask the time say Кото́рый час? and answer with a number and the word час. The word changes with the number: оди́н час for 1, then часа́ for 2, 3 and 4, then часо́в for 5 and up. (Часа́ and часо́в are the genitive forms, which you will study later. For now just learn the pattern.)

rows: два часа́ · три часа́ · четы́ре часа́
пять часо́в · во́семь часо́в · двена́дцать часо́в

It's five o'clock.

explanations.title: Minutes: мину́та, мину́ты, мину́т
explanations.body: Minutes work the same way with three forms. One is мину́та (feminine, so одна́ мину́та). Two, three and four use мину́ты (две мину́ты). Five and more use мину́т. With long numbers only the last word counts, so 21 uses мину́та and 22 uses мину́ты. The teens are the exception: 11 to 19 always take мину́т, whatever the last digit.

examples.translation: It's two minutes past six.
It's seven fifteen.

examples.text: Сейча́с де́вять часо́в два́дцать одна́ мину́та.

lessons.title: 63. At what time? Во ско́лько?
lessons.subtitle: В шесть часо́в утра́, в час дня

explanations.title: At a certain time: в + hour
explanations.body: To ask at what time something happens, say Во ско́лько? (informal) or В кото́ром часу́? (formal). Answer with в and the hour: в два часа́, в пять часо́в. For one o'clock say simply в час.

examples.text: Во ско́лько ты встаёшь? — В семь часо́в.
examples.translation: What time do you get up? — At seven.
Our plane is at six o'clock.
We have lunch at one.

explanations.title: Morning, day, evening, night
explanations.body: Russian has no a.m. or p.m. Instead you add a word for the part of the day, always in the same fixed form: утра́ (in the morning), дня (in the afternoon), ве́чера (in the evening), но́чи (at night). Roughly: утра́ is up to noon, дня is the afternoon, ве́чера is the evening and но́чи is the small hours. Without a clock time, use the single words у́тром, днём, ве́чером and но́чью.

rows: в час дня · в три часа́ дня
в час но́чи · в три часа́ но́чи

lessons.title: 64. Playing and tickets: в or на?
lessons.subtitle: Игра́ть в футбо́л, игра́ть на гита́ре, биле́т на конце́рт

explanations.title: Play a game, play an instrument
explanations.body: With игра́ть the preposition depends on what you play. For sports and games use в plus the accusative: игра́ть в футбо́л. For musical instruments use на plus the prepositional: игра́ть на гита́ре. Some instrument names never change, such as пиани́но.

explanations.title: A ticket to…
explanations.body: Биле́т is followed by в or на and then the accusative. Use в for a ticket to a place, such as a theater, a museum, a city or a country. Use на for a ticket to an event or a means of transport: a concert, a game, a lecture, a film, a ballet, a train, a plane.

lessons.title: 66. The future tense: two ways to form it
lessons.subtitle: Я бу́ду чита́ть, я прочита́ю

explanations.title: Imperfective future: бу́ду + infinitive
explanations.body: You already know that most verbs come in two aspects. In the past tense both aspects look alike (де́лал, сде́лал). In the future they are built differently. For the imperfective, take the future of быть and add the infinitive. The verb быть changes for the person, and the infinitive stays as it is.

explanations.title: Perfective future: just conjugate it
explanations.body: For the perfective, you do not use бу́ду at all. You conjugate the perfective verb with the same endings as the imperfective, but the result is future in meaning, since the perfective has no real present tense. So сде́лаю means “I will do it (and finish it)”. Never say бу́ду сде́лать.

examples.translation: Tomorrow I will be reading a book.
Tomorrow I will read this book through.

examples.text: В суббо́ту я сде́лаю дома́шнюю рабо́ту.
examples.translation: On Saturday I will do my homework.
On Sunday we will relax.

lessons.title: 67. Aspect in the past: process or result?
lessons.subtitle: Я чита́л два часа́, я прочита́л кни́гу

explanations.title: What each aspect says
explanations.body: In the past, the imperfective names the action itself: it was going on (for a while), it was repeated, or you simply tell what you did. The perfective stresses that one action was completed and that you have the result. English uses different tenses for these ideas, but Russian only has the two aspects.

rows: Когда́ я де́лал уро́ки, он слу́шал му́зыку.
Снача́ла я сде́лал уро́ки, а пото́м отдыха́л.

explanations.title: Words that give it away
explanations.body: Certain words usually point to one aspect. Duration and repetition words go with the imperfective. Words that suggest completion, a moment, or a result go with the perfective.

lessons.title: 68. Aspect in the future: the same two ideas
lessons.subtitle: За́втра я бу́ду гото́вить, в суббо́ту я пригото́влю

explanations.title: The contrast stays the same
explanations.body: The two aspects do the same jobs in the future as in the past. The imperfective future (бу́ду + infinitive) is for something in progress, repeated, or simply named. The perfective future is for one action that you plan to complete, with a result in mind.

rows: В пять часо́в мы бу́дем гото́вить у́жин.
В суббо́ту я сде́лаю дома́шнюю рабо́ту.
Я бу́ду встава́ть в де́сять часо́в ка́ждый день.
Пока́ мы бу́дем гото́вить, мы бу́дем слу́шать му́зыку.
Снача́ла мы пригото́вим у́жин, а пото́м сде́лаем уро́ки.

explanations.title: Words that signal completion
explanations.body: Сра́зу (right away) and как то́лько (as soon as) are followed by the perfective, because they refer to a finished action. Пока́ (while) is followed by the imperfective, because it describes something that goes on for a while.

examples.text: Как то́лько я прочита́ю э́ту кни́гу, я напишу́ письмо́.
examples.translation: As soon as I finish this book, I'll write a letter.

examples.text: Пока́ мы бу́дем де́лать уро́ки, мы бу́дем слу́шать му́зыку.
examples.translation: While we do our lessons, we'll listen to music.

examples.text: Обы́чно я встаю́ в шесть часо́в, но за́втра я вста́ну в де́вять.
examples.translation: I usually get up at six, but tomorrow I'll get up at nine.

examples.text: В суббо́ту и в воскресе́нье я бу́ду то́лько чита́ть.
examples.translation: On Saturday and Sunday I'll only read.

exercises.prompt: За́втра в пять часо́в мы ___ у́жин.
exercises.explanation: In progress at a given time: imperfective future.

lessons.title: 69. Learning aspect pairs: встава́ть / встать, гото́вить / пригото́вить
lessons.subtitle: Я встаю́, я вста́ну, я гото́влю, я пригото́влю

explanations.title: Always learn both
explanations.body: There is no single rule for making the perfective, so look the verb up and learn both forms together. The most common method is a prefix (по-, при-, про-, на-, с-). Another is changing the suffix, as in встава́ть → встать. When you conjugate a perfective verb, use the same endings as its partner, but remember it is future.

explanations.title: Two patterns to see side by side
explanations.body: Гото́вить → пригото́вить keeps every ending the same, because only the prefix is added. Встава́ть → встать changes more. The imperfective present is встаю́, встаёшь … while the perfective future adds an н to the stem: вста́ну, вста́нешь …

lessons.subtitle: Я за́втракаю, мы пообе́дали, на у́жин я ем ка́шу

explanations.title: Three meals, three verbs
explanations.body: Each meal has a noun and a verb that is made from it. All of these verbs are regular -ать verbs. Their perfective partners add по-: you finish the meal. To say what you eat for a meal use на plus the accusative: на за́втрак, на обе́д, на у́жин.

explanations.title: To eat, to drink
explanations.body: Есть (to eat) and пить (to drink) are irregular, so learn the forms. Есть is the same word you saw in “there is”, but its meaning here is different and it changes by person. Past: ел, е́ла, е́ли · пил, пила́, пи́ли.

lessons.title: 71. When and if: когда́ and е́сли about the future
lessons.subtitle: Когда́ я бу́ду в Москве́, е́сли ты прочита́ешь

explanations.title: Future inside, future outside
explanations.body: English often uses the present in a clause that starts with “when” or “if” but still talks about the future (“When I am in Moscow, I will visit museums”). Russian never does this. If the action has not happened yet, the verb is in the future tense, in the “when” or “if” clause as well. You can use the imperfective (бу́ду + infinitive, or бу́ду + place) or the perfective (a plan to finish).

Когда́ я прочита́ю кни́гу, я позвоню́.

lessons.title: 72. In January, this year, this week
lessons.subtitle: В январе́, в э́том году́, на э́той неде́ле

explanations.title: In a month
explanations.body: To say that something happens in a month, use в and the prepositional of the month. Most months take -е, and those that end in -ь drop it and replace it with -е. Note the stress: some months are stressed on the ending (январе́), and some on the stem (в ма́рте).

explanations.title: This year, this month, this week
explanations.body: With год and ме́сяц use в, with неде́ля use на. The words go in the prepositional, and adjectives in front of them take the endings you learned. Год is another word with the stressed -у́ place form: в э́том году́, but о го́де for “about the year”. Useful modifiers: э́тот, про́шлый (last) and бу́дущий (next, future).

lessons.title: 73. All day, all week: весь, and “about” a time
lessons.subtitle: Весь день, всю неде́лю, часа́ два

explanations.title: Весь, вся, всё, все
explanations.body: To say that something lasted a whole day, week, month or year, use весь (all, the whole) with the time word in the accusative. Весь agrees with the noun in gender. Feminine words change to -у (всю неде́лю), while masculine and neuter words look like the nominative.

rows: весь день · весь ме́сяц · весь янва́рь
всю неде́лю · всю ночь · всю зи́му

examples.translation: I will live in England for the whole year.

explanations.title: Exactly or about?
explanations.body: To say “about” with a number of units of time, reverse the order: the unit comes first and the number second. Compare два часа́ (exactly two hours) and часа́ два (about two hours). The same reversal works with в, че́рез and за: в во́семь часо́в → часо́в в во́семь, че́рез три часа́ → часа́ че́рез три.

units.title: Unit 11: Reflexive verbs, the genitive and numbers

lessons.title: 75. Verbs with -ся: washing and dressing
lessons.subtitle: Я умыва́юсь, он одева́ется

explanations.title: The little word -ся
explanations.body: Many Russian verbs end in -ся, or in -сь after a vowel. It is a leftover of себя́ (oneself). When the action is done to the person who does it, the verb takes this ending: I wash myself becomes Я умыва́юсь. A verb without -ся needs someone else to act on, and that someone is the direct object, in the accusative. Verbs of grooming are the clearest case.

explanations.title: Same endings, plus -ся
explanations.body: A verb with -ся is conjugated like the verb without it. Just add -ся after a consonant or й, and -сь after a vowel. The ты-form ends in -шься and the он-form in -тся, and -тся is pronounced as if it were -ца, which you will quickly get used to. English often drops “himself” (“he is shaving”), but Russian never can: Он бре́ется, never just Он бре́ет.

tables.note: Past: умыва́лся, умыва́лась, умыва́лось, умыва́лись.

examples.translation: The girl is washing her face.
The boy is getting dressed.
The man is shaving.
The woman is combing her hair.
I am washing the child's face.

exercises.explanation: The action is done to oneself: -сь after a vowel.
exercises.promptTranslation: I wash my face in the morning.
The boy is getting dressed.
The man is shaving.
We get dressed early.

exercises.explanation: There is an object (дочь), so no -ся.
exercises.promptTranslation: She is combing her daughter's hair.

exercises.explanation: A direct object that is a person: accusative.
exercises.promptTranslation: I am washing the child's face.
Do you wash up early?

lessons.title: 76. Things that start, open and end by themselves
lessons.subtitle: Уро́к начина́ется, магази́н открыва́ется

explanations.title: From object to subject
explanations.body: Most -ся verbs are not about washing yourself at all. Adding -ся to a verb that needs an object makes it a verb that does not. The thing that was the object becomes the subject: the teacher starts the lesson, and the lesson starts. The meaning of the verb hardly changes. The new verb can never take a direct object, so no accusative follows it.

explanations.title: Called, and the past tense
explanations.body: Называ́ться is also a -ся verb. It is how you ask and say what something is called: Как называ́ется э́тот фильм? — Он называ́ется «Весна́». For more than one thing use называ́ются. In the past tense -ся stays at the end: the verb agrees with its subject, and then -ся or -сь follows.

lessons.title: 77. To study and to learn: учи́ться
lessons.subtitle: Я учу́сь, мы у́чимся, ребёнок у́чится ходи́ть

explanations.title: Учи́ть and учи́ться
explanations.body: Учи́ть takes an object. It means to learn something by heart (Он у́чит слова́) or to teach someone (Мать у́чит ребёнка ходи́ть). Учи́ться has -ся and no object: it means to study or to learn. It is a second-family verb with a consonant change in the я-form: учу́сь, у́чишься, у́чится. The perfective is научи́ться, which adds на-, and means to learn how to do something once and for all.

tables.note: Past: учи́лся, учи́лась, учи́лось, учи́лись. Future: бу́ду учи́ться. Command: Учи́сь! Учи́тесь!

explanations.title: Three ways to use it
explanations.body: To say where you study, use в and the prepositional: Она́ у́чится в шко́ле. To say how well, add an adverb: Она́ у́чится хорошо́. To say what you are learning to do, add an infinitive: Ребёнок у́чится ходи́ть. Compare Мать у́чит ребёнка ходи́ть, where somebody teaches.

lessons.title: 78. Whose? The owner in the genitive
lessons.subtitle: Маши́на бра́та, кни́ги студе́нта

explanations.title: The new case: the genitive
explanations.body: The genitive is the most used case in Russian. It answers Кого́? and Чего́?, and one of its jobs is to show who owns something. English adds 's (Anton's bicycle) or uses “of”. Russian puts the thing first and the owner second, and puts the owner in the genitive: велосипе́д Анто́на. A masculine noun gets -а, or -я if it ends in -й or -ь.

tables.note: Remember the consonant: no ending in the nominative of a hard masculine noun, so the genitive just adds -а.

explanations.title: The owner never changes its case
explanations.body: No matter what case the thing owned is in, its owner stays in the genitive. In the first example the thing is the subject, in the second it is the object, and in the third it follows на.

examples.text: Чей э́то велосипе́д? — Э́то велосипе́д Анто́на.
examples.translation: Whose bicycle is this? — It's Anton's bicycle.

examples.text: Чьи э́то кни́ги? — Э́то кни́ги преподава́теля.
examples.translation: Whose books are these? — They are the teacher's books.
Sergei is the director of the museum.
I see my friend's house.

exercises.explanation: The owner goes in the genitive: -а.

exercises.explanation: The owner stays genitive even after я ви́жу.
exercises.promptTranslation: I see my friend's house.

exercises.explanation: Музе́й ends in -й, so the genitive ends in -я.
exercises.promptTranslation: Sergei is the director of the museum.

exercises.explanation: The owner stays genitive after на + prepositional.
exercises.promptTranslation: We are going in my brother's car.

options: the thing owned, then the owner
the owner, then the thing owned

lessons.title: 79. The genitive of feminine and neuter nouns
lessons.subtitle: Ко́мнаты, дере́вни, окна́, мо́ря

explanations.title: Feminine: -ы or -и
explanations.body: Feminine nouns drop their ending and add -ы (hard) or -и (soft). Nouns in -а become -ы. Nouns in -я, -ь and -ия become -и. Those in -ия end in two letters и: аудито́рия → аудито́рии.

explanations.title: Neuter: -а or -я
explanations.body: Neuter nouns work like masculine ones. Nouns in -о become -а, and those in -е and -ие become -я. Note the stress, which often moves to the end: окно́ → окна́. Then you can use the genitive to describe a noun as well as to show who owns it: магази́н о́буви (a shoe store), дире́ктор шко́лы (the school principal).

examples.translation: Here is the window of the room.
This is my sister's book.
This is the village school.
He works in a shoe store.
On the wall there is a portrait of a young woman.

exercises.promptTranslation: Here is the window of the room.

lessons.title: 80. Genitive: spelling and special nouns
lessons.subtitle: Кни́ги, отца́, дня, ма́тери, и́мени

explanations.title: The seven-letter rule
explanations.body: After г, к, х, ж, ч, ш and щ you never write ы or я: only и and а. This is the rule from lesson 25. In the genitive it affects feminine nouns: since -ы would follow a к or г, the ending is -и. Masculine nouns in these letters are not affected, since they already take -а: каранда́ш → карандаша́, ключ → ключа́.

explanations.title: Nouns that change shape
explanations.body: Some common words change inside. Nouns ending in -ец lose the е: оте́ц → отца́, америка́нец → америка́нца. День loses its е too: день → дня. Мать and дочь add -ер-: ма́тери, до́чери. Neuter nouns in -мя add -ен-: и́мя → и́мени, вре́мя → вре́мени. Learn these as a set, since they will come back in other cases.

explanations.title: Three prepositions, one case
explanations.body: До (before, until), по́сле (after) and из (from, out of) are always followed by the genitive. Из is also the preposition for where you come from: Я из Росси́и. It is the opposite of в. If you go в шко́лу you come back из шко́лы.

lessons.title: 82. Thirty to a thousand
lessons.subtitle: Три́дцать, со́рок, пятьдеся́т … сто, две́сти, ты́сяча

explanations.title: The tens and the hundred
explanations.body: From 50 to 80 the tens are built as “five tens”, “six tens” and so on, and each has a soft sign in the middle: пятьдеся́т, шестьдеся́т, се́мьдесят, во́семьдесят. The numbers 40, 90 and 100 are separate words that have to be learned: со́рок, девяно́сто, сто. Thirty is three + дцать. To build a number such as 35 or 47, say the tens first and the units second.

tables.note: In a compound ordinal only the last word is an ordinal: шестьдеся́т восьмо́й (68th).

explanations.title: Hundreds and building bigger numbers
explanations.body: The hundreds from 200 to 400 are two and three words glued together: две́сти, три́ста, четы́реста. Put the larger part first: два́дцать оди́н, со́рок пять, сто три́дцать. The time-telling rules from lesson 62 still decide the form of мину́та and час: со́рок одна́ мину́та, пятьдеся́т пять мину́т.

lessons.title: 84. What did you do? Did you finish?
lessons.subtitle: Что ты де́лал? Ты уже́ написа́л?

explanations.title: The question picks the aspect
explanations.body: You can usually tell which aspect to use from the question. If you ask what someone did, how long it took or whether they spent time on it, you only want to know about the activity, so the imperfective is used and the result does not matter. If you ask whether something is finished, when it will be finished, or want to see the result, the perfective is used.

explanations.title: Two ways to say the same day
explanations.body: The choice depends on what you want to stress. Compare the sentences below. In the first, the speaker lists what was accomplished. In the second, the speaker lists what was done, and we do not know whether anything was finished. A short answer to a question about the activity repeats the imperfective, and the answer to a question about completion uses the perfective.

examples.text: Сего́дня я сде́лала дома́шнюю рабо́ту, пригото́вила у́жин и убрала́ ко́мнату.

lessons.title: 85. Aspect in the infinitive: хочу́ есть or хочу́ съесть?
lessons.subtitle: Я начина́ю чита́ть, я хочу́ прочита́ть

explanations.title: Which aspect after a helper verb?
explanations.body: An infinitive takes its aspect from the word in front of it. After verbs of beginning, ending, learning, liking and knowing how, always use the imperfective: начина́ть, зака́нчивать, учи́ться, люби́ть, уме́ть. After verbs of wanting, being able and having to do something once, use the imperfective for the activity in general or the perfective for completing it.

tables.note: До́лжен changes by gender: до́лжен, должна́, должно́, должны́.

explanations.title: Permitted, forbidden, impossible
explanations.body: With мо́жно and нельзя́ the aspect shows what you mean. The imperfective is for a general rule: В э́той ко́мнате мо́жно открыва́ть о́кна (you may), нельзя́ открыва́ть (you may not). The perfective is for one specific action: Мо́жно откры́ть окно́? (May I open it now?). And Нельзя́ откры́ть окно́ says that it cannot be opened, because it is stuck.

lessons.title: 86. Commands: every day or just once?
lessons.subtitle: Гуля́йте ка́ждый ве́чер! Погуля́йте вме́сте!

explanations.title: Two aspects, two kinds of command
explanations.body: In a command the imperfective means do it regularly, as a habit, or in general. The perfective means do it once, now, or all the way to the end. Negative commands almost always use the imperfective: Не покупа́й! Not “Не купи́!”. The endings are the same as in lesson 26: -й or -и for one person (informal), and -йте or -ите for several people or politeness.

explanations.title: Choosing
explanations.body: Гуля́йте ка́ждый ве́чер! tells people to make a habit of it. Погуля́йте вме́сте! asks them to go once, right now. Ешь суп! means eat soup as a general habit, while Съешь э́тот суп! means eat all of this soup. When you want to see the result, use the perfective.

Go for a walk together! (this time)
Eat all of this soup!

Don't buy this car!

lessons.title: 87. Making the perfective: prefixes
lessons.subtitle: Чита́ть → прочита́ть, писа́ть → написа́ть

explanations.title: Seven common prefixes
explanations.body: The simplest way to make a perfective verb is to add a prefix. The prefix does not change the meaning, only the aspect. Seven prefixes do most of the work. The stress stays on the same syllable as in the imperfective, except with вы-, which always carries the stress.

tables.note: Also: слы́шать → услы́шать, пить → вы́пить, де́лать → сде́лать. Съесть has a hard sign, because the prefix с- ends in a consonant and е follows.

explanations.title: Learn to memorize, teach to teach
explanations.body: Учи́ть has two perfectives. Вы́учить means to learn by heart, to memorize: Он вы́учил слова́. Научи́ть means to teach someone how to do something: Мать научи́ла ребёнка ходи́ть. Remember the pairs, since you cannot always guess the prefix from the verb.

lessons.title: 88. Making the perfective: suffixes and different verbs
lessons.subtitle: Открыва́ть → откры́ть, встава́ть → встать, говори́ть → сказа́ть

explanations.title: Dropping or changing the suffix
explanations.body: Many pairs do not use a prefix at all. Some drop the suffix -ва-: открыва́ть → откры́ть, закрыва́ть → закры́ть, продава́ть → прода́ть, встава́ть → встать. In others the ending changes: -ать or -ять becomes -ить or -нуть, as in изуча́ть → изучи́ть, отвеча́ть → отве́тить, отдыха́ть → отдохну́ть. Спра́шивать changes to спроси́ть.

explanations.title: Pairs you just have to learn
explanations.body: A few verbs use two completely different words for the two aspects. The most common are говори́ть / сказа́ть (to say) and покупа́ть / купи́ть (to buy). Always learn a verb together with its partner. Here are their past forms in use:

lessons.title: 89. Say, tell, order: сказа́ть, рассказа́ть, заказа́ть
lessons.subtitle: Скажу́, расскажу́, закажу́

explanations.title: Говори́ть and сказа́ть
explanations.body: Говори́ть is a regular second-family verb. Its perfective сказа́ть is a first-family verb with a consonant change (з → ж) throughout the future: скажу́, ска́жешь, ска́жет. Two other very common pairs follow the same pattern: зака́зывать / заказа́ть (to order) and расска́зывать / рассказа́ть (to tell, to narrate). The commands are скажи́(те), закажи́(те), расскажи́(те).

tables.note: Past: сказа́л, сказа́ла, сказа́ли.

explanations.title: Ordering and telling
explanations.body: Заказа́ть and рассказа́ть have the same pattern in the future, where з changes to ж. Their imperfective partners are regular -ывать verbs: зака́зываю, зака́зываешь and расска́зываю.

lessons.title: 90. A glass of water, a piece of bread

explanations.title: Amounts take the genitive
explanations.body: After a word for a part or an amount, the thing measured goes in the genitive: кусо́к хле́ба (a piece of bread), стака́н воды́ (a glass of water), литр молока́ (a liter of milk). This is the genitive you already know, used for “of”.

tables.note: Ко́фе never changes, so it looks the same in every case.

explanations.title: Parts and fractions
explanations.body: Fractions are also followed by the genitive: полови́на (a half), треть (a third), че́тверть (a quarter). Where the whole is a single word, the half can be joined to it with пол-: полчаса́ (half an hour).

lessons.title: 91. Some tea, some cheese: the genitive for “some”

explanations.title: Not all, just some
explanations.body: The genitive can also mean “some” or “any”, when the amount is not stated and you do not mean a specific, known thing. This is common with commands and wishes: Купи́ сы́ра (buy some cheese), Хочу́ ча́я (I want some tea), Дай воды́ (give me some water). The same word in the accusative points to something definite: Купи́ э́тот сыр.

explanations.title: Informal -у and -ю
explanations.body: Some masculine nouns, especially food and drinks, have a second, informal “some” ending: -у or -ю instead of -а or -я. You can use either in speech, but only the -а/-я form is possible in writing for every noun. Feminine and neuter nouns have no such alternative.

lessons.title: 92. At the checkout: rubles and kopecks

explanations.title: Polite phrases
explanations.body: In a store, Бу́дьте добры́, … (Would you be so kind …) opens a polite request. Ско́лько с меня́? asks how much you owe, and the answer begins С вас … (from you …). Благодарю́ (вас) is a formal thank-you. Ско́лько сто́ит …? asks the price of one thing, and to pay for something use плати́ть за plus the accusative.

explanations.body: Рубль and копе́йка use the same three forms as час and мину́та: one form after 1, another after 2, 3 and 4, and another from 5 up. The last digit decides, except for the teens, which always take the plural form. Also learn the new hundreds from 200 to 400: две́сти, три́ста, четы́реста.

lessons.title: 93. Tasty, fresh, too hot: describing food
lessons.subtitle: Вку́сный суп, све́жая ры́ба, сли́шком горя́чий

explanations.title: Describing food
explanations.body: Food words are ordinary adjectives, so they agree with the noun in gender and number. The adjectives with a hard stem follow the pattern you know (вку́сный, вку́сная, вку́сное, вку́сные). Those that end in -ий after ч or ж (горя́чий) or have a soft stem (све́жий) follow the soft pattern, with a spelling twist after ж/ч. Use сли́шком for “too” and да́же for “even”.

explanations.title: Courses, “too”, “even”, “ago”
explanations.body: A meal has courses: пе́рвое (the first course, usually soup), второ́е or горя́чее (the main course), and десе́рт. Пе́рвое and второ́е are neuter adjectives used as nouns. The word сли́шком (too) goes in front of the adjective, and да́же (even) stands in front of the word it stresses. To say how long ago something was, put тому́ наза́д after the time: год тому́ наза́д.

lessons.title: 94. Review: aspect, amounts and prices

explanations.title: What you can do now

lessons.title: 95. There isn't any: нет and the genitive
lessons.subtitle: В па́рке нет туале́та. У меня́ нет бра́та.

explanations.title: Есть or нет
explanations.body: To say that something exists, use есть and the nominative: Здесь есть магази́н. To say that it does not exist, use нет and put the missing thing in the genitive: Здесь нет магази́на. So нет is not only “no”: it also means “there isn't”, and the genitive tells you what is missing.

tables.note: Some words never change: кафе́, метро́, такси́. Здесь есть кафе́. Здесь нет кафе́.

explanations.title: У меня́ нет …
explanations.body: To say what you do not have, use у + the owner in the genitive, then нет + the missing thing in the genitive. Both the owner and the thing are in the genitive: У ма́мы нет маши́ны.

examples.translation: I have no time.
We don't have a teacher.
There is no café here.
There is no sea in this city.

exercises.promptTranslation: There is no bathroom in the park.
I don't have a brother.

exercises.explanation: Feminine nouns in -а take -ы in the genitive.

exercises.explanation: Вре́мя is one of the special nouns: вре́мени.

lessons.title: 96. There was no, there will be no: не́ было, не бу́дет
lessons.subtitle: Вчера́ не́ было дождя́. За́втра не бу́дет конце́рта.

explanations.title: The past: не́ было
explanations.body: In the past, есть becomes был, была́, бы́ло or бы́ли and agrees with what existed. When something did not exist, Russian uses one fixed form, не́ было, with the stress on не. It never changes for gender or number, and the missing thing goes in the genitive.

explanations.title: The future: не бу́дет
explanations.body: In the future, бу́дет (or бу́дут) agrees with what will exist. When something will not exist, use one fixed form, не бу́дет, and the genitive.

lessons.title: 97. Without me, near him: pronouns in the genitive
lessons.subtitle: У меня́ нет, у него́ нет, без неё

explanations.title: The genitive of pronouns
explanations.body: The genitive of the personal pronouns is the same as the accusative that you learned in lesson 29: меня́, тебя́, его́, её, нас, вас, их. Use them after нет, у, без, до, из and every other preposition that takes the genitive.

explanations.title: Add н after a preposition
explanations.body: After a preposition, его́, её and их become него́, неё and них. This applies only to the personal pronouns (him, her, them). The possessives его́ (his), её (her) and их (their) never get н: У его́ отца́ есть маши́на. Compare the two rows below.

lessons.title: 98. Two, three, four: the genitive after small numbers
lessons.subtitle: Два стола́, две кни́ги, три окна́, четы́ре ко́мнаты

explanations.title: A noun after 2, 3 and 4
explanations.body: After два (две), три and четы́ре, the noun takes the genitive singular. Два is for masculine and neuter nouns, две is for feminine ones. The stress moves in the same way as in the genitive: стол → стола́. After пять and larger numbers the noun takes a different form that you will learn later (you have already seen it in пять рубле́й).

explanations.title: 22, 33, 104 and the rest
explanations.body: Look only at the last word of the number. If it is два (две), три or четы́ре, use the genitive singular: два́дцать два стола́. If it is оди́н, use the nominative: два́дцать оди́н стол. The numbers 12, 13 and 14 are the exception: they end in -надцать, so they follow the later rule. This works for time words too: два часа́, три дня, четы́ре го́да.

lessons.title: 99. For how long? In how long?
lessons.subtitle: Я чита́л три часа́. Я прочита́л за три часа́.

explanations.title: For how long? The imperfective
explanations.body: A time word in the accusative with no preposition says how long an action lasted, and the verb is imperfective: Я чита́л э́ту кни́гу три часа́. The questions are Как до́лго …? and Ско́лько вре́мени …?

explanations.title: In how long? The perfective with за
explanations.body: To say how much time it took to finish, use the perfective and за + the accusative: Я прочита́л э́ту кни́гу за три часа́. The question is За ско́лько вре́мени …?

lessons.title: 100. Didn't try, or didn't manage?
lessons.subtitle: Я не учи́л. Я не вы́учил.

explanations.title: Negation and aspect
explanations.body: With не, the imperfective says that the action did not happen at all: no time was spent on it, no attempt was made. The perfective says that the action was not completed: you may have tried, but there is no result to show. So Я не учи́л э́тот диало́г means “I didn't study this dialog at all”, while Я не вы́учил э́тот диало́г means “I can't recite it, because I didn't learn it”.

explanations.title: Negation in the future
explanations.body: The same contrast works in the future. Я не бу́ду де́лать э́ту рабо́ту! says that you will not even start. Я не сде́лаю э́ту рабо́ту says that you believe you will not manage to finish it. In both sentences the reason can be the same: the job is too big (сли́шком большо́й).

lessons.title: 101. Suddenly! At once! Begin, continue, finish
lessons.subtitle: Он вдруг уви́дел кота́. Мы на́чали смотре́ть фильм.

explanations.title: A quick, single action
explanations.body: Words such as сра́зу (at once), как то́лько (as soon as) and вдруг (suddenly) show an action that happens in a moment. The verb is perfective.

rows: Как то́лько я уви́дел су́мку, я купи́л её.

examples.text: Как то́лько я уви́дела э́ту су́мку, я сра́зу купи́ла её.
examples.translation: As soon as I saw this bag, I bought it right away.

examples.text: И́горь чита́л газе́ту, когда́ вдруг услы́шал му́зыку.
examples.translation: Igor was reading the paper when he suddenly heard music.

examples.text: Я откры́л дверь и вдруг уви́дел кота́.
examples.translation: I opened the door and suddenly saw a cat.

explanations.title: Begin, continue, finish
explanations.body: The verbs начина́ть / нача́ть, продолжа́ть and зака́нчивать / зако́нчить are followed only by an imperfective infinitive, whatever the aspect of the first verb. Мой брат на́чал изуча́ть францу́зский (perfective нача́ть, imperfective infinitive). When the first verb is imperfective, it can also mean that you tried several times: Я мно́го раз начина́л изуча́ть францу́зский.

rows: Мой брат на́чал изуча́ть францу́зский язы́к.

lessons.title: 102. Let's! Дава́й and дава́йте
lessons.subtitle: Дава́йте говори́ть по-ру́сски! Дава́й напи́шем!

explanations.title: Let's do it regularly
explanations.body: Дава́й (to one friend) or Дава́йте (to several people, or politely) + a verb makes a suggestion. To suggest doing something regularly, from now on, use the imperfective infinitive. You can add бу́дем before it. To say “Let's not …”, put не before the imperfective infinitive.

explanations.title: Let's do it once
explanations.body: To suggest doing something once, from start to finish, use дава́й(те) and the perfective “we” form. It is the same as the future tense: напи́шем, посмо́трим, ку́пим.

examples.text: Дава́йте говори́ть в кла́ссе то́лько по-ру́сски!

Let's watch this film!

exercises.explanation: A regular habit: the imperfective infinitive.
exercises.promptTranslation: Let's speak only Russian in the classroom!

exercises.explanation: Once, to the end: the perfective we-form.
exercises.promptTranslation: Let's write a story!

exercises.explanation: A negative suggestion: the imperfective infinitive.

exercises.explanation: To a result: the perfective we-form.

lessons.subtitle: Ку́ртка, пла́тье, ша́пка, пальто́

explanations.title: To wear: носи́ть
explanations.body: Носи́ть means to wear (and also to carry). The я form has the stress on the end, then it moves back: ношу́, но́сишь, но́сит. The adjectives мужско́й (men's), же́нский (women's) and де́тский (children's) agree with the noun.

explanations.title: Clothes and things you carry
explanations.body: Пальто́ never changes. Перча́тки and носки́ are usually used in the plural. In the genitive you can say, for example, В карма́не нет телефо́на.

explanations.title: Four pairs with unusual perfectives
explanations.body: Four common verbs form their perfective in an unusual way. Learn the pairs: пока́зывать / показа́ть (to show), продава́ть / прода́ть (to sell), находи́ть / найти́ (to find), понима́ть / поня́ть (to understand). Their perfective future forms follow.

explanations.title: The past of найти́ and поня́ть
explanations.body: Найти́ has an irregular masculine past: нашёл, нашла́, нашли́. Поня́ть is regular, but the stress moves: по́нял, поняла́, по́няли.

explanations.title: Four words that do not change
explanations.body: Four useful comparative words never change for gender or number: лу́чше (better), ху́же (worse), бо́льше (bigger, more) and ме́ньше (smaller, less, fewer). To compare, put чем (than) before the second thing, which stays in the nominative. Намно́го means “much”: намно́го лу́чше.

lessons.subtitle: Пятьсо́т, шестьсо́т, семьсо́т, восемьсо́т, девятьсо́т

explanations.title: Hundreds from 500
explanations.body: From 500 the hundreds are written as one word: пять + сот, шесть + сот and so on. The stress is on the last syllable (пятьсо́т). Together with 200, 300 and 400 you now have every hundred: сто, две́сти, три́ста, четы́реста, пятьсо́т, шестьсо́т, семьсо́т, восемьсо́т, девятьсо́т.

explanations.title: Prices
explanations.body: Combine them with the numbers you know: пятьсо́т два́дцать пять is 525. In a price the word рубле́й follows (you learned it in lesson 92).

examples.translation: How much does this jacket cost?

lessons.title: 107. Review: absence, numbers and aspect
lessons.subtitle: Putting lessons 95 to 106 together

explanations.title: What you can do now
explanations.body: You can say what is missing (нет, не́ было, не бу́дет + genitive), use the genitive of pronouns (у него́, без неё), use the genitive singular after два, три and четы́ре, choose the aspect with time expressions, negation, sudden actions and suggestions, talk about clothes, compare with лу́чше, ху́же, бо́льше and ме́ньше, and say hundreds up to 900.

units.title: Unit 14: From, near, seasons and going

lessons.title: 108. Where from? из and с
lessons.subtitle: Я иду́ из шко́лы. Она́ идёт с рабо́ты.

explanations.title: из: the opposite of в
explanations.body: To say where you are coming from, use из or с with the genitive. The question is Отку́да? Use из for everything you say в about: countries, cities, buildings and enclosed spaces. If you say в for “to” and “in”, say из for “from”.

explanations.title: с: the opposite of на
explanations.body: Use с for everything you say на about: open spaces, events, compass points, and words like по́чта, вокза́л and заво́д. If you say на for “to” and “on”, say с for “from”.

examples.text: Отку́да ты идёшь? — Я иду́ из шко́лы.
examples.translation: Where are you coming from? — I'm coming from school.
We are coming from a concert.
He is coming from the station.
I am coming from class.

explanations.title: From here, from there
explanations.body: Three questions have their own words for “from”: отку́да (from where), отсю́да (from here) and отту́да (from there).

examples.translation: It is far from here to the station.
From there I went home.

exercises.promptTranslation: We are coming from the club.
I'm coming from work.
She is coming from Moscow.
They are coming from the station.
We are coming from the concert.
He is coming from school.
I'm coming from the post office.
Where are you coming from? — From school.

exercises.prompt: If you say в for “to”, which preposition do you use for “from”?
Which phrase goes with на рабо́ту?

lessons.title: 109. From a person: от and у
lessons.subtitle: Я была́ у врача́. Я иду́ от врача́.

explanations.title: At someone's place, from someone's place
explanations.body: With a person, у + the genitive means “at that person's place” (У кого́? At whose place?), and от + the genitive means “from that person's place” (От кого́? From whom?). It can also mean the person's office or room: Анто́н сейча́с у врача́.

explanations.title: Buying and asking: у
explanations.body: The preposition у also works with покупа́ть / купи́ть (to buy from someone) and спра́шивать / спроси́ть (to ask someone). От also means “from” when something comes from a person, like a letter.

examples.text: У кого́ ты был? — Я был у дру́га.
examples.translation: At whose place were you? — I was at a friend's.

examples.text: Где вы жи́ли ра́ньше? — Я жил у тёти.
examples.translation: Where did you live before? — I lived at my aunt's.
Anton is at the doctor's right now.

examples.text: Я купи́л э́ту маши́ну у дру́га.
examples.translation: I bought this car from a friend.

examples.text: Спроси́ у преподава́теля, что зна́чит э́то сло́во.
examples.translation: Ask the teacher what this word means.
This letter is from my brother.

exercises.promptTranslation: I was at the doctor's.
I'm coming from the doctor's.
We were at a friend's.
This letter is from my brother.
She lived at her aunt's.
I bought this car from a friend.
Whose place are you coming from? — Grandma's.

exercises.prompt: Which question matches Я был у врача́?

lessons.title: 110. Near: о́коло and у
lessons.subtitle: Они́ живу́т о́коло больни́цы. Он стои́т у доски́.

explanations.title: о́коло: near, by
explanations.body: О́коло means near or by, and it can be used with anything: a thing, a place or a person. The noun that follows is in the genitive.

rows: The dog is lying by the table.
В кла́ссе я сижу́ о́коло окна́.
In class I sit by the window.

explanations.title: у also means near, but only for things
explanations.body: У + the genitive also means near, but only with things. With people, у means “at that person's place”. So Учени́к стои́т у доски́ and Учени́к стои́т о́коло доски́ mean the same, but Учени́к стои́т о́коло учи́теля must use о́коло. If two things are of similar size, use о́коло: Письмо́ лежи́т о́коло газе́ты.

examples.translation: The pupil is standing at the board.
The pupil is standing by the board.
The pupil is standing next to the teacher.
The car is standing by the house.
The letter is lying next to the newspaper.

exercises.promptTranslation: They live near the hospital.
I sit by the window.
Don't stand near me!
The pupil is standing next to the teacher.

exercises.explanation: Near a thing: у is possible.
exercises.promptTranslation: The car is standing by the house.

exercises.prompt: Учени́к стои́т ___ учи́теля. (next to a person)
exercises.promptTranslation: The pupil is standing next to the teacher.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition can be used with a person for “near”?
exercises.explanation: У + a person means “at that person's place”.

exercises.prompt: What does Он сидит у врача́ mean?
options: He is sitting near the doctor.
exercises.explanation: У + a person = at their place.

lessons.title: 111. Spring, summer, autumn, winter
lessons.subtitle: Весно́й, ле́том, о́сенью, зимо́й

explanations.title: The four seasons
explanations.body: To say “in spring” and so on, use a special form with no preposition: весно́й, ле́том, о́сенью, зимо́й. Do not say в весну. The question is Како́е сейча́с вре́мя го́да? (What season is it?).

examples.translation: It is warm in spring.
In summer I like to swim.
It rains in autumn.
It snows in winter.

examples.text: Зимо́й хо́лодно, и я но́шу шу́бу.
examples.translation: In winter it is cold and I wear a fur coat.
Which season do you like?

exercises.promptTranslation: It is hot in summer.
It snows in winter.
It rains in autumn.
It is warm in spring.

lessons.title: 112. North, south, east, west
lessons.subtitle: На се́вере, на ю́ге, с восто́ка, на за́пад

explanations.title: The compass points take на and с
explanations.body: The four points of the compass are се́вер, юг, восто́к and за́пад. They go with на (where, where to) and с (where from).

tables.note: Where to? is на + the nominative form: Мы е́дем на юг.

explanations.title: Between the points
explanations.body: Join two points with a hyphen to name the directions between them. The first part ends in -о.

examples.translation: We are going on vacation to the south.
We are on vacation in the south.
We are coming from the south.
My brother lives in the north.
This city is in the east.

exercises.promptTranslation: We live in the north.
We are going to the south.
He is coming from the east.
They live in the west.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition goes with the points of the compass?
How do you say “from the south”?

lessons.title: 113. Setting off: пошёл, пое́хал, полечу́
lessons.subtitle: Он пошёл в магази́н. Я пое́ду в Москву́.

explanations.title: Past: someone set off
explanations.body: Adding по- to идти́, е́хать, лете́ть and плыть makes a perfective verb. In the past it says that someone set off: Он пошёл в магази́н means “He has gone to the store” (he headed there). We do not know whether he arrived, and that does not matter. Compare Он ходи́л в магази́н, which means that he went and came back.

explanations.title: Future: I will go
explanations.body: In the future the focus is on the intention. These are perfective, so the forms look like the present but mean the future. Note the change of consonant in полечу́ (т → ч), just like in лечу́.

examples.text: — Где Рома́н? — Он пошёл в магази́н.
examples.translation: — Where is Roman? — He has gone to the store.

examples.text: Кири́лл пое́хал на по́езде в Ки́ев.
examples.translation: Kirill left for Kiev by train.

examples.text: Я хочу́ пойти́ на конце́рт. Е́сли я пойду́, я наде́ну но́вое пла́тье.
examples.translation: I want to go to the concert. If I go, I will put on my new dress.

examples.text: У меня́ ско́ро бу́дет о́тпуск. Я полечу́ на Гава́йи.
examples.translation: My vacation is soon. I will fly to Hawaii.

examples.text: Мы поплывём на теплохо́де в круи́з.
examples.translation: We will go on a cruise by steamship.

exercises.promptTranslation: He has gone to the store.

exercises.prompt: Она́ ___ в Ки́ев на по́езде. (set off)
exercises.promptTranslation: She left for Kiev by train.
Tomorrow I will go to the concert.
We will fly to Hawaii on vacation.
Will you go with us?
They will go on a cruise by steamship.

exercises.prompt: What does Он пошёл в магази́н mean?
options: He goes to the store every day.
He has set off for the store.
He has come back from the store.
exercises.explanation: The emphasis is on the beginning of the motion.

exercises.prompt: What is the perfective of лете́ть?

lessons.title: 114. Walk around, drive around: походи́ть, пое́здить
lessons.subtitle: Он немно́го походи́л по па́рку и пошёл домо́й.

explanations.title: A little while: по- with repeating verbs
explanations.body: With ходи́ть, е́здить, лета́ть and пла́вать, the prefix по- makes a perfective verb that means “for some time”. It describes movement limited in time and is often followed by another action: Рома́н походи́л полчаса́ по пля́жу и пошёл домо́й (he walked around the beach for half an hour, then left). Compare пошёл, which means “set off”: the stress and the meaning are both different.

examples.text: Рома́н походи́л полчаса́ по пля́жу и пошёл домо́й.
examples.translation: Roman walked around the beach for half an hour and went home.

examples.text: Кири́лл пое́здил по Ки́еву на маши́не.
examples.translation: Kirill drove around Kiev by car.

examples.text: За́втра у́тром де́ти попла́вают в о́зере и пото́м пойду́т в шко́лу.
examples.translation: Tomorrow morning the children will swim in the lake for a while and then go to school.

examples.text: Моя́ канаре́йка полета́ет и ся́дет на ла́мпу.
examples.translation: My canary will fly around for a while and then land on the lamp.

exercises.prompt: Он немно́го ___ по па́рку и пошёл домо́й. (walked around)
exercises.explanation: Walking around for a while: походи́ть.
exercises.promptTranslation: He walked around the park for a bit and went home.

exercises.prompt: Кири́лл два дня ___ по Ки́еву на маши́не. (drove around)
exercises.explanation: Driving around for a while: пое́здить.
exercises.promptTranslation: Kirill drove around Kiev for two days.

exercises.prompt: За́втра они́ ___ в о́зере. (will swim for a while)
exercises.promptTranslation: Tomorrow they will swim in the lake for a while.

exercises.prompt: Моя́ канаре́йка ___ и ся́дет на ла́мпу.
exercises.explanation: Flying around for a while: полета́ть.
exercises.promptTranslation: My canary will fly around and land on the lamp.

exercises.prompt: What does по- add to ходи́ть, е́здить, лета́ть, пла́вать?
Which word means “swam for a while”?
Which word means “drove around for a while”?
Which word means “walked around for a while”?

lessons.title: 115. Sitting, standing, lying, hanging
lessons.subtitle: Ка́рта виси́т на стене́. Маши́на стои́т у до́ма.

explanations.title: Four verbs for where things are
explanations.body: Russian often says how something is positioned, where English only says “is”. Use сиде́ть (to sit), стоя́ть (to stand), лежа́ть (to lie) and висе́ть (to hang). They are in the second family: -и- in the middle, but the я form changes: сижу́, стою́, лежу́, вишу́.

examples.translation: The book is lying on the table.
The map is hanging on the wall.
The car is parked by the house.

examples.text: В кла́ссе я сижу́ о́коло окна́.
examples.translation: In class I sit by the window.

examples.text: Э́та фотогра́фия год висе́ла на стене́.
examples.translation: This picture hung on the wall for a year.

explanations.title: For a while
explanations.body: With по- these verbs mean “for some time”: посиде́ть, постоя́ть, полежа́ть, повисе́ть. Combine with дава́йте: Дава́йте посиди́м здесь!

examples.translation: Let's sit here for a while.
He lay for a bit and got up.

exercises.promptTranslation: I'm sitting by the window.
They are standing by the house.
Do you lie in bed for long?
This map hung here for a year.
The map is hanging on the wall.
The car is standing by the house.

exercises.prompt: Which is the я form of висе́ть?
exercises.explanation: Висе́ть → вишу́, not ви́жу (that is ви́деть).

exercises.prompt: Which verb describes a book on the table?
exercises.explanation: A book lies flat on a table.

lessons.title: 116. For a week, for a week, in a week
lessons.subtitle: неде́лю · на неде́лю · че́рез неде́лю

explanations.title: Three ways to say a time
explanations.body: A time word can answer three questions. With no preposition (accusative), it says how long something lasted. With на + the accusative, it says how long you intend to stay or be somewhere. With че́рез + the accusative, it says after how long something will happen.

rows: Я пое́хал в Москву́ на неде́лю.
Я пое́ду в Москву́ че́рез неде́лю.

examples.translation: I was writing this letter for an hour.
We vacationed in the village for a month.

examples.text: Он пошёл туда́ на час, а был там це́лый день.
examples.translation: He went there for an hour, but was there all day.

examples.text: В Москву́ я е́здил на два дня.
examples.translation: I went to Moscow for two days.
He will go there in an hour.

examples.text: Мы пое́дем в дере́вню че́рез три дня.
examples.translation: We will go to the village in three days.

exercises.prompt: Я пое́ду в Москву́ ___ неде́лю. (in a week)
exercises.promptTranslation: I will go to Moscow in a week.

exercises.prompt: Я пое́ду в Москву́ ___ неде́лю. (for a week)
exercises.promptTranslation: I will go to Moscow for a week.

exercises.prompt: Мы отдыха́ли в дере́вне ___. (for a month)
exercises.explanation: How long it lasted: no preposition.
exercises.promptTranslation: We vacationed in the village for a month.

exercises.prompt: Он пойдёт туда́ ___ час. (in an hour)
exercises.promptTranslation: He will go there in an hour.

exercises.prompt: Мы пое́дем в дере́вню че́рез три ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: We will go to the village in three days.

exercises.prompt: В Москву́ я е́здил на два ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: I went to Moscow for two days.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means “for a planned hour”?

lessons.title: 117. One and a half: полтора́ and полторы́
lessons.subtitle: Полтора́ часа́, полторы́ неде́ли

explanations.title: Two forms
explanations.body: Полтора́ (“one and a half”) goes with masculine and neuter nouns, and полторы́ goes with feminine ones. The noun after it takes the genitive singular, just like after два.

examples.text: Я жил в Москве́ полтора́ го́да.
examples.translation: I lived in Moscow for a year and a half.
I worked for an hour and a half.
Buy a liter and a half of milk.
She drank a cup and a half of coffee.
We were there for a week and a half.

exercises.promptTranslation: I lived there for a year and a half.
We were there for a week and a half.
Buy a liter and a half of milk.
She drank a cup and a half of coffee.
I worked for an hour and a half.

exercises.prompt: Which numeral goes with feminine nouns?
What case does the noun after полтора́ take?

lessons.title: 118. I have to: мне на́до, тебе́ ну́жно
lessons.subtitle: Мне на́до рабо́тать. Вчера́ мне на́до бы́ло рабо́тать.

explanations.title: The person is in the dative
explanations.body: To say that someone must or needs to do something, put that person in the dative and add на́до or ну́жно with an infinitive. You know the dative pronouns from мне нра́вится: мне, тебе́, ему́, ей, нам, вам, им. The word на́до never changes.

explanations.title: Past, future and “don't have to”
explanations.body: In the past, add бы́ло: Вчера́ мне на́до бы́ло рабо́тать. In the future, add бу́дет: За́втра нам на́до бу́дет е́хать. To say that you do not have to, put не before на́до: Ей не на́до ждать.

examples.translation: I have to work.
Yesterday I had to work.

examples.text: За́втра нам на́до бу́дет е́хать в Москву́.
examples.translation: Tomorrow we will have to go to Moscow.
You need to rest.
She doesn't have to wait.

exercises.explanation: The person goes in the dative.
exercises.promptTranslation: I have to work.
You need to rest.
He has to go home.
She needs to write a letter.
They have to study.
Yesterday I had to work.

exercises.prompt: За́втра нам на́до ___ е́хать в Москву́.
exercises.promptTranslation: Tomorrow we will have to go to Moscow.

exercises.prompt: In which case is the person after на́до?
Which means “She doesn't have to wait”?

lessons.title: 119. You're right! In my opinion …
lessons.subtitle: Ты прав. По-мо́ему, э́то ва́жно.

explanations.title: To be right: прав
explanations.body: To say that someone is right, use the short adjective прав, права́ or пра́вы. It has no other forms. Use прав for a man, права́ for a woman and пра́вы for several people. In the past add был, была́ or бы́ли.

examples.translation: You are right.
Masha is right.
You are right!
I was right.

explanations.title: Opinions and reactions
explanations.body: Some short words help you take part in a conversation: По-мо́ему (in my opinion), Ла́дно (all right), Снача́ла (at first), and the adjectives ва́жный (important), прекра́сный (wonderful) and прия́тный (pleasant). Тяжело́ means “it is hard”.

examples.translation: I think this is very important.
— Let's watch a film. — Okay.

examples.text: Снача́ла он шёл ме́дленно, а пото́м вдруг пошёл о́чень бы́стро.
examples.translation: At first he walked slowly, but then suddenly he started walking very fast.
It is a wonderful day!
It is hard to study and work.

exercises.promptTranslation: You are right.
Masha is right.
You are right!
In my opinion, this is very important.
— Let's watch a film. — Okay.

exercises.prompt: ___ он шёл ме́дленно, а пото́м бы́стро. (At first)
exercises.promptTranslation: At first he walked slowly, and then fast.

exercises.prompt: Which form is used for “she is right”?

lessons.title: 120. Review: from, near, seasons and going
lessons.subtitle: Putting lessons 108 to 119 together

explanations.title: What you can do now
explanations.body: You can say where you are coming from (из, с, от), where someone is (у), what is near (о́коло), name the seasons and compass points, say that someone set off (пошёл, пое́хал, полечу́), say that things sit, stand, lie or hang, give a time as how long, for how long or in how long, say полтора́, say that someone must (мне на́до), and say that someone is right (прав).

rows: From an open place or event

exercises.promptTranslation: We are coming from the club.
I'm coming from the concert.
She is coming from the doctor's.
I was at the doctor's.
It snows in winter.

exercises.prompt: Он ___ в магази́н и ещё не вернулся.
exercises.explanation: Set off and not yet back: пошёл.
exercises.promptTranslation: He went to the store and hasn't come back yet.
The map is hanging on the wall.

exercises.prompt: Я пое́ду в Москву́ ___ три дня. (for three days)
exercises.promptTranslation: I will go to Moscow for three days.
I have to go home.
You are right.

units.title: Unit 15: Genitive adjectives, dates and describing people

lessons.title: 121. Adjectives in the genitive: нет но́вого, без хоро́шей
lessons.subtitle: В кла́ссе нет но́вого студе́нта.

explanations.title: Four endings
explanations.body: A singular adjective in the genitive takes -ого or -его for masculine and neuter nouns, and -ой or -ей for feminine ones. Use the hard endings (-ого, -ой) after hard stems like но́вый and the soft ones (-его, -ей) after soft stems like си́ний and тре́тий.

explanations.title: Spelling and stress
explanations.body: After ж, ш, ч, щ and ц write е instead of an unstressed о: хоро́шего, хоро́шей, свежего. If the ending is stressed, write о: большо́го, большо́й. After к, г and х the endings stay the same (ни́зкого), because the spelling rule only changes ы to и.

examples.translation: The new student is not in the classroom.

examples.text: В э́той ко́мнате нет большо́го окна́.
examples.translation: There is no big window in this room.
This man is of average height.

examples.text: Я не могу́ жить без хоро́шей му́зыки.
examples.translation: I can't live without good music.
Turn right at the third building.

explanations.title: Compare three cases
explanations.body: The masculine and neuter genitive is the same as the accusative of masculine adjectives with animate nouns. The feminine genitive is the same as the feminine prepositional.

exercises.promptTranslation: The new student is not in the classroom.
I don't have a new car.

exercises.explanation: Окно́ is neuter: -ого, stressed so written о.
exercises.promptTranslation: There is no big window in this room.

exercises.prompt: Я не могу́ жить без ___ му́зыки.
exercises.promptTranslation: I can't live without good music.
This man is of average height.
Turn right at the third building.
There is no fresh milk here.

exercises.prompt: Which form is the feminine genitive?
Which ending do you write after ш, ж, ч, щ if it is unstressed?

lessons.title: 122. My, this, which: other words in the genitive
lessons.subtitle: Нет моего́ ключа́. Чьей ку́ртки нет?

explanations.title: Possessives and question words
explanations.body: Possessive pronouns (мой, твой, наш, ваш), question words (како́й, кото́рый, чей) and the words э́тот, тот, тако́й, друго́й and оди́н take the same endings as adjectives. Его́, её and их never change.

explanations.title: This, that, such, another, one
explanations.body: These words follow the same pattern. Remember that оди́н becomes одного́ and одно́й.

examples.translation: This doctor's son is my friend.
That girl's name is Vera.

examples.text: Ключ ва́шей сестры́ лежи́т на столе́.
examples.translation: Your sister's key is lying on the table.
Near which building is the bus stop?
Whose jacket isn't here?

examples.text: У меня́ никогда́ не бу́дет друго́го тако́го дру́га.
