lessons.title: 123. What is the date?
lessons.subtitle: Како́е сего́дня число́? — Сего́дня тре́тье ию́ня.

explanations.title: The months in the genitive
explanations.body: When a month follows the date, it goes in the genitive: тре́тье ию́ня (the third of June). Masculine months take -а or, after ь and й, -я.

explanations.title: Asking and answering
explanations.body: The question is Како́е сего́дня число́? The answer is an ordinal number in the neuter nominative (because число́ is neuter), then the month in the genitive. In the future бу́дет can be left out, but in the past бы́ло cannot.

examples.translation: Today is the fifth of May.
Yesterday was the first of March.
Tomorrow is the twenty-fifth of December.

exercises.explanation: The month after the date: genitive.
exercises.promptTranslation: Today is the third of June.
Yesterday was the nineteenth of January.
Tomorrow is the twenty-sixth of November.
Today is the fifth of May.
What is today's date?
Today is the first of March.

exercises.prompt: Which question asks for the date?

exercises.explanation: In the past бы́ло cannot be left out.

exercises.prompt: What is ию́ль in the genitive?

lessons.title: 124. On what date? Когда́ ты роди́лся?
lessons.subtitle: Четвёртого ма́я. Я роди́лся тре́тьего а́вгуста.

explanations.title: On a date: the ordinal in the genitive
explanations.body: To say that something happens on a date, put the ordinal in the genitive (masculine, like числа́) and the month in the genitive. There is no preposition. The question is Како́го числа́? or Когда́?

explanations.title: Dates in sentences, and years
explanations.body: Years work the same way: the last word of the ordinal and the word го́да are in the genitive. So 1982 on a birthday is ты́сяча девятьсо́т во́семьдесят второ́го го́да. To say where something happened you still say в + the prepositional (в 1982 году́), but for a full date use the genitive.

examples.text: Како́го числа́ наш экза́мен? — Четвёртого ма́я.
examples.translation: On what date is our exam? — On the fourth of May.

examples.text: Когда́ мы е́дем в Москву́? — Мы е́дем пя́того января́.

lessons.title: 125. Tall, short, slim: height and build
lessons.subtitle: Он высо́кого ро́ста. Она́ стро́йная.

explanations.title: How tall? Како́го ро́ста?
explanations.body: To describe someone's height, use рост in the genitive after a genitive adjective: высо́кого ро́ста (tall), сре́днего ро́ста (average height), ни́зкого ро́ста (short). The question is Како́го он ро́ста? The adjectives show the endings you have just learned.

explanations.title: Build and appearance
explanations.body: Pairs of opposite adjectives help you describe a person. Use вне́шность (appearance) for the whole picture and телосложе́ние for build. Ask Как он вы́глядит? (What does he look like?).

tables.note: Стро́йный means slim, in a pleasant way.

explanations.title: Describing with у + genitive
explanations.body: To describe someone's features, use у + the person in the genitive (у него́, у неё) and the feature as the subject: У неё дли́нные во́лосы. The word во́лосы (hair) is plural in Russian. Ask Каки́е у него́ во́лосы? (What kind of hair does he have?).

explanations.title: Eyes and face
explanations.body: Ask Како́го цве́та у неё глаза́? (What colour are her eyes?). The answer is a plural adjective. Other parts of the face: лицо́, нос, рот, борода́, усы́.

lessons.title: 127. The body: head, arm, leg, eye
lessons.subtitle: Две руки́, две ноги́, два глаза́, два у́ха

explanations.title: Parts of the body
explanations.body: Several parts of the body have an irregular plural. Learn them in pairs. Глаз, ухо and плечо are neuter or masculine in the singular and change completely in the plural.

tables.note: Prepositional: в глазу́, на носу́, во рту.

explanations.title: Counting body parts
explanations.body: After два, три and четы́ре the noun takes the genitive singular: две руки́, две ноги́, два глаза́, два уха́. This is the rule from lesson 98.

explanations.title: To look: вы́глядеть, похо́ж на …
explanations.body: Вы́глядеть is an imperfective verb (я вы́гляжу, ты вы́глядишь …). Похо́ж (похо́жа, похо́жи) means similar; use it with на + the accusative: Она́ похо́жа на ма́му.

examples.translation: What does she look like?
She looks very good.

explanations.title: Character
explanations.body: Use these adjectives to say what someone is like. They agree with the person in gender and number.

exercises.promptTranslation: She looks like her mom.

exercises.explanation: На + accusative; for an animate masculine noun it looks like the genitive.

lessons.title: 129. When, while, as soon as: which aspect?
lessons.subtitle: Пока́ я смотре́ла телеви́зор, он пригото́вил у́жин.

explanations.title: Three patterns
explanations.body: Clauses with когда́ (when), пока́ (while) and как то́лько (as soon as) say when the main action happens. The aspect depends on how the two actions relate. At the same time: both verbs are imperfective. One action goes on while another happens: imperfective in the когда́/пока́ clause, perfective in the main clause. One action follows another: both are perfective.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: Compare the three sentences. In the first the two activities run in parallel, in the second the dinner is cooked while the person watches TV, and in the third the dinner starts only after the film is over.

examples.text: Пока́ мой брат чита́л, я смотре́ла телеви́зор.
examples.translation: While my brother was reading, I was watching TV.

examples.text: Пока́ я смотре́ла телеви́зор, он пригото́вил у́жин и убра́л ко́мнату.
examples.translation: While I was watching TV, he cooked dinner and cleaned the room.

examples.text: Когда́ я посмотре́ла фильм, я начала́ гото́вить у́жин.
examples.translation: When I had watched the film, I started cooking dinner.

examples.text: Как то́лько я посмотрю́ фильм, я начну́ гото́вить у́жин.
examples.translation: As soon as I have watched the film, I will start cooking dinner.

examples.text: Пока́ я бу́ду смотре́ть телеви́зор, он пригото́вит у́жин.
examples.translation: While I watch TV, he will cook dinner.

exercises.prompt: Пока́ мой брат чита́л, я ___ телеви́зор.
exercises.promptTranslation: While my brother was reading, I was watching TV.

exercises.prompt: Пока́ я смотре́ла телеви́зор, он ___ у́жин.
exercises.explanation: One action is completed during the other: perfective in the main clause.
exercises.promptTranslation: While I was watching TV, he cooked dinner.

exercises.prompt: Когда́ я ___ фильм, я начала́ гото́вить у́жин. (finished it)

exercises.promptTranslation: When I had watched the film, I started cooking dinner.

explanations.title: A question inside a sentence
explanations.body: A question word can connect two clauses. Put a comma before it, keep the word order of the question, and use the same tense as in the original question: Кто до́ма? → Он спроси́л, кто до́ма. Question words that work this way are кто, что, како́й, кото́рый, чей and ско́лько.

lessons.title: 131. The one who, the thing that: тот, кто and то, что
lessons.subtitle: Я зна́ю того́, кто написа́л э́тот расска́з.

explanations.title: Тот, кто and то, что
explanations.body: To refer to a person or thing in general, use a demonstrative word in the main clause and a question word in the second clause. If the demonstrative has no noun, use кто for a person and что for a thing: Я зна́ю того́, кто написа́л э́тот расска́з. То, что я купи́ла, не мо́дно.

rows: Тот, кто написа́л э́тот расска́з, живёт здесь.
Я ви́дела то, что вы купи́ли.

explanations.title: With a noun: кото́рый; with тако́й: како́й
explanations.body: If the main clause has a noun, use кото́рый and make it agree with the noun in gender and number. If it has тако́й, use како́й. The case of each pronoun depends on its own clause.

units.title: Unit 16: The dative case

lessons.title: 133. To whom? Nouns in the dative
lessons.subtitle: Я пишу́ письмо́ дру́гу. Я звоню́ ма́ме.

explanations.title: Кому́? The dative endings
explanations.body: The dative case names the person who receives or benefits from an action: the indirect object. The question is Кому́? (To whom?). Masculine nouns with a hard consonant and neuter nouns in -о take -у. Masculine nouns in -й or -ь and neuter nouns in -е take -ю. Feminine nouns in -а and -я take -е. Feminine nouns in -ия and -ь take -и.

tables.note: Masculine nouns in -а and -я take -е: па́па → па́пе, дя́дя → дя́де, Ко́ля → Ко́ле.

explanations.title: Special nouns
explanations.body: Some nouns change their stem. Мать and дочь add -ер-: ма́тери, до́чери. The vowel е drops out of most nouns in -ец and out of день: отцу́, дню. Neuter nouns in -мя drop -я and add -ени: и́мени, вре́мени.

explanations.title: Verbs of giving and telling
explanations.body: Many verbs of giving, telling and writing take the person in the dative and the thing in the accusative. Learn them as pairs of imperfective and perfective.

explanations.title: Forms of дать
explanations.body: Дава́ть is regular (даю́, даёшь …), but дать is irregular.

explanations.body: Some nouns also take an indirect object in the dative: ответ дире́ктору (a reply to the director), письмо́ ма́тери (a letter to my mother), пода́рок сы́ну (a gift for my son), посы́лка вну́ку (a parcel for my grandson), по́мощь подру́ге (help for a friend) and сове́т дру́гу (advice for a friend).

explanations.title: Adjective endings
explanations.body: Masculine and neuter adjectives take -ому (hard) or -ему (soft); feminine adjectives take -ой (hard) or -ей (soft). After ж, ч, ш, щ, ц write е in place of an unstressed о.

explanations.title: Pronouns and ordinals
explanations.body: Question words, possessives, э́тот and тот, and ordinal numbers follow the same pattern.

lessons.title: 137. Pronouns in the dative: мне, тебе́, ему́
lessons.subtitle: Я скажу́ ему́. Я иду́ к нему́.

explanations.title: The dative of the personal pronouns
explanations.body: You already know мне from мне нра́вится. The full set: мне, тебе́, ему́, ей, нам, вам, им. After a preposition the third-person forms get н-: к нему́, к ней, к ним. Compare Я скажу́ ему́ (I will tell him) and Я иду́ к нему́ (I am going to see him).

examples.translation: I am going to his place.
I am going to her place.
I am going to their place.
Give me a pen, please.
We will help you.

exercises.promptTranslation: He calls me.
I will call you.
I will tell him.
I will tell her.
I am going to his place.
He will help us.
I am going to their place.

exercises.prompt: Which pronoun is “to you” (formal or plural)?
Which sentence means “I am going to her place”?

lessons.title: 138. It's hot for me: feelings and wishes in the dative
lessons.subtitle: Мне жа́рко. Де́вочке хо́лодно. Мне ка́жется, что …

explanations.title: Impersonal sentences
explanations.body: Russian often describes a feeling, impression or need with no real subject. The person goes in the dative and the word describing the feeling stands alone. Нра́виться, каза́ться (to seem), хоте́ться (to feel like) and на́до / ну́жно (need to) all work this way. In the past add бы́ло and in the future add бу́дет.

rows: The son feels like playing in the yard.
Ве́ре ка́жется, что за́втра бу́дет дождь.
It seems to Vera that it will rain tomorrow.
I need to learn to sing.

explanations.title: Past and future
explanations.body: The same sentences in the past use бы́ло and in the future бу́дет: Вчера́ мне бы́ло жа́рко. За́втра тебе́ бу́дет хо́лодно. The verbs каза́ться and хоте́ться take -ся forms: ка́жется, хо́чется.

examples.translation: I'm hot.
Yesterday I was hot.
Tomorrow you will be cold.

examples.text: Ему́ ка́жется, что пого́да за́втра бу́дет плоха́я.
examples.translation: It seems to him that the weather tomorrow will be bad.
She feels like sleeping.

exercises.explanation: The person goes in the dative.
exercises.promptTranslation: I am hot.
The girl is cold.

exercises.prompt: Ве́ре ___, что за́втра бу́дет дождь. (it seems)
exercises.promptTranslation: It seems to Vera that it will rain tomorrow.
The son feels like playing in the yard.
Yesterday I was hot.
Tomorrow you will be cold.
It seems to him that the weather is bad.

exercises.prompt: In which case is the person in Мне жа́рко?

lessons.title: 139. How old are you? Age with the dative
lessons.subtitle: Ско́лько тебе́ лет? — Мне два́дцать оди́н год.

explanations.title: Age: the person goes in the dative
explanations.body: Russian does not say “I am 20”. It says “to me 20 years”, so the person goes in the dative and the word for year depends on the last number: год after 1 (21, 31 …), го́да after 2–4 (22, 23, 24 …) and лет after 5–20 and everything that ends in 0 or 5–9. Numbers 11–14 always take лет.

examples.translation: How old are you?
I am 21.
My sister is 23.
My brother is 32.
Grandma is 70.

explanations.title: Asking, and past and future
explanations.body: Ask with Ско́лько + dative + лет: Ско́лько ему́ лет? In the past add бы́ло and in the future бу́дет, exactly as in the impersonal sentences you met before. Бы́ло and бу́дет do not change for the number.

examples.translation: How old is he?
I was 10.
In a year I will be 30.
How old is your grandmother?

exercises.promptTranslation: I am 21.
She is 23.
He is 25.

exercises.explanation: The person is in the dative.
exercises.promptTranslation: How old are you?
My sister is 19.
My brother is 32.
A year ago I was 20.
In a year I will be 30.

exercises.prompt: Which word goes with the number 12?

lessons.title: 140. To a person's place: к + dative
lessons.subtitle: Я иду́ к врачу́. Он идёт от бра́та.

explanations.title: Places and people
explanations.body: Use в or на for places, but к for the person you are heading to. The three questions use a different preposition and case set for places and for people. Ко is used before a few words, especially ко мне, ко всем and ко дню.

examples.translation: Where is Andrei? — He is at his brother's.

examples.text: Куда́ идёт Андре́й? — Он идёт к бра́ту.
examples.translation: Where is Andrei going? — To his brother's.

examples.text: Отку́да идёт Андре́й? — Он идёт от бра́та.
examples.translation: Where is he coming from? — From his brother's.

explanations.title: Other uses of к
explanations.body: К also goes with places you walk toward, and with a deadline it means “by”. Remember ко мне: Приходи́ ко мне! means “Come to my place!”.

examples.translation: We are walking toward the river.
The student walks to the board.
Tomorrow he is going to his grandmother's.
I will finish this by Monday.
Come over to my place!

exercises.explanation: Motion toward a person: к + dative.
exercises.promptTranslation: I am going to the doctor's.

exercises.explanation: Location at a person's: у + genitive.
exercises.promptTranslation: Where is Anya? — She is at grandma's.

exercises.explanation: Motion away from a person: от + genitive.
exercises.promptTranslation: He is coming from his brother's.
We are walking toward the river.
The student walks to the board.

exercises.explanation: Ко мне: the special form before мне.
exercises.promptTranslation: Come to my place!

exercises.explanation: К + dative with a deadline means “by”.
exercises.promptTranslation: I will finish this by Monday.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means “I am going to the doctor's”?
exercises.explanation: К + dative for heading to a person.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition means “from a person's place”?

lessons.title: 141. Along, around and by: по + dative
lessons.subtitle: Я хожу́ по го́роду. Он говори́т по телефо́ну.

explanations.title: Moving along or around
explanations.body: По takes the dative. With movement it means along or around: you walk along a corridor, drive down a road or wander around a city.

examples.translation: I am walking along the corridor.
They are driving along the central road.
We drive around town.
He paces around the room.

explanations.title: By phone, mail and on TV
explanations.body: По also names the means by which you send or receive something: по телефо́ну, по по́чте, по ра́дио, по телеви́зору, по интерне́ту. Radio is indeclinable, so it never changes.

examples.translation: An interesting film was shown on TV.
The weather forecast was broadcast on the radio.
I am talking on the phone.

exercises.promptTranslation: I am walking along the corridor.
We drive around town.
They are driving along the central road.
He is talking on the phone.
A film was shown on TV.
I saw it on the internet.
I will send the gift by mail.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means “I walk around the city”?
Which case does по take in по телефо́ну?

lessons.title: 142. Character and mood: умный, строгий, смеяться
lessons.subtitle: Он у́мный, но стро́гий. Она́ смеётся и поёт.

explanations.title: Describing character
explanations.body: These adjectives describe a person's character or how something feels. They agree with the noun in gender, number and case as always.

examples.translation: Our teacher is very strict.
He is clever but rude.
This film is boring.
My sister is cheerful.

explanations.title: Verbs of feeling and fun
explanations.body: Петь and смея́ться change their stem. Сердиться (to be angry) takes на + accusative, and an animate masculine noun in the accusative looks like the genitive: серди́ться на сы́на.

examples.translation: Mom is angry at her son.
Don't be angry with me!

examples.text: Кто тако́й Серге́й? — Э́то мой друг.
examples.translation: Who is Sergei? — He is my friend.

examples.text: Кто така́я Ни́на? — Э́то на́ша учи́тельница.
examples.translation: Who is Nina? — She is our teacher.

exercises.promptTranslation: Our teacher is very strict.

The children laugh and play.
Don't be angry with me!
Mom is angry at her son.
Who is Sergei? — He is my friend.
Who is Nina? — She is our teacher.

lessons.title: 143. Review: the dative case
lessons.subtitle: Я даю́ кни́гу сестре́. Я иду́ к врачу́.

explanations.title: Where the dative is used
explanations.body: The dative answers Кому́? (to whom?). Besides the indirect object, you meet it in impersonal feelings, in age, and after к and по.

explanations.title: Endings at a glance
explanations.body: Remember the pronouns мне, тебе́, ему́, ей, нам, вам, им, and the н- after a preposition: к нему́, к ней, к ним.

examples.translation: I will tell this to my friend.
I will call my mother.

exercises.promptTranslation: I will call my sister.
He is going to the doctor's.
I am 22.
The son feels like playing.
We drive around town.
I am talking on the phone.
I am giving her the book.
Show this to your father.

exercises.prompt: Which case follows по in по го́роду?

exercises.explanation: К + dative for heading to a person.

units.title: Unit 17: The instrumental case

lessons.title: 144. With whom? с + instrumental
lessons.subtitle: Я иду́ в парк с дру́гом. Она́ гуля́ет с сестро́й.

explanations.title: Together with: с + instrumental
explanations.body: The instrumental case answers the questions Кем? and Чем? (with whom? with what?). With the preposition с it means “together with”. Masculine and neuter nouns take -ом, or -ем after a soft stem, and feminine nouns take -ой, or -ей after a soft stem. When the ending is stressed, -ем and -ей are written -ём and -ёй.

examples.text: Я иду́ в парк с дру́гом.
examples.translation: I am going to the park with a friend.
She is walking with her sister.
I live with my family.
We are talking with the teacher.

explanations.title: Verbs that go with с
explanations.body: Several verbs of joint action take с + instrumental: знако́миться / познако́миться (to meet for the first time), встреча́ться (to meet, to date), разгова́ривать and поговори́ть (to talk). The word с becomes со before some clusters, as in со словарём.

examples.text: Я познако́мился с Ни́ной в сентябре́.
examples.translation: I met Nina in September.
Kolya is dating Masha.
Yesterday I talked with the director.

examples.text: Он идёт в магази́н со словарём.
examples.translation: He goes to the shop with a dictionary.

exercises.prompt: Я иду́ в парк с ___. (a friend)
exercises.promptTranslation: I am going to the park with a friend.
She is walking with her sister.
We are talking with the teacher.
I live with my family.
We lived with an aunt.

exercises.prompt: Он идёт в магази́н со ___. (a dictionary)
exercises.promptTranslation: He goes to the shop with a dictionary.
We are seeing Masha.

exercises.prompt: Which ending do feminine nouns with a hard stem take in the instrumental?

lessons.title: 145. Mother, daughter, father, day: special instrumentals
lessons.subtitle: Я горжу́сь ма́терью. С днём рожде́ния!

explanations.title: Soft-sign nouns and the long stems
explanations.body: Feminine nouns ending in -ь take -ью: но́чью. Мать and дочь add the syllable -ер- in all cases except the nominative and accusative: ма́терью, до́черью. Words in -ец and день lose the е: отцо́м, днём. The neuter nouns и́мя and вре́мя add -ен-: и́менем, вре́менем. Masculine nouns in -а or -я, such as па́па and дя́дя, take the feminine endings.

examples.translation: I am going with my mother.
The daughter is proud of her mother.
I talked with my father.
Happy birthday!

examples.text: Я горжу́сь ма́мой и па́пой, тётей и дя́дей!
examples.translation: I am proud of my mom and dad, my aunt and uncle!

exercises.promptTranslation: I am going with my mother.
She is walking with her daughter.
I talked with my father.
Happy birthday!
I am proud of my mom and dad.
We talked with my uncle.
He works at night and by day.

exercises.prompt: What is the instrumental of и́мя?
Which of these nouns loses the vowel е in the instrumental?

lessons.title: 146. Pronouns in the instrumental: со мной, с ним
lessons.subtitle: Пойдём со мной! Я иду́ с ни́ми.

explanations.title: The instrumental of pronouns
explanations.body: The personal pronouns are мной, тобо́й, им, ей, на́ми, ва́ми and и́ми, and the questions are кем? and чем? After a preposition the third-person forms add н-: с ним, с ней, с ни́ми. С becomes со before мной: Он лю́бит разгова́ривать со мной.

examples.translation: I need to talk with you.
He likes talking with me.
I am going with him.
I am going with them.

examples.text: С кем ты идёшь в кино́?
examples.translation: Who are you going to the cinema with?

exercises.promptTranslation: He is going to the park with me.
I want to talk with you.
I am going with him.
I am going with her.
We are going with them.
They are going with us.
Who are you going to the cinema with?

exercises.explanation: N- is added after the preposition.

lessons.title: 147. Adjectives in the instrumental: с но́вым другом
lessons.subtitle: Я говорю́ с но́вым студе́нтом.

explanations.title: Four endings again
explanations.body: Masculine and neuter adjectives take -ым after a hard stem and -им after a soft stem or after к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, щ. Feminine adjectives take -ой after a hard stem and -ей after a soft stem or after ж, ш, ч, щ when unstressed.

explanations.title: Pronouns that behave like adjectives
explanations.body: Question words, demonstratives, possessives, весь and оди́н use the same endings.

examples.translation: I am talking with the new student.
I live with my sister.
I am interested in that new book.
I am proud of your son.

examples.text: Я занима́юсь ру́сским языко́м с э́тим преподава́телем.
examples.translation: I study Russian with this teacher.

exercises.promptTranslation: I am talking with the new student.
She is walking with a good friend.
He works with this doctor.
I live with my sister.
I am interested in that book.
I am proud of your son.
Which student did you talk with?

exercises.prompt: Which ending do hard-stem feminine adjectives take in the instrumental?

lessons.title: 148. A house with a garden: с for features and manner
lessons.subtitle: Ко́фе с молоко́м. Они́ слу́шали с интере́сом.

explanations.title: Describing a thing or a person
explanations.body: С + instrumental also adds a feature: what a thing contains or what a person looks like. Note that ко́фе never changes. In English the same idea is “with”.

examples.translation: Coffee with milk, please.
This is a house with a garden.
This is a girl with a round face.
This is a man with a big nose.

explanations.title: How an action is done
explanations.body: С also tells the feeling or manner in which something is done. English often uses an adverb here.

examples.translation: The students listened with interest.

examples.text: Я с трудо́м запомина́ю но́вые слова́.
examples.translation: I remember new words with difficulty.

examples.text: Он с ра́достью рассказа́л мне об э́том.
examples.translation: He happily told me about it.
She answered with a smile.

exercises.promptTranslation: I drink coffee with milk.
This is a house with a garden.
This is a girl with a round face.
The students listened with interest.
I remember words with difficulty.
He answered with joy.

exercises.prompt: Она́ посмотре́ла на меня́ с ___. (a smile)
exercises.promptTranslation: She looked at me with a smile.

exercises.prompt: Which means “a man with a big nose”?
In с интере́сом, which case follows с?
exercises.explanation: With a meaning “with”, с takes the instrumental (with the meaning “from”, the genitive).

lessons.title: 149. Who do you work as? быть, работать, стать + instrumental
lessons.subtitle: Она́ рабо́тает учи́тельницей. Я хочу́ стать врачо́м.

explanations.title: A job or role after быть, работать, стать
explanations.body: After быть (past and future), работать (to work as) and стать (to become), the name of a job or role goes in the instrumental. The questions are Кем? and Каки́м? Кем она́ рабо́тает? — Она́ рабо́тает учи́тельницей.

examples.text: Кем она́ рабо́тает? — Она́ рабо́тает учи́тельницей.
examples.translation: What does she work as? — As a teacher.
My father was a doctor.
I want to be an engineer.
She wants to become a journalist.

explanations.title: But not in the present tense
explanations.body: Russian leaves out “am, is, are”. Without a form of быть the noun stays in the nominative. Compare Раньше оте́ц был врачо́м and Оте́ц — врач. Or Я хочу́ быть космонавтом and Я космона́вт.

exercises.promptTranslation: What does she work as? — As a teacher.
My father was a doctor.

exercises.explanation: No быть in the present: nominative.
exercises.promptTranslation: My father is a doctor.

exercises.explanation: After быть in the infinitive: instrumental.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want to be an engineer.
She wants to become a journalist.
She used to be a nurse.
Tomorrow he will be the director.

exercises.prompt: Why is врач in the nominative in Он — врач?
options: The verb быть is left out in the present tense
Because врач is a short word

lessons.title: 150. Interests and sports: заниматься, интересоваться
lessons.subtitle: Я занима́юсь футбо́лом. Я интересу́юсь му́зыкой.

explanations.title: Verbs that take the instrumental
explanations.body: Some verbs always take the instrumental for the thing you do, enjoy or use. Learn them as a set: занима́ться (to be busy with, to practise), интересова́ться (to be interested in), горди́ться (to be proud of) and по́льзоваться (to use).

examples.text: Чем вы занима́етесь в свобо́дное вре́мя?
examples.translation: What do you do in your free time?

examples.text: Каки́м ви́дом спо́рта вы занима́етесь? — Я занима́юсь футбо́лом.
examples.translation: Which sport do you practise? — I play soccer.

examples.text: Чем вы интересу́етесь? — Я интересу́юсь фотогра́фией.
examples.translation: What are you interested in? — Photography.

explanations.title: Sports and hobbies
explanations.body: Compare игра́ть в + accusative with занима́ться + instrumental: игра́ть в футбо́л and занима́ться футбо́лом mean almost the same. Nouns in -ия take -ией: фотогра́фия, фотогра́фией.

exercises.promptTranslation: I play soccer.
He is interested in music.
We are interested in photography.
What do you do in your free time?
She uses a dictionary.
I am proud of my brother.
My friend plays tennis.

exercises.prompt: Which case do заниматься and интересоваться take?

lessons.title: 151. By hand, with a pen: the instrumental of means; times of day
lessons.subtitle: Я пишу́ ру́чкой. У́тром я пью ко́фе.

explanations.title: With what? Чем?
explanations.body: Russian uses no preposition to say what you do something with. The tool simply goes in the instrumental: Чем ты пи́шешь? — Я пишу́ ру́чкой.

examples.translation: Usually I write with a pencil.
He eats soup with a spoon.
She cuts the bread with a knife.

explanations.title: Times of day and seasons
explanations.body: The instrumental also answers “when?” for times of day and seasons. Use these as ready-made words.

examples.translation: In the morning I drink coffee.
In summer we go to the seaside.
In winter it is very cold here.

exercises.explanation: The tool goes in the instrumental.
exercises.promptTranslation: I write with a pen.

exercises.explanation: The tool goes in the instrumental.
exercises.promptTranslation: He eats soup with a spoon.
She cuts bread with a knife.
Usually I write with a pencil.
In the morning I drink coffee.
In winter it is very cold here.
In summer we go to the seaside.

lessons.title: 152. Family and wedding: внук, племянник, жениться
lessons.subtitle: Он жени́лся на Ни́не. Она́ вы́шла за́муж за Анто́на.

explanations.title: Relatives
explanations.body: Besides родственник (a relative), you need the words for the next and previous generations.

examples.translation: I have a cousin.
My nephew plays soccer.

explanations.title: Weddings: who marries whom
explanations.body: A man uses жени́ться на + prepositional, a woman выхо́дит за́муж за + accusative. To say that someone is married, use жена́т на + prepositional for a man and за́мужем за + instrumental for a woman. A couple пожени́лись. The words you need: сва́дьба, жени́х, неве́ста, разво́д.

examples.translation: Their wedding is soon.

examples.text: На сва́дьбе жени́х и неве́ста о́чень счастли́вы.
examples.translation: At the wedding the groom and bride are very happy.

exercises.promptTranslation: He married Nina.
She married Anton.
She is married to Anton.
My sister's son is my nephew.
My son's son is my grandson.

exercises.prompt: Мой ___ брат живёт в друго́м го́роде. (cousin)
exercises.promptTranslation: My cousin lives in another city.
At the wedding: the groom and the bride.

lessons.title: 153. Must, can, know how: должен, мочь, уметь
lessons.subtitle: Он до́лжен э́то знать. Я не смогу́ вы́играть.

explanations.title: До́лжен has four forms
explanations.body: До́лжен means must or supposed to, and it agrees with the subject like a short adjective. It is followed by an infinitive, as are мочь, смочь, уме́ть and суме́ть.

explanations.title: Past and future with быть
explanations.body: Put the form of быть after до́лжен: in the past was or were, in the future the matching form of бу́ду. Compare Он до́лжен был рабо́тать and За́втра я должна́ бу́ду рабо́тать.

examples.translation: Yesterday we had to work.
Tomorrow I will have to work.

explanations.title: Can and know how
explanations.body: Мочь means can (circumstances allow it) and уме́ть means can (you have the skill). Смочь and суме́ть are the perfective forms: they mean to manage to.

examples.translation: He knows how to swim.

examples.text: Он не мо́жет говори́ть гро́мко: у него́ боли́т го́рло.
examples.translation: He cannot speak loudly: his throat hurts.

examples.text: Я не смогу́ вы́играть э́ту па́ртию.
examples.translation: I will not be able to win this game.
He must know this.

exercises.promptTranslation: She must work today.
We had to work yesterday.
Yesterday he had to work.
Tomorrow I will have to work.

exercises.prompt: Он не ___ говори́ть гро́мко: у него́ боли́т го́рло.
exercises.promptTranslation: He cannot speak loudly: his throat hurts.

exercises.prompt: Я пло́хо ___ игра́ть в ша́хматы. (know how)
exercises.promptTranslation: I don't know how to play chess well.

exercises.prompt: Я не ___ вы́играть э́ту па́ртию. (will be able to)
exercises.promptTranslation: I will not be able to win this game.

lessons.title: 154. Review: the instrumental case
lessons.subtitle: Я иду́ с дру́гом. Она́ рабо́тает врачо́м.

explanations.title: Where the instrumental is used
explanations.body: The instrumental answers Кем? and Чем? Remember the main jobs it does.

rows: Ко́фе с молоко́м. Она́ рабо́тает с интере́сом.

explanations.title: Endings at a glance
explanations.body: Nouns, adjectives and pronouns each have a short set of endings.

examples.translation: I am talking with a new friend.
I am going with her.

exercises.prompt: Я иду́ в кино́ с ___. (my sister)
exercises.promptTranslation: I am going to the cinema with my sister.
She works as a doctor.
I am interested in music.
I write with a pen.
In the morning I drink coffee.
He is going with me.
I am talking with this student.

exercises.explanation: No быть in the present: nominative.
exercises.promptTranslation: My father is an engineer.

exercises.explanation: After a past form of быть: instrumental.

units.title: Unit 18: Instrumental continued, reciprocal verbs and prefixed motion

lessons.title: 155. Mom and I: мы с мамой
lessons.subtitle: Мы с ма́мой живём в Москве́. Оле́г с О́лей рабо́тают вме́сте.

explanations.title: С + instrumental can mean “and”
explanations.body: Russians often say “I and my mother” as “we with my mother”. The pronoun мы, вы or они́ comes first, then с + instrumental, and the verb is plural. Use мы for “someone and I”, вы for “someone and you” and они́ for “someone and he or she”.

examples.text: Мы с ма́мой о́чень тебя́ лю́бим.
examples.translation: Mom and I love you very much.

examples.text: Оле́г с О́лей рабо́тают на одно́м заво́де.
examples.translation: Oleg and Olya work at the same factory.
You and I are so alike.
Where did you and she go?

exercises.prompt: ___ с тобо́й так похо́жи. (You and I)
exercises.explanation: “You and I” is мы с тобо́й.
exercises.promptTranslation: You and I are so alike.
Oleg and I are going to the park.

exercises.prompt: ___ с ма́мой живём в Москве́. (Mom and I)
exercises.explanation: The verb is first person plural: живём.
exercises.promptTranslation: Mom and I live in Moscow.

exercises.prompt: ___ с Оле́гом живёте в Москве́. (Oleg and you)
exercises.promptTranslation: Oleg and you live in Moscow.

exercises.prompt: ___ с ма́мой рабо́тают на заво́де. (She and mom)
exercises.promptTranslation: She and mom work at a factory.

exercises.prompt: Оле́г с О́лей ___ на одно́м заво́де. (work)
exercises.promptTranslation: Oleg and Olya work at the same factory.

exercises.prompt: What does мы с Оле́гом mean?

lessons.title: 156. Above, in front of, between: над, пе́ред, ме́жду, ря́дом с
lessons.subtitle: Ла́мпа виси́т над столо́м. Шкаф стои́т ме́жду столо́м и окно́м.

explanations.title: Four prepositions of place
explanations.body: Над (above), пе́ред (in front of, before), ме́жду (between) and ря́дом с (next to) always take the instrumental. They answer the question Где?

rows: Шкаф стои́т ме́жду столо́м и окно́м.

examples.text: Где виси́т ла́мпа? — Ла́мпа виси́т над столо́м.
examples.translation: Where does the lamp hang? — Over the table.

examples.text: Где ты стои́шь? — Я стою́ пе́ред карти́ной.
examples.translation: Where are you standing? — In front of the picture.

examples.text: Стул стои́т ме́жду столо́м и стено́й.
examples.translation: The chair is between the table and the wall.
The lamp is next to the chair.

explanations.title: With мной
explanations.body: Над and пе́ред add an -о before мной and are said together with it: надо мной, передо мной. Compare Вы бы́ли передо мной (You were in front of me) and Переста́ньте смея́ться надо мной! (Stop laughing at me!).

examples.translation: You were in front of me.
Stop laughing at me!

exercises.promptTranslation: The lamp hangs above the table.
I am standing in front of the picture.

exercises.prompt: Шкаф стои́т ме́жду столо́м и ___. (the window)
exercises.promptTranslation: The cupboard is between the table and the window.
The lamp is next to the chair.
He is standing in front of the picture.
Stop laughing at me!

exercises.prompt: Which case follows пе́ред, над, ме́жду and ря́дом с?

lessons.title: 157. Behind and under: Где? or Куда́?
lessons.subtitle: Рюкза́к лежи́т под столо́м. Положи́ рюкза́к под стол.

explanations.title: Same preposition, different case
explanations.body: Unlike the other prepositions, за (behind, at) and под (under) take two cases. For where something is, use the instrumental. When something moves there (Куда́?), use the accusative.

examples.translation: Put the bag under the table.
The bag is under the table.

examples.text: Мы сиди́м за столо́м и у́жинаем.
examples.translation: We sit at the table and have dinner.

exercises.promptTranslation: The backpack is under the table.
The backpack is under the table.
Put the backpack under the table.
We are sitting at the table.
Sit down at the table.
The picture is standing behind the cupboard.
The cat sleeps under the bed.
The cat ran under the bed.

exercises.prompt: Which means “Put the bag under the table”?

lessons.title: 158. Put, stand and hang: класть, ставить, вешать
lessons.subtitle: Я кладу́ кни́гу на стол. Кни́га лежи́т на столе́.

explanations.title: Where? and Куда́?
explanations.body: Russian uses different verbs for being somewhere and for putting something there. Лежа́ть, стоя́ть and висе́ть say where it is. Класть / положи́ть (lay flat), ста́вить / поста́вить (stand upright) and ве́шать / пове́сить (hang) move it there. They take an accusative object, and the place is Куда́? (accusative) after на, в, за, под.

examples.text: Я кладу́ кни́гу на стол. Кни́га лежи́т на столе́.
examples.translation: I put the book on the table. The book lies on the table.

examples.text: Он ста́вит ла́мпу на стол. Ла́мпа стои́т на столе́.
examples.translation: He puts the lamp on the table. The lamp stands on the table.

examples.text: Мы ве́шаем карти́ну на сте́ну. Карти́на виси́т на стене́.
examples.translation: We hang the picture on the wall. The picture hangs on the wall.

explanations.title: Forms to remember
explanations.body: Класть: кладу́, кладёшь, кладёт. Ста́вить: ста́влю, ста́вишь. Ве́шать: ве́шаю, ве́шаешь. The perfective forms are положу́, поста́влю and пове́шу. Stand, lie and hang up in the past use the regular imperfective: стоя́л, лежа́л, висе́л.

examples.translation: Where did you put my book?
Put the bag on the chair.
Tomorrow we will hang the picture.

exercises.promptTranslation: The book is lying on the table.
I am putting the lamp on the table.
We are hanging the picture on the wall.
The picture is hanging on the wall.
Where did you put my book?
He puts the bag on the chair.

exercises.prompt: Which verb means “to stand something upright”?
Which case does the object of класть, ставить, вешать take?

lessons.title: 159. Meeting and hugging: reciprocal -ся verbs
lessons.subtitle: Мы встреча́емся в кафе́. Они́ познако́мились в Москве́.

explanations.title: -ся can mean “each other”
explanations.body: Some reflexive verbs describe an action two or more people do to each other. English adds “each other” or “together”.

rows: to get to know each other

examples.translation: They met in Moscow.
The girlfriends hug.
We write to each other online.

examples.text: Я не зна́ю, когда́ мы уви́димся.
examples.translation: I don't know when we will see each other.

explanations.title: Naming the partner with с
explanations.body: To stress who the second person is, keep the same verb and add с + instrumental. With a singular subject the verb is singular: Он познако́мился с Ви́кой.

examples.text: Он познако́мился с Ви́кой в Москве́.
examples.translation: He met Vika in Moscow.

examples.text: Я встреча́юсь с Са́шей ка́ждый день.
examples.translation: I meet Sasha every day.
Kolya is dating Sveta.

examples.text: Я не зна́ю, когда́ я уви́жусь с тобо́й.
examples.translation: I don't know when I will see you.

exercises.prompt: Мы с Са́шей ка́ждый день ___ в кафе́. (meet)
exercises.promptTranslation: Sasha and I meet in a café every day.

exercises.prompt: Они́ ___ в Москве́. (met for the first time)
exercises.promptTranslation: They met in Moscow.
The girlfriends hug.

exercises.prompt: Мы ___ по интерне́ту. (write to each other)
exercises.promptTranslation: We write to each other online.
I am seeing Sasha.
Kolya is dating Sveta.

exercises.prompt: Я не зна́ю, когда́ мы ___. (will see each other)
exercises.promptTranslation: I don't know when we will see each other.

exercises.prompt: Why are verbs like встреча́ться reflexive?
options: Because it is in the past
Both people take part in the action
The action is done to oneself

exercises.prompt: Which means “They met each other in Moscow”?

lessons.title: 160. Friends and arguments: дружить, спорить, друг друга
lessons.subtitle: Они́ дру́жат пять лет. Они́ помога́ют друг дру́гу.

explanations.title: Other verbs with с
explanations.body: Not every reciprocal verb ends in -ся. Дружи́ть с, разгова́ривать с and спо́рить с (о + prepositional for the topic) all take с + instrumental.

examples.translation: They have been friends for five years.
Boris is friends with Lena.

examples.text: Мы уже́ два дня не разгова́риваем.
examples.translation: We haven't talked for two days.

examples.text: Мы с му́жем никогда́ не спо́рим о поли́тике.
examples.translation: My husband and I never argue about politics.

explanations.title: друг друга
explanations.body: With many verbs “each other” is друг дру́га. Only the second word changes, according to the case the verb or preposition needs. Put the preposition between the two words: друг с дру́гом.

exercises.promptTranslation: Boris is friends with Lena.

exercises.prompt: Мы с му́жем никогда́ не ___ о поли́тике. (argue)
exercises.promptTranslation: My husband and I never argue about politics.

exercises.prompt: Они́ зна́ют друг ___ уже́ пять лет. (each other)
exercises.promptTranslation: They have known each other for five years.

exercises.prompt: Брат и сестра́ всегда́ помога́ют друг ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: The brother and sister always help each other.
They talk to each other.
We have loved each other for a long time.
They think about each other.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means “each other” as a direct object?

lessons.title: 161. Declining last names: Петро́в, Толсто́й, Смит
lessons.subtitle: Я говорю́ с Петро́вым. Я чита́ю кни́гу Толсто́го.

explanations.title: Men's Russian surnames
explanations.body: Surnames in -ов, -ев and -ин decline like nouns, except that the instrumental is -ым. Surnames in -ой and -ий decline like adjectives in every case.

examples.translation: I am reading Tolstoy's book.
We are talking about Mayakovsky.
I am talking with Petrov.

explanations.title: Women's and foreign surnames
explanations.body: Russian women's surnames decline like feminine adjectives, but those in -ова, -ева and -ина have the accusative -у (Петро́ву), not -ую. Foreign men's surnames ending in a consonant decline like nouns (Смит, Сми́та), but foreign women's surnames do not change at all.

examples.translation: I know Ms. Petrova.
This is Smith's book.
I know Emma Gill.

exercises.promptTranslation: I am talking with Mr Petrov.
I am talking with Ms Petrova.
We are reading Tolstoy's book.
We are talking about Mayakovsky.
I know Ms Petrova.

exercises.explanation: Foreign men's surnames decline like nouns.
exercises.promptTranslation: This is Smith's book.

exercises.explanation: Foreign women's surnames do not change.
exercises.promptTranslation: I know Emma Gill.

exercises.prompt: How does a man's surname in -ов decline in the instrumental?

exercises.explanation: Foreign women's surnames are not declined.

lessons.title: 162. Going in, out, to, away: в-, вы-, при-, у-
lessons.subtitle: Он вошёл в класс. Она́ вы́шла из ко́мнаты. Они́ прие́хали.

explanations.title: Prefixes change the meaning
explanations.body: Add a prefix to a verb of motion and it stops being unidirectional or multidirectional and becomes an ordinary imperfective or perfective verb. From -ходи́ть you get an imperfective and from -йти́ the perfective. The prefix в- (in) is the opposite of вы- (out), and при- (arrive) is the opposite of у- (leave).

examples.text: В класс не входи́ть! Там идёт экза́мен.
examples.translation: Don't enter the room! There is an exam.
Guests came to see us yesterday.
He has already gone home.

explanations.title: Other verbs of motion
explanations.body: Ездить becomes -езжа́ть / -е́хать, бе́гать becomes -бега́ть / -бежа́ть, лета́ть becomes -лета́ть / -лете́ть and пла́вать becomes -плыва́ть / -плыть. After в- the hard sign appears before е: въезжа́ть, въе́хать.

explanations.title: Running, flying, swimming
explanations.body: The same pattern works for running (-бега́ть, -бежа́ть), flying (-лета́ть, -лете́ть) and swimming (-плыва́ть, -плыть). Note that in perfective forms with вы- the stress moves onto the prefix: вы́бежать, вы́лететь, вы́плыть.

exercises.prompt: Он ___ в класс и сел. (walked in)
exercises.promptTranslation: He walked into the classroom and sat down.
She walked out of the room.

exercises.prompt: Вчера́ к нам ___ го́сти. (arrived on foot)
exercises.promptTranslation: Guests came to see us yesterday.

exercises.prompt: За́втра они́ ___ домо́й. (will leave by car)
exercises.promptTranslation: Tomorrow they will drive off home.
The birds flew south.

exercises.prompt: Я ___ из до́ма в 7 часо́в. (every day, leave)
exercises.promptTranslation: I leave the house at 7 o'clock.

exercises.prompt: What happens to в- before -езжа́ть and -е́хать?
options: a hard sign is added: въезжа́ть

lessons.title: 163. Where to, where from: prepositions with prefixed motion verbs
lessons.subtitle: Он вошёл в ко́мнату. Она́ прие́хала к дру́гу.

explanations.title: Prefix and preposition
explanations.body: Each prefix pairs with certain prepositions. Войти́ and вы́йти have one each. При- and у- mean going to or away from a place, so they use the same prepositions as ordinary motion: в / на + accusative, к + dative for destinations and из / с / от + genitive for starting points.

rows: прийти́ в теа́тр, прие́хать к дру́гу
прийти́ из теа́тра, прие́хать от дру́га
уйти́ в теа́тр, уе́хать к дру́гу
уйти́ из теа́тра, улете́ть с конфере́нции

examples.translation: He walked into the room.
She walked out of the classroom.
We arrived at a friend's.
We came back from a friend's.

explanations.title: Opposites and stepping out
explanations.body: Войти́ is the opposite of вы́йти, and прийти́ is the opposite of уйти́. Вы́йти also means to step out for a short time: Где дире́ктор? — Он вы́шел. Подожди́те немно́го.

examples.text: Где дире́ктор? — Он вы́шел. Подожди́те немно́го.
examples.translation: Where is the director? — He stepped out. Wait a bit.
We flew in from a conference.

exercises.promptTranslation: He walked into the room.
She walked out of the classroom.
We arrived at a friend's.
We came from a friend's.
She flew in from the conference.
He ran out into the street.
He left the theater at 10.

exercises.prompt: Which is the opposite of войти́?
Which preposition means “from a person's place”?

lessons.title: 164. Aspect with prefixed motion verbs
lessons.subtitle: Обы́чно я выхожу́ в 7, но вчера́ вы́шел в 9.

explanations.title: Which aspect?
explanations.body: Prefixed verbs of motion follow the same aspect rules as other verbs. The perfective exists only in the past and the future. The imperfective works in all three tenses and shows habit, repetition or process. The perfective shows a single completed action or an intention to complete it.

rows: Обы́чно я выхожу́ из до́ма в 7 утра́.
Вчера́ я вы́шел из до́ма в 9. За́втра я вы́йду в 9.
Когда́ я выходи́л из до́ма, зазвони́л телефо́н.

examples.text: В про́шлом году́ я ка́ждый день выходи́л из до́ма в 8 часо́в.
examples.translation: Last year I left the house at 8 every day.
Soon the birds will fly south.

explanations.title: “Visited” and “has been”
explanations.body: In the past tense the imperfective can also report that an action happened and is over: the person came and left. The perfective says that they arrived and are still there.

rows: Сего́дня ко мне никто́ не приходи́л.

examples.translation: Guests visited us yesterday.

examples.text: Дверь откры́та. В э́ту ко́мнату кто-то входи́л.
examples.translation: The door is open. Someone has been in this room.

exercises.prompt: Обы́чно я ___ из до́ма в 7 часо́в. (leave, habit)
exercises.promptTranslation: I usually leave the house at 7.

exercises.prompt: Вчера́ я ___ из до́ма в 9 часо́в. (left, once)
exercises.promptTranslation: Yesterday I left the house at 9.
Tomorrow I will also leave at 9.
He has already gone home.

exercises.prompt: Ско́ро пти́цы ___ на юг. (will fly away)
exercises.promptTranslation: Soon the birds will fly south.

exercises.prompt: What does Вчера́ к нам приходи́ли го́сти mean?
exercises.explanation: Imperfective past: the visit is over.

exercises.prompt: Which aspect can be used in the present tense?
exercises.explanation: Only the imperfective has a present tense.

lessons.title: 165. Guests and holidays: гость, праздник, С днём рождения!
lessons.subtitle: Поздравля́ю тебя́ с днём рожде́ния! Жела́ю тебе́ здоро́вья!

explanations.title: Having people over
explanations.body: Go to someone's house в го́сти (as a guest). The person who invites you is the хозя́ин (host, owner) or хозя́йка. Приглаша́ть / пригласи́ть means to invite, and отмеча́ть means to celebrate a holiday.

examples.translation: Come and visit us!
The host invited Nina to the table.
We are celebrating the holiday on Saturday.

explanations.title: Congratulations, wishes and toasts
explanations.body: Поздравля́ть с + instrumental names the occasion. Жела́ть takes the dative of the person and the genitive of what you wish. The toast За + accusative names the person or thing you drink to.

examples.translation: I congratulate you on your birthday!
I wish you health and happiness!

exercises.promptTranslation: Happy birthday to you!
I wish you health.
Come visit us!

lessons.title: 166. Setting the table: таре́лка, ви́лка, блины́
lessons.subtitle: Ма́ма накрыва́ет на стол. Положи́ ви́лку ря́дом с таре́лкой.

explanations.title: On the table
explanations.body: To set the table is накрыва́ть на стол (accusative!). Here are the things you put on it.

examples.translation: Mom is setting the table.

examples.text: На столе́ стоя́т таре́лки и ло́жки.
examples.translation: Plates and spoons are on the table.

explanations.title: Food and treats
explanations.body: These words are useful for any Russian meal. Note that пиро́жное and моро́женое decline like adjectives, and пече́нье and колбаса́ follow the patterns you know.

examples.translation: We drink tea with cookies.

lessons.title: 167. Relative clauses in every case: с которым, о которой
lessons.subtitle: Э́то де́вушка, о кото́рой я говорю́.

explanations.title: Gender from the noun, case from the clause
explanations.body: Кото́рый (which, who, that) agrees in gender and number with the noun it refers to, but its case depends on its job in its own clause, including after a preposition.

examples.text: Э́то ма́льчик, с кото́рым я дружу́.
examples.translation: This is the boy I am friends with.

examples.text: Э́то де́вушка, о кото́рой я говорю́.
examples.translation: This is the girl I am talking about.

examples.text: Вот дом, в кото́ром я живу́.
examples.translation: Here is the house I live in.
This is the teacher I help.

examples.text: Вот кни́га, кото́рую я купи́л вчера́.
examples.translation: Here is the book that I bought yesterday.

exercises.explanation: Gender from the noun it replaces.

options: Its role in its own clause

units.title: Unit 19: Comparison, the dative plural, need and own

lessons.title: 169. More interesting, faster, colder: the comparative in -ее
lessons.subtitle: Э́тот фильм интере́снее, чем тот.

explanations.title: Add -ее to the stem
explanations.body: You know лу́чше and бо́льше. Most other comparatives are built the same simple way: take the stem of the adjective and add -ее. The result never changes for gender, number or case, and it is used with чем (than).

rows: Мой брат бе́гает быстре́е, чем я.

examples.text: Э́тот фильм интере́сный, но тот был интере́снее.
examples.translation: This film is interesting, but that one was more interesting.

examples.text: Мой брат бе́гает быстре́е, чем я.
examples.translation: My brother runs faster than I do.
Today is colder than yesterday.

explanations.title: Where does the stress go?
explanations.body: The stress often jumps onto the -ее: быстре́е, холодне́е, нове́е. Words with three or more syllables may keep their stress where it was: краси́вее, прия́тнее. Check each new word.

examples.translation: This river is more beautiful than that one.
You are stronger than I am.

exercises.promptTranslation: This film is more interesting than that one.
My brother runs faster than I do.
Today is colder than yesterday.
My car is newer than yours.
This river is more beautiful than that one.
You are stronger than I am.

exercises.prompt: Which suffix forms the simple comparative?
Does интере́снее change for gender or number?

lessons.title: 170. Closer, higher, cheaper: irregular comparatives
lessons.subtitle: Мой друг живёт бли́же к институ́ту, чем я.

explanations.title: Learn these by heart
explanations.body: Some very common comparatives are not made with -ее. The final consonant of the stem changes and the ending is -е (or -ше). Here are the first ones, about size, distance and price.

examples.text: Мой друг живёт бли́же к институ́ту, чем я.
examples.translation: My friend lives closer to the institute than I do.

examples.text: Та ку́ртка дешёвая, но э́та ещё деше́вле.
examples.translation: That jacket is cheap, but this one is even cheaper.
This river is deeper than that one.

explanations.title: More irregular comparatives
explanations.body: These are about time, frequency and everyday qualities.

examples.translation: English is easier than Russian.
He comes later than I do.
I get up earlier than you do.

exercises.prompt: Мой друг живёт ___ к институ́ту, чем я. (closer)
exercises.promptTranslation: My friend lives closer to the institute than I do.

exercises.prompt: Та ку́ртка дешёвая, но э́та ещё ___. (cheaper)
exercises.promptTranslation: That jacket is cheap, but this one is even cheaper.
English is easier than Russian.

exercises.prompt: Моя́ шко́ла ___ от до́ма, чем твоя́. (farther)
exercises.promptTranslation: My school is farther from home than yours.
I get up earlier than you do.
He comes later than I do.
This room is cleaner than mine.
My desk is higher than yours.

exercises.prompt: Which is the comparative of дорого́й?
Which is the comparative of ча́сто?

lessons.title: 171. Than: чем or the genitive
lessons.subtitle: Я ни́же, чем он. Я ни́же тебя́.

explanations.title: Two ways to say “than”
explanations.body: After a comparative you can use чем and put the second thing in the same case as the first, or, if the first thing is in the nominative, you can drop чем and put the second thing in the genitive.

examples.translation: My brother is older than me.
You are younger than us.
Anton is younger than Nina.

explanations.title: When чем is required
explanations.body: You may use the genitive only when the first thing is a subject in the nominative. If the first thing is an object, keep чем: Ты лю́бишь меня́ ме́ньше, чем его́. Here меня́ is the accusative, so what follows чем must be accusative too (его́).

examples.text: Ты лю́бишь меня́ ме́ньше, чем его́.
examples.translation: You love me less than him.
I am shorter than he is.

exercises.promptTranslation: My brother is older than me.
You are younger than us.
I am shorter than he is.
You love me less than him.
My house is closer than yours.
Anton is younger than Nina.

exercises.prompt: When can you replace чем with the genitive?
options: When the first thing is in the accusative
When the first thing is in the nominative

lessons.title: 172. More, most, very: бо́лее, са́мый, -ейший
lessons.subtitle: Э́то са́мый краси́вый го́род.

explanations.title: A second way to compare: бо́лее and ме́нее
explanations.body: Besides the -ее form, Russian has a compound comparative: бо́лее (more) or ме́нее (less) + the full adjective. Бо́лее and ме́нее never change, but the adjective agrees with its noun in the usual way. It is mostly used before a noun.

examples.translation: This is a more beautiful city.

examples.text: Я не зна́ю бо́лее краси́вого го́рода.
examples.translation: I don't know a more beautiful city.

explanations.title: The superlative: са́мый and всех
explanations.body: Са́мый + adjective means the most. Both words agree with the noun. As a predicate you can use the simple comparative plus всех (than all). For adverbs use всего́: лу́чше всего́ (best of all).

examples.translation: Viktor runs faster than anyone.

examples.text: Я люблю́ танцева́ть, но лу́чше всего́ я танцу́ю та́нго.
examples.translation: I love dancing, but best of all I dance the tango.

explanations.title: Very: -ейший, лу́чший, ху́дший
explanations.body: Adding -ейш- (or -айш- after г, к, х, which become ж, ч, ш) says that something has a quality to a very high degree. It is not compared with anything. Лу́чший and ху́дший mean best and worst; са́мый can be added for emphasis.

examples.translation: This is a very interesting book. Read it.
Andrei is my best friend.

exercises.promptTranslation: This is the most beautiful city.
This is the most beautiful river.
This is a more interesting film.
Viktor runs faster than anyone.

exercises.prompt: Я люблю́ танцева́ть, но лу́чше ___ я танцу́ю та́нго.
exercises.promptTranslation: I love dancing, but best of all I dance the tango.
Andrei is my best friend.

exercises.prompt: Э́то ___ уро́к в уче́бнике. (a very hard)
exercises.promptTranslation: This is a very hard lesson in the textbook.

options: Forms the superlative and agrees with the noun

exercises.prompt: Which means “She is the most beautiful”?

lessons.title: 173. Much faster, a bit slower, the sooner the better
lessons.subtitle: Чем ра́ньше, тем лу́чше! Как мо́жно скоре́е!

explanations.title: Making a comparison stronger or weaker
explanations.body: Put гора́здо or намно́го (much) or ещё (even) before the comparative to strengthen it. Add the prefix по- to the comparative to say “a bit”: побыстре́е (a bit faster), посмеле́е (a bit braver).

rows: Э́та кни́га гора́здо интере́снее, чем та.
Моя́ но́вая маши́на е́здит намно́го быстре́е.
Я сме́лый, но он ещё смеле́е!

examples.text: Э́та кни́га гора́здо интере́снее, чем та.
examples.translation: This book is much more interesting than that one.

examples.text: Я сме́лый, но он ещё смеле́е!
examples.translation: I am brave, but he is even braver!
Speak a bit more slowly, please.

explanations.title: Set patterns
explanations.body: Learn these ready-made ways to compare: чем … тем … (the … the …), всё + comparative и … (more and more) and как мо́жно + comparative (as … as possible). To say by how much two people differ in age, use на: ста́рше на три го́да.

rows: Он ста́рше меня́ на три го́да.
He is three years older than me.
Она́ моло́же му́жа на пять лет.
She is five years younger than her husband.

exercises.promptTranslation: This book is much more interesting than that one.
I am brave, but he is even braver!
The sooner the better.
As soon as possible!
He is three years older than me.
She is five years younger than her husband.
He is two years older than me.
Higher and higher.

lessons.title: 174. To the students, to the parents: nouns in the dative plural
lessons.subtitle: Я звоню́ роди́телям. Учи́тель помога́ет студе́нтам.

explanations.title: -ам or -ям
explanations.body: The dative plural is the easiest plural form: add -ам after a hard stem and -ям after a soft one. It is built from the nominative plural, so the stress is the same as there, and the spelling rule applies: after ж, ч, ш and щ write а, not я.

examples.translation: The teacher helps the students.
I call my parents.
The doctor helps the sick.

explanations.title: Words to remember
explanations.body: Plural words that are not regular in the nominative plural give an irregular dative plural. Learn these.

examples.translation: We write letters to our friends.
He shows photos to the children.
We say this to people.

exercises.promptTranslation: I call my parents.
The teacher helps the students.
We write letters to our friends.
The doctor helps the children.
We tell this to people.
We show the station to the guests.
We call our aunts.

exercises.prompt: Which ending do hard-stem nouns take in the dative plural?
What is the dative plural of дя́дя?

lessons.title: 175. To new friends, on Saturdays: adjectives in the dative plural
lessons.subtitle: По суббо́там мы убира́ем ко́мнату.

explanations.title: -ым or -им
explanations.body: In the dative plural adjectives, ordinal numbers and adjectival pronouns take -ым after a hard stem and -им after a soft stem or after к, г, х, ж, ч, ш, щ. The same endings serve all three genders.

tables.note: Те and все take -ем: тем, всем. Его́, её and их do not change.

examples.translation: I write a letter to old friends.
We call our parents.
I will tell this to everyone.

explanations.title: Days and times: по + dative plural
explanations.body: По + the dative plural says that something happens regularly on those days or at those times: по суббо́там (on Saturdays), по у́трам (in the mornings), по вечера́м (in the evenings).

examples.translation: On Saturdays we clean our room.
He studies in the evenings.
It is important to eat breakfast in the morning.

exercises.promptTranslation: I write letters to good friends.
We help the new students.
I call my parents.
I will tell this to all the students.
On Saturdays we clean our room.
He studies in the evenings.
I work nights.
We have physical training on Wednesdays.

exercises.prompt: Which ending do hard-stem adjectives take in the dative plural?

lessons.title: 176. Time to sleep, it's a pity: more impersonal dative sentences
lessons.subtitle: Де́тям пора́ спать. Нам о́чень жаль.

explanations.title: Dative + a word for a state
explanations.body: You know Мне жа́рко. The same pattern works for many more states: the person is in the dative and the state is a single word that never changes. Add бы́ло or бу́дет for the past and the future.

rows: It is time for the children to sleep.
The director feels like going on vacation.

examples.translation: It's time for the children to go to bed.

examples.text: Нам о́чень жаль, что ты уезжа́ешь.
examples.translation: We are very sorry that you are leaving.
He has nothing to do.
We found the lecture interesting.

explanations.title: No subject at all
explanations.body: Some sentences have no subject whatever: На у́лице темно́. (It is dark outside.) Темне́ет. (It is getting dark.) Here Russian simply leaves out “it”.

examples.translation: It is dark outside.
It is getting dark.

exercises.promptTranslation: It's time for the children to go to bed.
We are very sorry that you are leaving.
He has nothing to do.

exercises.explanation: A state word does not change.
exercises.promptTranslation: We found the lecture interesting.
Anya and Katya are cold.
It is dark outside.
The director feels like going on vacation.

exercises.prompt: In which case is the person in Де́тям пора́ спать?

lessons.title: 177. I need a dictionary: нужен, нужна, нужно, нужны
lessons.subtitle: Мне ну́жен словарь. Тебе́ нужна́ маши́на.

explanations.title: Two ways to say “need”
explanations.body: На́до, ну́жно and необходи́мо (necessary) are followed by an infinitive: Мне на́до идти́. For a thing you need, use ну́жен, нужна́, ну́жно or нужны́ (and necessary: необходи́м, необходи́ма, необходи́мо, необходи́мы). The person who needs it is in the dative, and the word needed is the subject: it is in the nominative and the adjective agrees with it.

examples.translation: I need a new computer.
You do not need a car.
My son needs a coat.
Do you need money?
I need you.

explanations.title: Past and future
explanations.body: Put the right form of быть after the word. In на́до, ну́жно and необходи́мо sentences use бы́ло or бу́дет. With ну́жен use был, была́, бы́ло, бы́ли or бу́дет, бу́дут to agree with the thing needed. The need word comes first.

examples.translation: I needed a dictionary.
They needed me.
We will have to get up early.
Vitya had to call Anya.

exercises.promptTranslation: I need a new computer.
You do not need a car.
Do you need money?
My son needs a coat.
I need you.
I need to go.
Yesterday I needed a dictionary.
They needed me.

exercises.prompt: What do ну́жен, нужна́, ну́жно and нужны́ agree with?
exercises.explanation: They agree with the subject: the thing needed.

lessons.title: 178. My own: свой, своя, своё, свои
lessons.subtitle: Он лю́бит своего́ бра́та. Она́ пи́шет своему́ бра́ту.

explanations.title: One's own
explanations.body: Свой means “one's own” and refers back to the subject of the clause. Use it to make clear that the thing belongs to the person who does the action. With я, ты, мы and вы, свой is optional, but with он, она́ and они́ it prevents confusion: его́, её and их mean someone else's.

examples.translation: He loves his (own) brother very much.
I love his brother very much (not mine).
Anya is writing to her own brother.
He is looking for his (own) documents.

explanations.title: Forms and limits
explanations.body: Свой declines like мой and твой. It always refers to the subject of its own clause, so it can't be used when the owner is in another clause, and it can't describe the subject itself.

examples.text: Кири́лл говори́т, что его́ сестра́ пое́хала в магази́н.
examples.translation: Kirill says his sister has gone to the shop.

examples.text: У меня́ тепе́рь есть свой компью́тер.
examples.translation: I now have my own computer.

exercises.promptTranslation: He loves his own brother very much.
Anya is writing a letter to her own brother.
He is looking for his own documents.
The children are calling their father.

exercises.prompt: У меня́ тепе́рь есть ___ компью́тер. (my own)
exercises.promptTranslation: I now have my own computer.

exercises.prompt: Кири́лл говори́т, что ___ сестра́ пое́хала в магази́н. (his)
exercises.explanation: Свой can't modify the subject of another clause.
exercises.promptTranslation: Kirill says his sister went to the shop.

options: It refers to the subject of the clause
exercises.explanation: Свой refers back to the subject.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says Anya writes to her own brother?

lessons.subtitle: Э́тот фильм интере́снее, чем тот. Мне ну́жен словарь.

explanations.title: Quick map
explanations.body: A review of the main points of this unit.

rows: Я ни́же тебя́. Я ни́же, чем он.
Мне ну́жен словарь. Тебе́ нужна́ маши́на.
