units.title: Unit 20: Many, few, five: the genitive plural

lessons.title: 180. Many students, few lessons: the genitive plural in -ов
lessons.subtitle: В на́шем институ́те мно́го студе́нтов.

explanations.title: Hard consonant: add -ов
explanations.body: You know the genitive singular (нет кни́ги). Now the genitive plural. Most masculine nouns that end in a hard consonant simply add -ов. If the plural is stressed on the ending (столы́, дома́, города́), the genitive plural is stressed on -ов too.

examples.translation: There are many students at our institute.
There are few theaters in this city.
There are no tables in the room.

explanations.title: How many? Many, few, several
explanations.body: Words of quantity are followed by the genitive plural when you can count the things. This is the most common use of the case, so learn these words well.

examples.translation: How many students are in the group?
We have many lessons.
Most of the students live here.

explanations.title: Also: “of”, and nothing at all
explanations.body: The genitive plural also means “of” (the house of the students) and appears after нет (there are no).

examples.translation: This is the students' house.
There are no telephones in the hotel.

exercises.promptTranslation: We have many students at the institute.
There are several tables in the room.
How many theaters are in this city?
There are few stores in this district.

exercises.explanation: Дом → домо́в, with the stress on the ending.
exercises.promptTranslation: We saw many houses.
We have few lessons today.
There are no telephones in the hotel.

exercises.prompt: What ending do most masculine nouns in a hard consonant take in the genitive plural?
After мно́го, ма́ло and не́сколько with things you can count, the noun is in the...
exercises.explanation: Quantity words take the genitive plural.

lessons.title: 181. Museums, teachers, doctors: -ев and -ей
lessons.subtitle: В э́том го́роде мно́го музе́ев и учителе́й.

explanations.title: Nouns in -й: -ев
explanations.body: A masculine noun that ends in -й loses the -й and takes -ев (or -ёв when the ending is stressed).

examples.translation: There are many museums in Moscow.
There are few heroes in this book.

explanations.title: Soft sign, ж, ч, ш, щ: -ей
explanations.body: A masculine noun that ends in -ь takes -ей, and so does a masculine noun ending in ж, ч, ш or щ. Often the stress falls on the ending: учителе́й, ноже́й, враче́й.

examples.translation: How many teachers are in your school?
There are many doctors at the hospital.
I have no keys.

explanations.title: Nouns in -ец
explanations.body: A masculine noun in -ец loses the e and takes -цев when the stress stays on the stem, but -цов when the ending is stressed.

examples.translation: There are many Americans at the hotel.
There are three salesmen in the store.

exercises.promptTranslation: There are many museums in the city.
He has no dictionaries.
How many teachers are in your group?
There are many doctors at the hospital.
There are no knives on the table.
There are many cars in the parking lot.
There are many Americans at the hotel.
We have few guests.

exercises.prompt: What is the genitive plural ending of a masculine noun in -й, like музе́й?
What ending do masculine nouns in -ь, ж, ч, ш and щ take?
exercises.explanation: -ей after -ь and ж ч ш щ.

lessons.title: 182. Books, rooms, words: the zero ending
lessons.subtitle: В э́той ко́мнате мно́го книг.

explanations.title: Drop the last vowel
explanations.body: Feminine nouns in -а and neuter nouns in -о simply lose their ending in the genitive plural. There is nothing to add: кни́га → книг. This works when the stem ends in a single consonant.

examples.translation: There are many books in this room.
How many words do you know?
There are no seats on the bus.

explanations.title: The stress often moves back
explanations.body: Many nouns that are stressed on the ending in the singular are stressed on the stem in the genitive plural. Learn the common ones.

examples.translation: There are many countries in Europe.
There are many rivers in Russia.

explanations.title: Feminine nouns in -я
explanations.body: After a single consonant, many nouns in -я replace it with -ь: неде́ля → неде́ль.

examples.text: Я не был дома́ не́сколько неде́ль.
examples.translation: I was not at home for several weeks.

exercises.promptTranslation: I have many books.
There are many rooms in our house.
There are many countries in Europe.
How many schools are in your city?
We lived there for several weeks.
There are many words in this text.
There are no cars in the garage.
There are no free seats on the bus.

exercises.prompt: What happens to кни́га in the genitive plural?

lessons.title: 183. Female students, plates, windows: the fleeting vowel
lessons.subtitle: На столе́ нет таре́лок.

explanations.title: Two consonants need a vowel
explanations.body: When the stem ends in two consonants (as in студе́нт-к-а), the zero ending would leave them piled up at the end of the word. So Russian inserts a vowel between them: usually -о-, but -е- after ж, ч, ш, щ and after й.

examples.translation: There are many female students in our group.
There are no plates on the table.
I have no pens.

explanations.title: Words in -ня
explanations.body: Words in -ня do not follow one pattern, so learn them as they come. Some take -е- and no soft sign, and some take a vowel and a soft sign.

examples.translation: How many songs do you know?
There are no kitchens in this house.

explanations.title: Neuter nouns and “sisters”
explanations.body: Neuter nouns in -о can need a fleeting vowel too, and the stress may move to the first syllable. Сестра́ becomes сестёр.

examples.translation: There are many windows in this room.

examples.text: У неё нет ни бра́тьев, ни сестёр.
examples.translation: She has neither brothers nor sisters.

exercises.promptTranslation: There are many female students in our group.
There are no plates on the table.
There are many windows in this room.
We have no spoons.
How many songs do you know?
There are no kitchens in this house.
We bought several cups.
How many girls are in this group?

exercises.prompt: Why is the form студе́нток and not студе́нтк?
options: two consonants need a vowel between them

exercises.prompt: Which vowel is inserted in ру́чка → ру́чек?

lessons.title: 184. Squares, nights, lectures: -ей and -ий
lessons.subtitle: В э́том го́роде мно́го площаде́й.

explanations.title: Feminine -ь and neuter -е: -ей
explanations.body: Feminine nouns in a soft sign and neuter nouns in -е take -ей. The stress is often on the ending.

examples.translation: There are many squares in Moscow.
We did not sleep for several nights.
There are many seas in Russia.

explanations.title: Nouns in -ия and -ие: -ий
explanations.body: Nouns in -ия and -ие end in -ий in the genitive plural, the -ия or -ие is simply replaced by -ий.

examples.translation: There are many lectures at the institute.
There are many buildings in this city.
We have few classes today.

exercises.promptTranslation: There are many squares in our city.
How many doors are in this room?
We did not sleep for several nights.
There are many lectures at the institute.
How many buildings are in your city?
We have few classes today.
There are many seas in Russia.
There are no stations in this district.

exercises.prompt: What is the genitive plural ending of nouns in -ия and -ие?
What is the genitive plural ending of feminine nouns in a soft sign?

lessons.title: 185. Friends, children, people, years: irregular genitive plurals
lessons.subtitle: У неё мно́го друзе́й и пять лет опы́та.

explanations.title: Family and friends
explanations.body: These very common words are irregular. Learn them as they are.

examples.translation: I have many friends.

examples.text: У неё нет ни бра́тьев, ни сестёр.
examples.translation: She has neither brothers nor sisters.
There are many children in the park.

explanations.title: Years, times, days, names
explanations.body: After the numbers 5 and above, and after мно́го, ско́лько and не́сколько, use лет for years, раз for times and челове́к for a count of people. For people in general (not counting) use люде́й.

examples.translation: I have lived here for five years.
I was there many times.
There were five people at the lecture.
There were many people there.

explanations.title: Plural-only nouns and more
explanations.body: Nouns that exist only in the plural often have no ending at all, or a special one.

examples.translation: I have no money.
We waited two days.

exercises.promptTranslation: I have many friends.

exercises.prompt: У неё нет ни бра́тьев, ни ___. (sisters)
exercises.promptTranslation: She has neither brothers nor sisters.
There are many children in the park.
There were five people there.
Many people came to the concert.
I have lived here for five years.
I have been there many times.
I have no money.
How many names do you know?

lessons.title: 186. Of new friends, of all those: adjectives in the genitive plural
lessons.subtitle: У меня́ нет ру́сских друзе́й.

explanations.title: -ых or -их
explanations.body: Adjectives take -ых after a hard stem and -их after к, г, х, ж, ч, ш, щ and after a soft stem. The same ending serves all three genders, so you only need to learn one form for the plural.

examples.translation: I have no Russian friends.
He knows many new words.
How many good friends do you have?

explanations.title: Pronouns and “all”
explanations.body: Possessives, demonstratives and “all” follow the same pattern: -их with soft or ш/щ stems, and the special forms мои́х, твои́х, свои́х, всех, тех.

examples.translation: These are photographs of my parents.
There are none of those books in the store.

examples.text: Мы получи́ли письма́ от всех на́ших друзе́й.
examples.translation: We received letters from all our friends.

exercises.promptTranslation: I have no Russian friends.
We know many new words.
These are photographs of my parents.
There are none of those books in the store.
How many big cities have you seen?
We have few good cars.
We have none of these books.

exercises.prompt: Which ending do adjectives take in the genitive plural after к, г, х, ж, ч, ш, щ?
What is the genitive plural of мои́?

lessons.title: 187. Two new books, five new books: numbers with adjectives
lessons.subtitle: У нас два но́вых преподава́теля.

explanations.title: 2, 3, 4 and 5 and more
explanations.body: After 2, 3 and 4 the noun is in the genitive singular. The adjective before it is in the genitive plural for masculine and neuter nouns, but in the nominative plural for feminine nouns. After 5 and more, both the noun and the adjective are in the genitive plural.

examples.translation: We have two new teachers.
I bought two interesting books.
There are three big windows in the room.
There are five big windows in the room.

explanations.title: Longer numbers
explanations.body: Only the last word of the number matters: 22, 23 and 24 work like 2, 3 and 4, and 25 works like 5.

examples.text: В институ́те два́дцать два но́вых преподава́теля.
examples.translation: There are twenty-two new teachers at the institute.

examples.text: В институ́те два́дцать пять но́вых преподава́телей.
examples.translation: There are twenty-five new teachers at the institute.

exercises.promptTranslation: I have two older brothers.
We saw three big windows.
She has two younger sisters.
I bought two interesting books.
We have five new students.
We bought five interesting books.
There are six big windows in the room.

exercises.prompt: After 2, 3 and 4, a feminine adjective stands in the...
After 5 and more, adjective and noun are both in the...

lessons.title: 188. A lot of water, a little time: countable and uncountable
lessons.subtitle: У меня́ ма́ло вре́мени и мно́го рабо́ты.

explanations.title: Things you can count, things you cannot
explanations.body: After мно́го, ма́ло, ско́лько and сто́лько use the genitive plural for things you can count, but the genitive singular for things you cannot count: water, milk, time, work. Не́сколько always counts things, so for uncountable things use немно́го (a little).

examples.text: У меня́ ма́ло вре́мени и мно́го рабо́ты.
examples.translation: I have little time and a lot of work.
There is little water in the cup.
I need a little bread.

explanations.title: More uncountable words
explanations.body: Words for liquids, foods, materials, feelings and abstract ideas are usually uncountable.

examples.translation: There is little milk in the refrigerator.
Tomorrow there will be a lot of snow.

explanations.title: Most of...
explanations.body: Большинство́ (most) is followed by the genitive plural. The verb is usually singular.

examples.translation: Most of the students live in Moscow.

exercises.promptTranslation: There is little water in the cup.
I need a little bread.
I have a lot of work today.
How much time do you have?
There is little milk in the refrigerator.
I have few friends.
Most of the students live in Moscow.

exercises.prompt: What do you use after мно́го with an uncountable noun?

lessons.title: 189. Two of them, three children: двое, трое, четверо
lessons.subtitle: У них дво́е дете́й.

explanations.title: Collective numerals
explanations.body: For groups of male persons and for children there is a second set of numerals. They are followed by the genitive plural. They are not used for women, so say две сестры́, not дво́е сестёр.

examples.translation: They have two children.
We have four neighbors.
There were three of us.

explanations.title: Plural-only nouns
explanations.body: The same numerals are used with nouns that exist only in the plural, such as су́тки (a day and night), но́жницы (scissors) and часы́ (watch).

examples.translation: We waited for two days.
I need three pairs of scissors.

exercises.promptTranslation: They have three children.
There were two of us.
We have four neighbors.
She has two sisters.
We waited for two days.
There are five boys in the class.

exercises.explanation: Collective numerals are not used for women.

exercises.prompt: What case follows the collective numerals?

lessons.title: 190. Without friends, after classes: prepositions with the genitive plural
lessons.subtitle: По́сле заня́тий мы идём домо́й.

explanations.title: Prepositions that take the genitive
explanations.body: Every preposition that takes the genitive singular takes the genitive plural too. Here are the common ones.

examples.translation: He came without his friends.
After lessons we go home.
These are gifts for the children.

explanations.title: “Of” and “one of”
explanations.body: A noun in the genitive plural after another noun means “of”. After оди́н, ка́ждый and не́которые use из with the genitive plural.

examples.translation: This is my parents' house.

examples.text: Оди́н из мои́х друзе́й живёт в Ки́еве.
examples.translation: One of my friends lives in Kyiv.
Each of the students received a book.

exercises.promptTranslation: He came to the party without his friends.
I received a letter from my parents.
We arrived before the classes.
After the lessons we go home.

exercises.prompt: Оди́н из мои́х ___ живёт в Ки́еве. (friends)
exercises.promptTranslation: One of my friends lives in Kyiv.
My parents have a big apartment.
Because of problems we did not go.
These are gifts for the children.

exercises.prompt: What case do без, от, до, по́сле, из and для take?

lessons.title: 191. I know the students: the accusative plural of animate nouns
lessons.subtitle: Я зна́ю э́тих студе́нтов.

explanations.title: Animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative
explanations.body: In the accusative plural, nouns for people and animals look like the genitive plural. Nouns for things look like the nominative plural. Adjectives and pronouns follow the noun.

examples.translation: I know these students.
We saw my parents.
I am reading new magazines.

explanations.title: More examples
explanations.body: Remember this for all the verbs that take a direct object: знать, ви́деть, люби́ть, ждать, звать.

examples.translation: She loves her children.
Did you see our neighbors?
We are waiting for these guests.

exercises.promptTranslation: I know these students.
We saw my parents in the park.
She loves her children.
I am reading new magazines.
We are waiting for our friends.
Did you see these windows?
He knows all the neighbors.

exercises.prompt: The accusative plural of animate nouns is identical to the...
The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is identical to the...

lessons.title: 192. Review: the genitive plural
lessons.subtitle: У нас мно́го книг, друзе́й и зда́ний.

explanations.title: All the endings in one table
explanations.body: Look at the last letter of the singular and choose the ending.

examples.text: У нас мно́го книг, друзе́й и зда́ний.
examples.translation: We have many books, friends and buildings.

explanations.title: The irregular words
explanations.body: Learn these by heart: друзе́й, бра́тьев, сынове́й, матере́й, дочере́й, сестёр, дете́й, люде́й, челове́к, лет, раз, дней, имён, де́нег.

examples.text: Я жил там пять лет и ви́дел мно́го люде́й.
examples.translation: I lived there for five years and saw many people.

exercises.promptTranslation: There are many students at the institute.
How many rooms are in your house?
There are three big windows in this room.
I have lived here for five years.
I have many Russian friends.
There are many museums in Moscow.
There are many female students in the group.
There are many buildings in our city.
We saw my parents.
She has three children.

exercises.prompt: What is the genitive plural of сестра́?

units.title: Unit 21: Prefixed verbs of motion and driving

lessons.title: 193. Walk in, walk by, walk across: prefix + motion verb
lessons.subtitle: Он ка́ждый день захо́дит в магази́н.

explanations.title: What a prefix does to aspect
explanations.body: A plain verb of motion is always imperfective, with a multidirectional and a unidirectional form. Add a prefix and that pair disappears: the verb is now imperfective or perfective. A prefix on a multidirectional verb gives the imperfective, and a prefix on a unidirectional verb gives the perfective.

examples.text: Он ка́ждый день захо́дит в магази́н.
examples.translation: He stops in at the store every day.

examples.text: Вчера́ он зашёл в магази́н и купи́л хлеб.
examples.translation: Yesterday he stopped in at the store and bought bread.

explanations.title: The stems change a little
explanations.body: The prefix attaches to the stem, which is not always the same as the infinitive. Идти́ becomes -йти́ (зайти́), е́здить becomes -езжа́ть (заезжа́ть), пла́вать becomes -плыва́ть (переплыва́ть), and бе́гать becomes -бега́ть, with the stress shifting to the ending.

examples.text: Мы ка́ждое у́тро прохо́дим ми́мо шко́лы.
examples.translation: Every morning we walk past the school.
Suddenly a bus drove past us.

exercises.prompt: Ка́ждый день он ___ в магази́н. (stops in)
exercises.promptTranslation: Every day he stops in at the store.

exercises.prompt: Он ___ в магази́н и купи́л хлеб. (stopped in)
exercises.promptTranslation: He stopped in at the store and bought bread.

exercises.prompt: Ка́ждое у́тро мы ___ ми́мо шко́лы. (walk past)
exercises.promptTranslation: Every morning we walk past the school.
Suddenly a bus drove past us.

exercises.prompt: Он ___ ре́ку за пять мину́т. (swam across it)
exercises.explanation: Done once, in five minutes: perfective.
exercises.promptTranslation: He swam across the river in five minutes.

exercises.prompt: A prefix added to a unidirectional verb (идти́, е́хать) makes the verb...
What is the perfective partner of проезжа́ть?

lessons.title: 194. Come up to, move away from: под- and от-
lessons.subtitle: Же́нщина подошла́ к окну́.

explanations.title: под- means “up to”
explanations.body: Under the prefix под- the motion ends next to something: you come up to a person or a thing. The preposition is к with the dative. You can also leave out the thing and just say подойти́.

examples.text: Же́нщина подошла́ к окну́ и откры́ла его́.
examples.translation: The woman walked up to the window and opened it.
The taxi pulled up to the hotel.
The girl ran up to her mother.

explanations.title: от- means “away from”
explanations.body: The prefix от- is the opposite: you move away from something. The preposition is от with the genitive. It also describes the departure of buses and trains (but not planes).

examples.translation: Get away from the road!
The car drove away from the house.
Our train leaves at nine.

exercises.promptTranslation: The woman walked up to the window.
Get away from the road!
The taxi pulled up to the hotel.
The car drove away from the house.

exercises.prompt: Де́вочка ___ к ма́ме и обняла́ её. (ran up)
exercises.promptTranslation: The girl ran up to her mother and hugged her.
The train leaves at nine o'clock.
The boat came up to the shore.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition follows от-verbs such as отойти́?

lessons.title: 195. Up the mountain, down the stairs: вз- and с-
lessons.subtitle: Тури́сты взошли́ на верши́ну горы́.

explanations.title: вз- (вс-): up
explanations.body: The prefix вз- means motion up, onto something high, or off the ground. It is spelled вс- before voiceless consonants. The preposition is на or в with the accusative.

examples.translation: The tourists climbed to the top of the mountain.
The plane took off at eight o'clock.
The sun has already risen.

explanations.title: с-: down, off
explanations.body: The prefix с- is the opposite: motion down, or off something. The preposition is с with the genitive.

examples.translation: The children ran down from the hill.
The bird flew off the branch.

examples.text: Мы съе́хали с шоссе́ и пое́хали в дере́вню.
examples.translation: We turned off the highway and drove to the village.

exercises.promptTranslation: The tourists climbed to the top of the mountain.
The children ran down from the hill.
The bird flew off the branch.
The plane took off at eight o'clock.

exercises.prompt: Мы ___ с шоссе́ и пое́хали в дере́вню. (turned off)
exercises.promptTranslation: We turned off the highway and drove to the village.
The sun has already risen.

exercises.prompt: Он ___ с по́езда на ста́нции. (got off)
exercises.promptTranslation: He got off the train at the station.

exercises.prompt: What is the opposite of взбежа́ть?

lessons.title: 196. Get as far as, get across: до- and пере-
lessons.subtitle: Мы дошли́ до моста́ за де́сять мину́т.

explanations.title: до-: as far as
explanations.body: The prefix до- means reaching a certain point. The preposition is до with the genitive. Often you add за and a time to say how long it took.

rows: Мы дошли́ до моста́ за де́сять мину́т.
Она́ дое́хала до вокза́ла за час.
Мы долете́ли до Москвы́ за три часа́.

examples.text: Мы дошли́ до моста́ за де́сять мину́т.
examples.translation: We walked to the bridge in ten minutes.

examples.text: Она́ дое́хала до вокза́ла за час.
examples.translation: She got to the station in an hour.

explanations.title: пере-: across, over
explanations.body: The prefix пере- means motion across or over something. The thing crossed is in the accusative, with or without че́рез.

examples.text: Пешехо́д перешёл доро́гу на зелёный свет.
examples.translation: The pedestrian crossed the road on the green light.

examples.text: Мы перее́хали мост и пое́хали да́льше.
examples.translation: We drove across the bridge and drove on.
The ball flew over the fence.

exercises.prompt: Мы ___ до моста́ за де́сять мину́т. (walked as far as)
exercises.promptTranslation: We walked to the bridge in ten minutes.

exercises.prompt: Она́ ___ до вокза́ла за час. (drove as far as)
exercises.promptTranslation: She got to the station in an hour.
The pedestrian crossed the road on the green light.

exercises.prompt: Мы ___ мост и пое́хали да́льше. (drove across)
exercises.promptTranslation: We drove across the bridge and drove on.
He crossed the river by boat.
The ball flew over the fence.
We walked as far as the park.

lessons.title: 197. Walk past, miss the stop: про-
lessons.subtitle: Авто́бус прое́хал ми́мо остано́вки.

explanations.title: про-: past or through
explanations.body: The prefix про- covers three ideas: moving past something, moving through or across something, and covering a distance. Pass-by verbs take ми́мо with the genitive, and crossing verbs take че́рез with the accusative.

rows: За день мы прошли́ два́дцать киломе́тров.

examples.text: Она́ пробежа́ла ми́мо меня́ и не поздоро́валась.
examples.translation: She ran past me and did not say hello.
We walked through the park.

examples.text: За день мы прошли́ два́дцать киломе́тров.
examples.translation: In one day we covered twenty kilometers.

explanations.title: Missing your stop
explanations.body: When you go past a place where you meant to stop, you also use про-: прое́хать, пройти́. The place is in the accusative, with no preposition.

examples.text: Я заду́мался и прое́хал свою́ остано́вку.
examples.translation: I got lost in thought and missed my stop.
The bus drove past the stop.
The cars drove across the square.

exercises.promptTranslation: The bus drove past the stop.
We walked through the park.
I got lost in thought and missed my stop.
In one day we covered twenty kilometers.

exercises.prompt: Она́ ___ ми́мо меня́ и не поздоро́валась. (ran past)
exercises.promptTranslation: She ran past me and did not say hello.
We walked past the school.
The cars drove across the square.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition goes with про- when you pass by something?

options: I got off at my stop

lessons.title: 198. Drop in, go behind, go around: за- and о(б)-
lessons.subtitle: По доро́ге домо́й я зайду́ в апте́ку.

explanations.title: за-: behind, in, by
explanations.body: The prefix за- has several uses. All of them are about moving off the main path for a moment.

rows: Зайди́ в дом, на у́лице хо́лодно.
Я зайду́ к тебе́ по́сле рабо́ты.
По доро́ге домо́й я зайду́ в апте́ку.
Он зашёл сли́шком далеко́ в лес.

examples.translation: The dog ran behind the house.

examples.text: Я зайду́ к тебе́ по́сле рабо́ты.
examples.translation: I will drop in on you after work.

examples.text: По доро́ге домо́й я зайду́ в апте́ку.
examples.translation: On the way home I will stop at the pharmacy.

explanations.title: о- / об-: around
explanations.body: The prefix о- (об- before a vowel) means motion around something. It takes вокру́г with the genitive, or just the accusative. It also means going around an obstacle, and covering a whole area.

examples.translation: We walked around the lake.
The driver drove around the pothole.
We walked all over the city.

exercises.prompt: По доро́ге домо́й я ___ в апте́ку. (will stop in)
exercises.explanation: За- = stop in on the way.
exercises.promptTranslation: On the way home I will stop at the pharmacy.
The dog ran behind the house.
We walked around the lake.
The driver drove around the pothole.
He went too far into the forest.

exercises.prompt: Я ___ к тебе́ по́сле рабо́ты. (will drop in)
exercises.promptTranslation: I will drop in on you after work.
We walked all over the city.

options: I will go away from you
I will drop in on you

lessons.title: 199. Gather and disperse; walk around a while: с-…ся, раз-…ся, по-, за-
lessons.subtitle: Все ро́дственники съе́хались на пра́здник.

explanations.title: Coming together, going apart
explanations.body: With the particle -ся, the prefix с- means “gather from many places to one” and раз- (разъ- before я, е, ю, ё) means “scatter from one place to many”. The gathering place takes в, на or к, and the dispersal takes по with the dative.

rows: По́сле конце́рта все разошли́сь по дома́м.

examples.translation: All the relatives came together for the anniversary.

examples.text: По́сле конце́рта все разошли́сь по дома́м.
examples.translation: After the concert everyone went home.

explanations.title: A prefix that does not show direction
explanations.body: Sometimes a prefix with a multidirectional verb only tells you about time or about a round trip. По- means “for a while”, за- means “to begin”, and с- means “go there and come back”.

rows: Он встал и заходи́л по ко́мнате.
Я схожу́ в магази́н и бы́стро верну́сь.
go there and back by vehicle

examples.translation: The child ran around for a while and fell asleep.

examples.text: Я схожу́ в магази́н и бы́стро верну́сь.
examples.translation: I will pop out to the store and be right back.

exercises.promptTranslation: All the relatives came together for the holiday.
After the lecture the students went home.

exercises.prompt: Я ___ в магази́н и бы́стро верну́сь. (will go there and back)
exercises.promptTranslation: I will pop out to the store and be right back.

exercises.prompt: Ребёнок ___ по ко́мнате и успоко́ился. (ran around a while)
exercises.promptTranslation: The child ran around the room for a while and calmed down.

exercises.prompt: Он встал и ___ по ко́мнате. (began to pace)
exercises.promptTranslation: He got up and began to pace around the room.
The children scattered over the yard.

exercises.prompt: What does the prefix по- add to бе́гать?

lessons.title: 200. Move house, pass an exam, time flies: figurative prefixes
lessons.subtitle: Мы перее́хали в друго́й го́род.

explanations.title: The same prefixes, new meanings
explanations.body: Once you know what each prefix does, many figurative uses are easy to guess. Here are the most common ones.

examples.translation: We moved to another city.
The summer flew by.
This dress suits you.

explanations.title: More expressions
explanations.body: Some verbs of motion have become set phrases. Learn them whole.

rows: move away from (a topic, a habit)
Я схожу́ с ума́ от э́того шу́ма.

examples.translation: He gave up sports long ago.

examples.text: Я схожу́ с ума́ от э́того шу́ма.
examples.translation: This noise is driving me crazy.
The dog ran away from home.

exercises.promptTranslation: We moved to another city.
The summer flew by very quickly.
This dress suits you.
He passed the exam and is very glad.
The concert takes place on Saturday.
The dog ran away from home.

exercises.prompt: Я ___ с ума́ от э́того шу́ма! (am going crazy)
exercises.promptTranslation: This noise is driving me crazy!

exercises.prompt: What does «Он отошёл от спо́рта» mean?
What does «Мы с ним разошли́сь» mean?

lessons.title: 201. At the wheel: cars, roads and rentals
lessons.subtitle: Я получи́л права́ и купи́л маши́ну в автосало́не.

explanations.title: Cars and places
explanations.body: Here are the nouns you need to talk about cars and roads.

examples.text: Я получи́л права́ и купи́л маши́ну в автосало́не.
examples.translation: I got my driver's license and bought a car at a dealership.

examples.text: Мы взя́ли маши́ну напрока́т на неде́лю.
examples.translation: We rented a car for a week.

explanations.title: On the road
explanations.body: These words describe the road itself.

examples.translation: The light is red at the traffic light.

examples.text: В час пик на шоссе́ всегда́ про́бки.
examples.translation: At rush hour there are always traffic jams on the highway.

explanations.title: Verbs for drivers
explanations.body: Most of these come in aspect pairs. They are listed imperfective / perfective.

examples.text: Моя́ маши́на слома́лась, и я позвони́л в автомастерску́ю.
examples.translation: My car broke down and I called a repair shop.

examples.text: Нам ну́жно запра́виться: в ба́ке нет бензи́на.
examples.translation: We need to get gas: there is none in the tank.

exercises.prompt: Я получи́л ___ и купи́л маши́ну. (driver's license)
exercises.promptTranslation: I got my driver's license and bought a car.

exercises.prompt: В час пик на шоссе́ всегда́ ___. (traffic jams)
exercises.promptTranslation: At rush hour there are always traffic jams on the highway.

exercises.prompt: Нам ну́жно запра́виться: в ба́ке нет ___. (gasoline)
exercises.promptTranslation: We need to get gas: there is none in the tank.
We rented a car.
The light is red at the traffic light.
My car broke down.

explanations.title: Prefix meanings at a glance
explanations.body: Choose the prefix for the direction of the motion, then the preposition that goes with it.

units.title: Unit 22: Home, furniture and the instrumental plural

lessons.title: 204. Living room, bedroom, hallway: parts of a home
lessons.subtitle: Мы у́жинаем в гости́ной, а спим в спа́льне.

explanations.title: Rooms
explanations.body: Here are the rooms of a home. Note that гости́ная, ва́нная and прихо́жая look like feminine adjectives and decline that way: they are short for “living room”, “bathroom” and “entry room”, with the word ко́мната understood.

examples.translation: Mom spends a lot of time in the kitchen.

explanations.title: Parts of a house
explanations.body: These words describe the structure. Learn the unusual prepositional forms: на полу́ (on the floor) and на потолке́ (on the ceiling).

examples.translation: The staircase leads up to the roof.
The rug lies on the floor.
A chandelier hangs on the ceiling.

lessons.title: 205. Sofa, armchair, rug: furniture and interior
lessons.subtitle: Напро́тив дива́на стои́т кре́сло.

explanations.title: Furniture and interior
explanations.body: Learn the genders: they decide the adjective endings.

examples.translation: An armchair stands opposite the sofa.
A desk stands near the window.
A round mirror hangs on the wall.

explanations.title: Describing a place
explanations.body: These adjectives are useful when you describe a home. The shapes can be nouns or adjectives.

examples.translation: We want a spacious apartment.
We have a cozy living room.
The windows face the street.

explanations.title: Where things are: напро́тив, во́зле, среди́
explanations.body: These three prepositions take the genitive: напро́тив (opposite), во́зле (near), среди́ (among). Про́тив + genitive also means “against”.

examples.translation: A small table stands near the sofa.
The rug lies among the furniture.
I am against this plan.

exercises.promptTranslation: An armchair stands opposite the sofa.
A desk stands near the window.
A round mirror hangs on the wall.

The rug lies on the floor.

This is a comfortable chair.

lessons.title: 206. Lease, utilities, housewarming: renting and buying a home
lessons.subtitle: Мы подписа́ли догово́р аре́нды на год.

explanations.title: The housing market
explanations.body: These nouns come up when you rent, buy or move.

examples.text: Мы подписа́ли догово́р аре́нды на год.
examples.translation: We signed a lease for a year.
We found a place from an ad.
There is a playground in the yard.

explanations.title: Phrases
explanations.body: Useful set expressions for talking about where you live.

rows: С одно́й стороны́..., с друго́й стороны́...
On the one hand..., on the other hand...

examples.translation: We live on the outskirts of the city.

lessons.title: 207. Rent, hand over, host, forbid: verbs of the home
lessons.subtitle: Мы сня́ли кварти́ру в при́городе.

explanations.title: The verbs and their meanings
explanations.body: Many of these verbs have several meanings, so learn them with a typical object.

examples.translation: We rented an apartment in the suburbs.
Grandma rents two rooms to students.
This apartment suits me.

explanations.title: Some forms
explanations.body: Арендова́ть and сдава́ть are the new patterns here. The perfective forms of снять, приня́ть and сдать are worth memorizing.

examples.text: Не снима́йте пальто́, у нас хо́лодно.

lessons.title: 208. With friends, with children: the instrumental plural of nouns
lessons.subtitle: Я часто встречаюсь с друзья́ми.

explanations.title: -ами or -ями
explanations.body: In the instrumental plural, nouns take -ами after a hard stem and -ями after a soft stem. The stress stays where it was in the nominative plural. After к, г, х, ж, ч, ш, щ and ц the ending is -ами (never -ями).

examples.translation: I often meet with my friends.
We talk with our neighbors.
She is going to the doctors.

explanations.title: Remember these
explanations.body: Four nouns are special: люди, дети and дочери take -ьми and have end stress, and ма́тери becomes матеря́ми.

examples.translation: He got to know some interesting people.

examples.text: Она́ гуля́ет с детьми́ в па́рке.
examples.translation: She walks with the children in the park.
Paintings hang above the beds.

exercises.promptTranslation: I often meet with my friends.
We talk with our neighbors.
She walks with the children in the park.
He got acquainted with some people.
Mom is talking with her daughters.

exercises.explanation: Soft stem: -ями; stress as in учителя́.
exercises.promptTranslation: We talked with the teachers.
Paintings hang above the beds.
Snow lies under the trees.

exercises.prompt: Which ending do hard-stem nouns take in the instrumental plural?
After к, г, х, ж, ч, ш, щ the ending is...

lessons.title: 209. With new friends, with all of them: adjectives in the instrumental plural
lessons.subtitle: Мы ча́сто разгова́риваем с на́шими сосе́дями.

explanations.title: -ыми or -ими
explanations.body: Adjectives, ordinal numbers and adjectival pronouns take -ыми after a hard stem and -ими after a soft stem or after к, г, х, ж, ч, ш, щ. The stress stays where it was in the nominative plural.

examples.text: Я люблю́ знако́миться с интере́сными людьми́.
examples.translation: I like to get acquainted with interesting people.
He is interested in expensive cars.
We are friends with Russian students.

explanations.title: Pronouns
explanations.body: Possessives and demonstratives follow the same pattern. Те and все simply add -ми, and его, её, их never change.

examples.translation: I am not interested in those people.
I have already spoken with everyone.
She walks with his dogs.

exercises.promptTranslation: I like to get acquainted with interesting people.
He is interested in expensive cars.
I am speaking with everyone.
I am not interested in those people.
We went with my parents.
She walks with his dogs.

We are friends with Russian neighbors.

exercises.prompt: Which ending do adjectives take after к, г, х, ж, ч, ш, щ in the instrumental plural?
What is the instrumental plural of все?

lessons.title: 210. Interested in chess, proud of the children: using the instrumental plural
lessons.subtitle: Мама гордится свои́ми детьми́.

explanations.title: With, and verbs that take the instrumental
explanations.body: You already know the instrumental of the singular. The plural does the same jobs: with someone (с), the means or instrument, being or becoming someone, and verbs that require it.

examples.translation: I am interested in chess.
Mom is proud of her children.
We admire the paintings.

explanations.title: After над, под, перед, за, между
explanations.body: These prepositions take the instrumental when they say where something is. The plural noun ends in -ами or -ями.

examples.translation: Paintings hang above the beds.
Cars stand in front of the houses.
There is a square between the buildings.
We stood behind the trees.

explanations.title: Becoming and working as
explanations.body: After стать, рабо́тать and быть (in the past and future) the profession is in the instrumental.

examples.translation: They became doctors.
My sons work as engineers.

exercises.promptTranslation: I am interested in chess.
Mom is proud of her children.
We admire the paintings.
Paintings hang above the beds.
Cars stand in front of the houses.
They became doctors.
She speaks foreign languages.
We live together with our parents.

lessons.title: 211. They say, they sell, they called: indefinite-personal sentences
lessons.subtitle: Говоря́т, что он ско́ро же́нится.

explanations.title: No subject, “they” verb
explanations.body: When you do not say who does something, or it does not matter, Russian uses the third person plural of the verb and no subject. English uses “they”, “people” or the passive.

rows: They say he will get married soon.
Someone called me from the bank.
He was not admitted to the university.
In Russia people drink a lot of tea.
В на́шем до́ме не устра́ивают вечери́нок.
In our building people do not hold parties.

examples.translation: They say it will rain tomorrow.
Tickets are sold here.
Someone called me from the bank.

explanations.title: Tense and negation
explanations.body: In the past tense use the plural form in -ли. With a negative, a direct object goes into the genitive, as you saw with вечери́нок.

examples.translation: He was not admitted to the university.

examples.text: В на́шем до́ме не устра́ивают вечери́нок.
examples.translation: In our building people do not hold parties.
People do not smoke here.

People do not smoke here.

lessons.subtitle: Мы живём в просто́рной кварти́ре с хоро́шими сосе́дями.

explanations.title: The instrumental plural in one table
explanations.body: Memorize the five endings. Everything else is a special case.

headers: Soft or к г х ж ч ш щ

units.title: Unit 23: Health, the prepositional plural and short adjectives

lessons.title: 213. My throat hurts: illnesses, symptoms and parts of the body
lessons.subtitle: У меня́ боли́т го́рло и высо́кая температу́ра.

explanations.title: Illnesses and symptoms
explanations.body: The basic vocabulary for saying what is wrong.

examples.translation: I have a cold and a runny nose.
She has a high fever.
This is a cough medicine.

explanations.title: Parts of the body
explanations.body: In Russian you say that a part of the body hurts with у + genitive and the verb боле́ть in the third person. The body part is the subject, so the verb agrees with it: боли́т (singular), боля́т (plural).

examples.translation: My throat hurts.
The child has a stomachache.
His teeth hurt.

explanations.title: Pain in...
explanations.body: The noun боль takes в and the prepositional case: боль в спине́, боль в животе́, боль в го́рле.

examples.text: У неё си́льная боль в спине́.
examples.translation: She has severe back pain.
I have a sore throat.

exercises.promptTranslation: My throat hurts.
The child has a stomachache.
His teeth hurt.
She has a high fever.
I have severe back pain.
This is a cough medicine.
I have a cold and a runny nose.

exercises.prompt: What is the genitive of ка́шель?

lessons.title: 214. At the clinic: appointment, test, prescription
lessons.subtitle: Я записа́лся на приём к врачу́.

explanations.title: Words for a visit to the doctor
explanations.body: A clinic visit has its own vocabulary.

examples.text: Я записа́лся на приём к врачу́.
examples.translation: I made an appointment with the doctor.
The doctor wrote me a prescription.
I need to have a blood test.

explanations.title: Verbs at the doctor
explanations.body: These verbs come in aspect pairs.

rows: to call a doctor to the house

examples.translation: You take this medicine three times a day.

exercises.promptTranslation: I need a note from the clinic.
The nurse is measuring my blood pressure.

lessons.title: 215. I got the flu, I feel better: verbs of illness
lessons.subtitle: Как вы себя́ чу́вствуете? Спаси́бо, мне уже́ лу́чше.

explanations.title: Being ill
explanations.body: Боле́ть has two meanings. With the instrumental it means to be sick with an illness. With the body part as the subject it means to hurt.

rows: be sick with / get sick with

examples.translation: He came down with the flu.
We called an ambulance.
She got tired of the noise.

explanations.title: How are you feeling?
explanations.body: Чу́вствовать себя́ means to feel. Ask and answer with these phrases.

examples.translation: How are you feeling?
Thank you, I'm better already.

exercises.promptTranslation: He came down with the flu.
How are you feeling?

lessons.title: 216. In restaurants, about friends: the prepositional plural of nouns
lessons.subtitle: Мы ужинаем в рестора́нах и говори́м о друзья́х.

explanations.title: -ах or -ях
explanations.body: The prepositional plural is used after в, на, о (об), при. Nouns take -ах after a hard stem and -ях after a soft stem, and the stress stays where it was in the nominative plural.

examples.translation: We have dinner in restaurants.
We talk about problems.
In class we often read.

explanations.title: Special nouns
explanations.body: The same irregular plurals appear here. Watch for матеря́х and деревня́х, whose stress moves to the ending.

examples.translation: He often thinks about his friends.
Mom often talks about the children.

examples.text: Мы бы́ли в гостя́х у друзе́й.
examples.translation: We were visiting friends.

exercises.promptTranslation: We have dinner in restaurants.
She is reading about museums.
We talk about problems.
He often thinks about his friends.
Mom often talks about the children.
She works in hospitals.
We live in villages.
We were visiting friends.

exercises.prompt: Which ending do hard-stem nouns take in the prepositional plural?
Which ending do soft-stem nouns take in the prepositional plural?

lessons.title: 217. In big cities, about our friends: adjectives in the prepositional plural
lessons.subtitle: Мы ча́сто говори́м о на́ших ста́рых друзья́х.

explanations.title: -ых or -их
explanations.body: Adjectives, ordinal numbers and adjectival pronouns end in -ых after a hard stem and in -их after a soft stem or after к, г, х, ж, ч, ш, щ. This is the same ending as the genitive plural, and the same for all genders.

examples.translation: There are many people in big cities.
We are talking about our friends.
He thinks about all the problems.

explanations.title: Do not change: его, её, их
explanations.body: The possessives его́, её and их are indeclinable, so they stay the same in every case.

examples.translation: We are talking about their children.
I am thinking about his problems.

examples.text: Он ча́сто вспомина́ет о тех днях.
examples.translation: He often remembers those days.

exercises.explanation: After ш/щ/ж/ч/к/г/х: -их; here the stem is big-: больши́х.
exercises.promptTranslation: There are many people in big cities.
We are talking about our friends.

She works in Russian hospitals.
