exercises.prompt: Which ending do adjectives take after ш in the prepositional plural?
What happens to его́, её and их in the prepositional plural?

lessons.title: 218. She is young and beautiful: short-form adjectives
lessons.subtitle: Э́та же́нщина молода́ и краси́ва.

explanations.title: How the short form is built
explanations.body: Remove the ending of the full form. The masculine has no ending; the feminine adds -а; the neuter -о; the plural -ы (or -и after к, г, х, ж, ч, ш, щ).

examples.translation: This woman is young and beautiful.
These people are rich.
My brother is happy.

explanations.title: They are predicates only
explanations.body: A short adjective is never used in front of a noun. It stays at the end of the clause as part of the predicate. In the present tense there is no verb «быть», and the adjective agrees with the subject in gender and number.

examples.translation: This window is beautiful.
My mother is very clever.
You are right, Vanya.
We are very glad to see you.

exercises.promptTranslation: Anna is young and beautiful.
These people are happy.
He is very rich.
We are very glad to see you.
You are right, Vanya!
This window is beautiful.
My mother is very clever.

exercises.prompt: Short-form adjectives are used only as...
exercises.explanation: They stand at the end of the clause.

exercises.prompt: What is the masculine short form of краси́вый?

lessons.title: 219. Busy, sick, too big: fleeting vowels and велик, мал
lessons.subtitle: Я сего́дня за́нят, а ма́ма больна́.

explanations.title: A vowel appears in the masculine
explanations.body: When the stem ends in two consonants, the masculine short form has no ending, so a vowel slips in between them: usually о before к, and е (or ё) before н.

examples.text: Я сего́дня за́нят, а ма́ма больна́.
examples.translation: I am busy today, and Mom is sick.
This medicine is good for you.
Smoking is bad for you.

explanations.title: Too big, too small: вели́к and мал
explanations.body: Большо́й and ма́ленький have no short forms of their own. Instead the short forms of вели́кий and ма́лый are used, and they mean “too big” and “too small” for a particular person.

examples.translation: These shoes are too big for me.
This dress is too small for me.
This jacket is too big for you.

exercises.promptTranslation: I am very busy today.
Mom has been sick for three days.

exercises.prompt: Э́то лека́рство ___ для здоро́вья. (good for you)
exercises.promptTranslation: This medicine is good for your health.
Smoking is harmful.
These shoes are too big for me.
This dress is too small for me.
This jacket is too big for you.
Mom is pleased with my results.

exercises.prompt: What is the masculine short form of у́зкий?

lessons.title: 220. A beautiful girl, so beautiful today: short or full?
lessons.subtitle: Ты так краси́ва в э́том пла́тье!

explanations.title: Full form: a lasting quality; short form: a particular case
explanations.body: The full form describes what something is like in general and can stand in front of a noun. The short form says what a person or thing is like right now, or in a particular situation, and is common after как, так, слишком and о́чень.

rows: Ты так краси́ва в э́том пла́тье!
Он сли́шком мо́лод для э́той рабо́ты.

examples.text: Он сли́шком мо́лод для э́той рабо́ты.
examples.translation: He is too young for this job.
The child is sick, so he is at home.
Are you ready?

explanations.title: Words that have only a short form
explanations.body: A few adjectives exist only in the short form, such as рад (glad), до́лжен (must) and прав (right). Not every adjective has a short form: colors and materials do not, and neither do большо́й or ма́ленький.

examples.translation: I am glad to see you.
You are absolutely right.
He must call his mother.

exercises.promptTranslation: This is a beautiful girl.
You look so beautiful in this dress!
He is too young for this job.
Artur is a healthy person.
Are you ready?
I am glad to see you.
This advice is useful.

exercises.prompt: Which form can stand in front of a noun?
exercises.explanation: Only the full form modifies a noun.

exercises.prompt: Which adjective has only a short form?
exercises.explanation: Рад exists only as a short form.

lessons.title: 221. I feel sick, I have chills: impersonal verbs of the body
lessons.subtitle: Меня́ тошни́т, и меня́ зноби́т.

explanations.title: The person is the object, not the subject
explanations.body: Some verbs describe how the body feels without any subject. The verb is in the third person singular (neuter in the past tense), and the person who feels it is in the accusative or dative.

examples.translation: I feel nauseous.
I am not feeling well.
Masha feels sleepy.

explanations.title: Starting suddenly: за-
explanations.body: The prefix за- shows that the feeling has just begun: зазноби́ть, затошни́ть.

examples.translation: Vera started feeling nauseous on the bus.
Suddenly I started shivering.
He had chills all night.

exercises.promptTranslation: I feel nauseous.
Yesterday she felt nauseous all day.

exercises.prompt: Вдруг Ве́ру ___ в авто́бусе. (started feeling nauseous)
exercises.promptTranslation: Suddenly Vera felt nauseous on the bus.
He had chills all night.
I am not feeling well.
Masha feels like sleeping.

exercises.prompt: In «Меня́ тошни́т» the person who feels sick is in the...
What does the past tense of an impersonal verb end in?

lessons.title: 222. It got dark, it got colder: impersonal verbs of nature and forces
lessons.subtitle: Зимо́й о́чень ра́но темне́ет.

explanations.title: Nature acts on its own
explanations.body: Weather and the time of day are expressed with impersonal verbs: no subject, a verb in the third person singular or neuter past.

rows: it gets dark, it got dark
it is getting colder, it got colder

examples.translation: In winter it gets dark very early.
It got colder outside.
Suddenly it grew dark.

explanations.title: Outside forces
explanations.body: When something is done to a thing by a force that we do not name, Russian also uses an impersonal verb. The affected thing is in the accusative, and the force is in the instrumental.

rows: The road was covered with snow.
The window was blown open by the wind.

examples.translation: The basement was flooded by the rain.
The road was buried in snow.

explanations.title: Not enough: не хвата́ет
explanations.body: Хвата́ть with a negative means “to be short of”: the thing that is lacking is in the genitive, and the person who lacks it is in the dative.

examples.translation: I do not have enough time.
We do not have enough money.
There is a shortage of doctors in the hospitals.

exercises.promptTranslation: In winter it gets dark very early.
It got colder outside.
Suddenly it grew dark.
The basement was flooded by the rain.
The road was covered with snow.
We do not have enough money.
I do not have enough time.

exercises.prompt: What case follows не хвата́ет for the thing that is lacking?

lessons.title: 223. Let him call, may you be happy: the particle пусть
lessons.subtitle: Пусть он мне позвони́т. Пусть все бу́дут здоро́вы!

explanations.title: Пусть + subject + verb
explanations.body: Пусть is placed at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the subject and a verb in the present or future tense. It tells a third person to do something, or expresses a wish. The subject is usually he, she, they or a name.

rows: Let the children play in the yard.
Пусть они́ так бо́льше не де́лают.
I don't want them to do that anymore.

examples.translation: Have him call me.
Let the children play in the yard.

explanations.title: Wishes and toasts
explanations.body: Пусть also expresses good wishes in toasts, birthday greetings and holiday cards.

rows: Пусть у вас всегда́ бу́дет мно́го друзе́й!
May you always have many friends!
May all your dreams come true!

examples.translation: May everyone be healthy!
Good luck to you!

examples.text: Пусть у вас всегда́ бу́дет мно́го друзе́й!
examples.translation: May you always have many friends!

exercises.promptTranslation: Have him call me.
Let the children play outside.
May everyone be healthy!
Good luck to you!

exercises.prompt: Пусть у вас ___ бу́дет мно́го друзе́й! (always)
exercises.promptTranslation: May you always have many friends!
Have Liza learn this rule.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means “May all your dreams come true!”?

lessons.title: 224. Review: the plural cases, short adjectives and health
lessons.subtitle: Мы говори́м о больны́х друзья́х, а врачи́ лечат пациентов.

explanations.title: The plural, case by case
explanations.body: You now have every plural case. Learn them as a set. Adjectives and pronouns always follow the noun.

examples.translation: We talk about our new friends.

explanations.title: Health and short adjectives
explanations.body: Remember the key forms: боли́т/боля́т for pain, the instrumental after заболе́ть, and the short forms бо́лен, больна́, больны́ for “is sick”.

examples.text: У меня́ боли́т го́рло, и я не здоро́в.
examples.translation: My throat hurts and I am not well.
May everyone be healthy!

exercises.promptTranslation: We talk about our sick friends.
The doctors treat patients.
She talks with the new doctors.
He works in big hospitals.
These shoes are too big for me.
He is too young for this job.
I felt nauseous on the bus.
In winter it gets dark early.
May everyone be healthy!
His teeth hurt.

exercises.prompt: Which case ending is -ах / -ях for nouns?

units.title: Unit 24: Carrying, leading and driving; самый and же

lessons.title: 225. Carry, lead, drive: носи́ть / нести́, води́ть / вести́, вози́ть / везти́
lessons.subtitle: Ма́ма ведёт ребёнка в шко́лу, а па́па везёт су́мки.

explanations.title: Three more pairs of motion verbs
explanations.body: You already know pairs such as ходи́ть / идти́ (on foot) and е́здить / е́хать (by vehicle). Russian has three more pairs for moving something or someone along with you. Each pair has a habitual or round-trip verb and a one-way verb, just like ходи́ть / идти́. The big difference: these verbs always take a direct object, because you carry, lead or drive somebody or something.

rows: carry; wear (in your hands or on you)
lead, take (a person or animal walking)

examples.translation: He is carrying a bag.
Mom is taking the child to school.

examples.text: Па́па везёт ребёнка в шко́лу на маши́не.
examples.translation: Dad is driving the child to school.

explanations.title: The present tense of носи́ть, нести́
explanations.body: Носи́ть is a regular second-conjugation verb with a consonant change in the я-form (с → ш). Нести́ is first conjugation and has the stress on the ending in я and они, and on ё in the other forms.

examples.text: Я ка́ждый день но́шу с собо́й кни́гу.
examples.translation: I carry a book with me every day.
Where are you taking these boxes?

explanations.title: The present tense of води́ть, вести́, вози́ть, везти́
explanations.body: Води́ть and вози́ть change д → ж and з → ж in the я-form (вожу́ for both!). Вести́ and везти́ are first conjugation and look like нести́.

examples.translation: I take my son to school.
They are taking the dog for a walk.

explanations.title: Walking or driving?
explanations.body: Води́ть / вести́ mean taking someone along on foot, so the object must be able to walk by itself: a child, a dog, a guest. You cannot ‘lead’ a table. Носи́ть / нести́ and вози́ть / везти́ work with any object, living or not.

examples.translation: Lida is walking the dog.
A truck is transporting fruit.

exercises.prompt: Ка́ждый день ма́ма ___ ребёнка в шко́лу пешко́м. (leads)
exercises.explanation: Every day, on foot, a child: води́ть.
exercises.promptTranslation: Every day Mom walks the child to school.

exercises.prompt: Ка́ждое у́тро па́па ___ ребёнка в шко́лу на маши́не. (drives)
exercises.promptTranslation: Every morning Dad drives the child to school.
She always carries a book in her bag.

exercises.explanation: Now, one way, in my hands: нести́.
exercises.promptTranslation: I am carrying the bag home now.

exercises.prompt: Вы ка́ждую суббо́ту ___ дете́й в парк? (take)
exercises.explanation: Every Saturday: habitual. On foot: води́ть.
exercises.promptTranslation: Do you take the children to the park every Saturday?
Look, Lida is walking the dog.

exercises.explanation: A truck, one way, now: везти́.
exercises.promptTranslation: The truck is taking fruit to the shop.

exercises.prompt: Which verb means to transport something by vehicle, as a habit?
What do all of these verbs need?
exercises.explanation: You carry, lead or drive somebody or something.

lessons.title: 226. Every day or right now: past and future of carrying and leading
lessons.subtitle: Когда́ мы встре́тили сосе́да, он вёл соба́ку.

explanations.title: Habit, round trip, or on the way
explanations.body: The rules are the same as for ходи́ть / идти́. The habitual verb covers a habit and a round trip. The one-way verb covers a movement in progress, a single trip in one direction.

examples.text: Вчера́ я носи́л су́мку в ремо́нт, и она́ уже́ до́ма.
examples.translation: Yesterday I took the bag to be repaired, and it is already back.

examples.text: Когда́ мы встре́тили сосе́да, он вёл соба́ку.
examples.translation: When we met our neighbor, he was walking his dog.

explanations.title: Past tense of the one-way verbs
explanations.body: The masculine past of нести́ and везти́ has no -л: нёс, вёз. Вести́ keeps it: вёл. The feminine, neuter and plural forms are regular, with the stress on the ending: несла́, вела́, везли́.

examples.translation: She was carrying a heavy bag.
They were leading the children by the hand.

explanations.title: Past tense of the habitual verbs
explanations.body: Носи́ть, води́ть and вози́ть form the past tense like any regular verb: -л, -ла, -ло, -ли. In the past they often mean a round trip: ‘took there and came back’.

examples.text: Ле́том па́па вози́л нас на мо́ре.
examples.translation: In summer Dad used to take us to the sea.
Grandma used to take me to the theater.

exercises.promptTranslation: She was carrying a heavy bag.
He was leading the dog down the street.
The truck was transporting fruit.
They were leading the children by the hand.

exercises.prompt: Ле́том па́па ___ нас на мо́ре. (used to drive)
exercises.explanation: A repeated trip each summer: вози́л.
exercises.promptTranslation: In summer Dad used to take us to the sea.

exercises.prompt: Ба́бушка ча́сто ___ меня́ в теа́тр. (used to take)
exercises.promptTranslation: Grandma often took me to the theater.

exercises.prompt: Вчера́ я ___ су́мку в ремо́нт, и она́ уже́ до́ма. (took there and back)
exercises.promptTranslation: Yesterday I took the bag in for repair and it is already home.

exercises.prompt: What is the feminine past of нести́?
In the past, ‘He was driving the children to the dacha (at that moment)’ is:
exercises.explanation: A trip in progress, by vehicle: вёз.

lessons.title: 227. Set off, or for a while: понести́, повезти́, поводи́ть
lessons.subtitle: Ко́ля сейча́с повёз бра́та на вокза́л.

explanations.title: Unprefixed verbs are all imperfective
explanations.body: Like ходи́ть and идти́, every one of these verbs is imperfective. If you need a perfective verb without a precise direction, add по-.

examples.text: Я немно́го поноси́л э́ту ша́пку и снял её.
examples.translation: I wore this hat for a little while and took it off.

explanations.title: По- + habitual verb: for a little while
explanations.body: The perfective of носи́ть, води́ть, вози́ть means doing the action for a short time, usually going around with someone.

examples.text: Он поводи́л госте́й по го́роду и показа́л им па́мятники.
examples.translation: He took the guests around town for a while and showed them the monuments.
Dad drove us around the city for a while.

explanations.title: По- + one-way verb: set off
explanations.body: The perfective of нести́, вести́, везти́ stresses the start of the movement: ‘picked up and set off’. The past masculine is понёс, повёл, повёз. The future is formed with the personal endings: понесу́, поведу́, повезу́.

examples.text: Ко́ли сейча́с нет до́ма. Он повёз бра́та на вокза́л.
examples.translation: Kolya is not home now. He has taken his brother to the station.
I will carry the bag.

examples.text: Де́вочка взяла́ зо́нтик и понесла́ его́ ба́бушке.
examples.translation: The girl took the umbrella and set off to bring it to her grandmother.

exercises.prompt: Он ___ гостей по городу и показал им памятники. (took around for a while)
exercises.promptTranslation: He took the guests around town for a while.

exercises.prompt: Ко́ли нет до́ма. Он ___ бра́та на вокза́л. (has set off with)
exercises.explanation: A start of a trip by vehicle: повёз.
exercises.promptTranslation: Kolya has taken his brother to the station.

exercises.prompt: Я ___ су́мку, а ты откро́й дверь. (will carry)
exercises.promptTranslation: I will carry the bag; you open the door.

exercises.prompt: Па́па ___ нас по го́роду. (drove around for a while)
exercises.promptTranslation: Dad drove us around town for a while.

exercises.prompt: Де́вочка взяла́ зо́нтик и ___ его́ ба́бушке. (set off carrying)
exercises.promptTranslation: The girl took the umbrella and set off to bring it to Grandma.

exercises.prompt: Which prefix makes a perfective verb here?
exercises.explanation: По- gives a perfective with no direction.

lessons.title: 228. Behave, drive a car, wear glasses: set expressions
lessons.subtitle: Де́ти хорошо́ себя́ веду́т.

explanations.title: Вести́ себя́: to behave
explanations.body: Вести́ себя́ means to behave. It takes an adverb: хорошо́, пло́хо, споко́йно.

examples.translation: The children are behaving well.

examples.text: Почему́ ты так пло́хо себя́ ведёшь?
examples.translation: Why are you behaving so badly?
Yesterday she behaved calmly.

explanations.title: Other fixed expressions
explanations.body: These verbs appear in many fixed phrases. Learn each one as a unit.

examples.translation: She drives well.
My grandfather wears glasses.

examples.text: Я веду́ дневни́к уже́ пять лет.
examples.translation: I have been keeping a diary for five years.
Parents are responsible for their children.

explanations.title: Note: no ‘drive’ verb for the passenger
explanations.body: Води́ть маши́ну is what the driver does. For a passenger the verb is е́хать (or е́здить): Я е́ду на маши́не. Do not say вожу́ when you are only a passenger.

examples.text: Я не вожу́ маши́ну, я е́зжу на авто́бусе.
examples.translation: I don't drive; I go by bus.

exercises.promptTranslation: The children are behaving well.
Why are you behaving so badly?

exercises.explanation: To drive a car: води́ть маши́ну.
exercises.promptTranslation: She drives well.
My grandfather wears glasses.
I have been keeping a diary for five years.
Parents are responsible for their children.

exercises.prompt: Я не вожу́ маши́ну, я ___ на авто́бусе. (ride)
exercises.promptTranslation: I don't drive; I ride the bus.

exercises.prompt: How do you say ‘to behave well’?

lessons.title: 229. Bags, suitcases, keys: what we carry
lessons.subtitle: Он несёт два пакета и тяжёлый чемода́н.

explanations.title: Things we carry
explanations.body: A short vocabulary of everyday objects that go with нести́ and носи́ть.

examples.text: Он несёт два паке́та и тяжёлый чемода́н.
examples.translation: He is carrying two bags and a heavy suitcase.

examples.text: Я всегда́ но́шу ключи́ в карма́не.
examples.translation: I always keep my keys in my pocket.

explanations.title: Heavy, light, full
explanations.body: To describe what you carry, use these adjectives.

examples.translation: I have a light backpack.
This box is very heavy.

explanations.title: Counting what you carry
explanations.body: After 2, 3, 4 use the genitive singular: два чемода́на, три су́мки. After 5 and more, use the genitive plural: пять паке́тов.

examples.translation: She is carrying three bags.
We have five suitcases.

exercises.prompt: Он несёт два ___ и тяжёлый чемода́н. (bags)
exercises.promptTranslation: He is carrying two bags and a heavy suitcase.
She is carrying three bags.
We have five suitcases.

exercises.explanation: Accusative plural of an inanimate noun = nominative.
exercises.promptTranslation: I always keep my keys in my pocket.
This box is very heavy.
I have a light backpack.

lessons.title: 230. Games and winning: игра́, вы́играть, проигра́ть, ве́сти в счёте
lessons.subtitle: На́ша кома́нда вы́играла матч со счётом два—оди́н.

explanations.title: Playing, winning and losing
explanations.body: Игра́ is a game. The verb for taking part is игра́ть. The result of a game is expressed by two perfective verbs: вы́играть (to win) and проигра́ть (to lose). Both take a direct object: вы́играть матч, проигра́ть игру́.

examples.translation: We won the match.
Our rival lost.
Who won?

explanations.title: The score: со счётом
explanations.body: To say the score of a game, use со счётом + the numbers. A dash or двоеточие is read as ‘to’: два оди́н means 2:1.

examples.text: На́ша кома́нда вы́играла матч со счётом три—оди́н.
examples.translation: Our team won the match 3–1.
What is the score?

explanations.title: Вести́ в счёте: to lead
explanations.body: Вести́ also means to be ahead in a game. The usual phrase is вести́ в счёте.

examples.translation: Our side is leading.

examples.text: Они́ вели́ в счёте до са́мого конца́.
examples.translation: They were ahead until the very end.

explanations.title: Online games
explanations.body: Players and teams can be anywhere; these words are the same for a video game.

examples.translation: He plays online with a friend.
That was our first victory.

exercises.promptTranslation: We won the match.
Our rival lost.

exercises.prompt: На́ша кома́нда вы́играла матч ___ счётом три—оди́н. (with)
exercises.explanation: Со счётом, because счёт begins with a consonant cluster.
exercises.promptTranslation: Our team won the match 3–1.
Our side is leading.
What is the score?
That was our first victory.
Who won?

exercises.prompt: Which verb means ‘to lose a game’?

lessons.title: 231. Right at the start, in the very center: са́мый as ‘very’
lessons.subtitle: С са́мого утра́ идёт дождь.

explanations.title: Two jobs of са́мый
explanations.body: You know са́мый from the superlative: са́мый большо́й го́род = the biggest city. Russian also uses са́мый to point to the exact extreme of a place or a time. English says ‘very’ or ‘right’: in the very center, right at the start.

examples.translation: This is the most interesting book.

examples.text: Фонта́н стои́т в са́мом це́нтре пло́щади.
examples.translation: The fountain stands in the very center of the square.

explanations.title: Fixed phrases
explanations.body: In this meaning са́мый agrees with the noun in case, number and gender. The noun is usually a place or a point in time.

examples.text: Мы бы́ли там с са́мого нача́ла.
examples.translation: We were there from the very beginning.

examples.text: Дом стои́т на са́мом берегу́ реки́.
examples.translation: The house stands right on the riverbank.

examples.text: Мы дошли́ до са́мого конца́ у́лицы.
examples.translation: We walked right to the end of the street.

explanations.title: The endings
explanations.body: Са́мый is a regular hard adjective, so you already know its endings.

examples.text: У са́мой две́ри стои́т ма́ленький стол.
examples.translation: A little table stands right by the door.

exercises.prompt: Ресторан стои́т на ___ берегу́ реки́. (right on)
exercises.promptTranslation: The restaurant is right on the riverbank.

exercises.prompt: Мы дошли́ до ___ конца́ у́лицы. (right to)
exercises.promptTranslation: We walked right to the end of the street.
It has been raining since early morning.

exercises.prompt: Фонта́н стои́т в ___ це́нтре пло́щади. (in the very)
exercises.promptTranslation: The fountain is in the very center of the square.

exercises.prompt: Магази́н нахо́дится в ___ конце́ коридо́ра. (at the very)
exercises.promptTranslation: The shop is at the very end of the corridor.

exercises.prompt: У ___ две́ри стои́т ма́ленький стол. (right by)
exercises.promptTranslation: A little table stands right by the door.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses са́мый as ‘the very’ (not a superlative)?
options: Мы жи́ли на са́мом берегу́ мо́ря.
exercises.explanation: Right on the shore: са́мом берегу́.

lessons.title: 232. The same one: тот же, то же са́мое, там же
lessons.subtitle: У нас те же проблемы, и я смотрю́ то же са́мое.

explanations.title: Тот же
explanations.body: Же after тот means ‘the same’. Тот declines as usual, and же does not change: тот же, та же, то же, те же. The word са́мый can follow for emphasis: тот же са́мый.

examples.text: Он живёт в том же до́ме.
examples.translation: He lives in the same house.
We have the same problems.
This is the very same book.

explanations.title: Same thing, same time, same place
explanations.body: То же (са́мое) means ‘the same thing’. Же also joins a place or time word to mean ‘the same’: там же, туда́ же, тогда́ же. And в то же вре́мя means ‘at the same time’.

examples.translation: I want the same thing.

examples.text: Они́ пришли́ в то же вре́мя.
examples.translation: They arrived at the same time.

examples.text: Мы встре́тились там же, где и вчера́.
examples.translation: We met in the same place as yesterday.

explanations.title: Такой же ... как
explanations.body: Такой же means ‘just such’, similar rather than identical. The comparison is introduced by как.

examples.text: У него́ така́я же маши́на, как у меня́.
examples.translation: He has the same kind of car as mine.
They wear identical hats.

exercises.prompt: Он живёт в ___ же до́ме. (the same)
exercises.promptTranslation: He lives in the same house.
We have the same problems.

exercises.prompt: Я хочу́ то же ___. (the very same thing)
exercises.promptTranslation: I want the very same thing.

exercises.prompt: Они́ пришли́ в ___ же вре́мя. (the same)
exercises.promptTranslation: They arrived at the same time.

exercises.prompt: Мы встре́тились ___ же, где и вчера́. (in the same place)
exercises.explanation: Там же = in the same place.
exercises.promptTranslation: We met in the same place as yesterday.

exercises.prompt: У него́ ___ же маши́на, как у меня́. (the same kind of)
exercises.promptTranslation: He has the same kind of car as mine.

lessons.title: 233. But I told you! After all, who is it? The particle же
lessons.subtitle: Я же тебе́ говори́л!

explanations.title: A particle that adds feeling
explanations.body: Particles are small words that colour a sentence. They are not translated word for word. Же is the most common. It sits after the word it emphasizes, often right after the verb or the pronoun.

examples.translation: But you know!
But I told you!

explanations.title: Emphasis: after all, but
explanations.body: The speaker reminds the listener of something that should be obvious, often with a hint of irritation. Ведь does almost the same thing and is often interchangeable.

examples.text: Вы же врач, вы должны́ знать.
examples.translation: But you're a doctor, you ought to know.

explanations.title: Question words + же
explanations.body: After a question word же adds impatience or surprise: ‘so what exactly...?’

rows: What on earth are you doing?

examples.translation: What on earth are you doing?
So who was it?

explanations.title: Именно and даже
explanations.body: Two related words that point to one thing out of many: и́менно (exactly, precisely) and да́же (even).

examples.text: Э́то и́менно то, что мне ну́жно.
examples.translation: This is exactly what I need.
Even a child knows this.

exercises.promptTranslation: But you know!
What on earth are you doing?
Even a child knows this.
This is exactly what I need.

exercises.prompt: Вы ___ врач, вы должны́ знать. (after all)
exercises.promptTranslation: But you're a doctor, you ought to know.
But this is impossible!

exercises.prompt: Which word is nearly the same as же in ‘Ты же зна́ешь’?
What does Что же ты де́лаешь? express?

lessons.title: 234. Review: carrying, driving, the very, the same, же
lessons.subtitle: Ма́ма ведёт дете́й в шко́лу, а па́па везёт су́мки.

explanations.title: What you now know
explanations.body: Six verbs: носи́ть / нести́ (carry; wear), води́ть / вести́ (lead on foot), вози́ть / везти́ (transport). They take an object. The habitual verb covers habit and round trip; the one-way verb covers ‘on the way’. Add по- for a perfective. Са́мый means ‘very’ before a place or time. Тот же = the same. Же adds emphasis.

examples.text: Ма́ма ведёт дете́й в шко́лу, а па́па везёт су́мки.
examples.translation: Mom is taking the children to school, and Dad is driving the bags.

exercises.prompt: Ка́ждый день ма́ма ___ ребёнка в шко́лу. (walks)
exercises.promptTranslation: Every day Mom walks the child to school.

exercises.prompt: Сейча́с она́ ___ ребёнка в шко́лу. (is walking)
exercises.promptTranslation: She is walking the child to school now.

exercises.prompt: Вчера́ па́па ___ нас на да́чу на маши́не. (was driving)
exercises.explanation: A trip in progress by car: вёз.
exercises.promptTranslation: Yesterday Dad was driving us to the dacha.
She wears glasses.
The children behave well.

exercises.prompt: Мы бы́ли там с ___ нача́ла. (the very)
exercises.promptTranslation: We were there from the very beginning.

exercises.prompt: Он живёт в ___ же до́ме. (the same)
exercises.promptTranslation: He lives in the same house.
But you know!

exercises.prompt: Which pair means ‘to drive / to transport’?
Which verb takes only animate objects when you walk?
exercises.explanation: You lead a person or an animal.

units.title: Unit 25: Prefixed carrying verbs, чтобы, -то and -нибудь

lessons.title: 235. Bring and take away: приноси́ть, приводи́ть, привози́ть and у-
lessons.subtitle: Па́па привёз нам пода́рки из Москвы́.

explanations.title: Prefix + motion verb = one aspect pair
explanations.body: Just as ходи́ть / идти́ become приходи́ть / прийти́, the verbs of carrying and leading combine with directional prefixes. The rule is the same as before: prefix + habitual verb gives the imperfective, prefix + one-way verb gives the perfective. No spelling changes happen; only the stress moves.

rows: to bring (leading a person on foot)

examples.translation: The waiter brought us soup.

examples.text: Па́па привёз нам пода́рки из Москвы́.
examples.translation: Dad brought us presents from Moscow.
I brought a friend to the party.

explanations.title: Forms
explanations.body: The perfective forms are built on the one-way stem. The я-form of приводи́ть and привози́ть is the same: привожу́.

examples.translation: Please bring me some water.

examples.text: Ка́ждое ле́то он приво́зит нам фру́кты.
examples.translation: Every summer he brings us fruit.

explanations.title: Taking away
explanations.body: The prefix у- is the opposite of при-: you carry, lead or drive somebody or something away from the place. Use из, с or от for ‘from where’ and в, на or к for ‘to where’.

examples.translation: They took the furniture away to the dacha.
Mom took the child home.
The waiter took the plates away.

exercises.explanation: A waiter carries a dish: принёс.
exercises.promptTranslation: The waiter brought us soup.

exercises.prompt: Па́па ___ нам пода́рки из Москвы́. (brought, by plane)
exercises.explanation: Gifts from a distant city came by vehicle: привёз.
exercises.promptTranslation: Dad brought us presents from Moscow.

exercises.prompt: Я ___ дру́га на вечери́нку. (brought, walking with him)
exercises.explanation: A person you walk with: привёл.
exercises.promptTranslation: I brought a friend to the party.
Mom took the child home.

exercises.prompt: Они́ ___ ме́бель на да́чу на грузовике́. (took away)
exercises.promptTranslation: They took the furniture to the dacha on a truck.

exercises.explanation: Принести́ a part of a substance: genitive.
exercises.promptTranslation: Please bring me some water.

exercises.prompt: Ка́ждое ле́то он ___ нам фру́кты. (brings, by car)
exercises.promptTranslation: Every summer he brings us fruit.

exercises.prompt: Which verb means ‘to bring a person on foot’?
What does the prefix у- add?
exercises.explanation: У- = away from the speaker or the place.

lessons.title: 236. In and out: внести́, вы́нести, ввести́, вы́вести
lessons.subtitle: Вы́неси му́сор, пожа́луйста.

explanations.title: В- and вы-
explanations.body: The prefix в- means ‘into’ and вы- means ‘out of’. They combine with the carrying and leading verbs just like при- and у-. Remember the one special rule: вы- is always stressed in the perfective.

rows: to lead out, to walk (an animal)
to export; to take out (by vehicle)

examples.translation: Carry the suitcase into the house.
Take out the trash, please.
I will take the dog for a walk.

explanations.title: Where is the stress?
explanations.body: Compare the imperfective, with the stress on the ending, and the perfective, with the stress on вы-.

examples.translation: Every evening he takes out the trash.

examples.text: Вчера́ мы вы́несли ста́рые кре́сла на у́лицу.
examples.translation: Yesterday we carried the old armchairs out to the street.

explanations.title: Prepositions
explanations.body: To say what you carry in, use в or на + accusative. To say what you carry out of, use из or с + genitive.

examples.translation: They carried the sofa into the apartment.
He led the child out of the room.

exercises.promptTranslation: Carry the suitcase into the house.

exercises.explanation: Вы- = out; imperative of the perfective.
exercises.promptTranslation: Take out the trash, please.

exercises.prompt: Я ___ соба́ку на прогу́лку. (will take out)
exercises.promptTranslation: I will take the dog for a walk.
They carried the sofa into the apartment.

exercises.prompt: Вчера́ мы ___ ста́рые кре́сла на у́лицу. (carried out)
exercises.promptTranslation: Yesterday we carried the old armchairs out to the street.
Every evening he takes out the trash.

exercises.prompt: Where is the stress in the perfective with вы-?
What is the masculine past of вы́нести?

lessons.title: 237. Across, back, a lift: перевести́, отнести́, отвезти́, подвезти́
lessons.subtitle: Я переведу́ ребёнка че́рез доро́гу.

explanations.title: More prefixes
explanations.body: These prefixes behave as they do with other motion verbs.

rows: to take (to a place, to someone)
to drive someone to a destination
to drop off on the way

examples.translation: I will take the child across the road.
Take this plate to the kitchen.

examples.text: За́втра мне ну́жно отвезти́ роди́телей в аэропо́рт.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I must drive my parents to the airport.

explanations.title: От- and за-
explanations.body: От- often means returning something to its place or taking someone to a specific destination. За- means dropping somebody off on your way: Заведи́ сестру́ в де́тский сад.

examples.text: Заведи́ сестру́ в де́тский сад по доро́ге в шко́лу.
examples.translation: Drop your sister at kindergarten on the way to school.

examples.text: Вчера́ па́па подвёз меня́ на рабо́ту.
examples.translation: Yesterday Dad gave me a lift to work.

explanations.title: Parents and children
explanations.body: Many situations have a typical verb:

rows: leading a child across a busy road
taking a plate to the kitchen
driving a guest to the airport
bringing a delivery to a client

examples.translation: The courier delivered the package to the office.

exercises.prompt: Я ___ ребёнка че́рез доро́гу. (will take across)
exercises.promptTranslation: I will take the child across the road.
Take this plate to the kitchen.

exercises.prompt: За́втра мне ну́жно ___ роди́телей в аэропо́рт. (to drive)
exercises.explanation: От- + везти́ = drive to a destination.
exercises.promptTranslation: Tomorrow I must drive my parents to the airport.

exercises.prompt: Вчера́ па́па ___ меня́ на рабо́ту. (gave a lift)
exercises.promptTranslation: Yesterday Dad gave me a lift to work.

exercises.prompt: ___ сестру́ в де́тский сад по доро́ге в шко́лу. (drop off!)
exercises.promptTranslation: Drop your sister at kindergarten on the way to school.
The courier delivered the package to the office.

exercises.prompt: Which verb fits ‘take a child across the street’?

exercises.explanation: Под-: pick up on the way.

exercises.prompt: What does the prefix от- often show?
options: returning to its place; to a destination

lessons.title: 238. Give an example, spend time, postpone: figurative uses
lessons.subtitle: Мы провели́ выходны́е на да́че.

explanations.title: The prefixes take on new meanings
explanations.body: Like перевести́ статью́ (to translate an article), many prefixed carrying and leading verbs have abstract meanings. Learn them as fixed phrases.

examples.translation: Give an example, please.
We spent the weekend at the dacha.

explanations.title: Postponing and introducing
explanations.body: Перенести́ means to move to a different time. The new time follows на + accusative: перенести́ встре́чу на за́втра.

examples.translation: They postponed the meeting until tomorrow.
A new rule was introduced at school.

explanations.title: Pets and cars
explanations.body: Завести́ has two everyday meanings. With an animal it means ‘to get one’. With a car or an engine it means ‘to start’.

examples.translation: We got a dog.
I cannot start the car.

exercises.promptTranslation: Give an example, please.
We spent the weekend at the dacha.
They postponed the meeting until tomorrow.
A new rule was introduced at the school.
We got a dog.

exercises.prompt: Он ___ текст с англи́йского на ру́сский. (translated)
exercises.promptTranslation: He translated the text from English into Russian.

exercises.explanation: Пере- = to move across to another time.

lessons.title: 239. I want you to come: хочу́, что́бы ты пришёл
lessons.subtitle: Я хочу́, что́бы ты пришёл ко мне.

explanations.title: Same subject: infinitive
explanations.body: When the person who wants and the person who acts are the same, Russian uses an infinitive, just like English: I want to go.

examples.translation: I want to go to the cinema.

explanations.title: Different subject: что́бы + past tense
explanations.body: When someone wants another person to act, the second verb goes into the past tense after что́бы. The past tense here does not point to the past. It only shows a wish: the time is decided by the context. The conjunction что́бы is not translated: ‘I want you to come’.

examples.text: Я хочу́, что́бы ты пришёл ко мне.
examples.translation: I want you to come to see me.

examples.text: Ма́ма хо́чет, что́бы мы позвони́ли ба́бушке.
examples.translation: Mom wants us to call Grandma.

explanations.title: The verb agrees with the subject
explanations.body: The past-tense verb after что́бы agrees with its own subject in gender and number.

examples.text: Она́ не хо́чет, что́бы мы уходи́ли.
examples.translation: She does not want us to leave.

exercises.promptTranslation: I want to go home.

exercises.prompt: Я хочу́, что́бы ты ___ ко мне. (came, m.)
exercises.promptTranslation: I want you to come to me.
Mom wants us to call Grandma.
She does not want us to leave.
I want you to help me.

exercises.prompt: Ма́ма хо́чет ___ ба́бушке. (to call, she herself)
exercises.promptTranslation: Mom wants to call Grandma.

exercises.prompt: Which form follows что́бы when the subject changes?
Does the past tense after что́бы refer to the past?
exercises.explanation: The time comes from the context.

lessons.title: 240. Ask, advise, demand: проси́ть, сове́товать, тре́бовать, приказа́ть
lessons.subtitle: Врач посове́товал, что́бы я отдыха́л.

explanations.title: Verbs that go with что́бы
explanations.body: After verbs of asking, advising, demanding and ordering, what you want someone to do can be expressed with что́бы + past tense. With most of these verbs you can also use an infinitive, as in English.

rows: Ма́ма сказа́ла, что́бы мы шли домо́й.

examples.translation: Mom asked me to buy bread.

examples.text: Ма́ма попроси́ла, что́бы я купи́л хлеб.
examples.translation: Mom asked me to buy bread.

explanations.title: Cases after these verbs
explanations.body: Проси́ть takes the accusative of the person: проси́ть кого́. Сове́товать and приказа́ть take the dative: сове́товать кому́, приказа́ть кому́. Тре́бовать takes что́бы or от + genitive.

examples.translation: The doctor advised me to rest.
The teacher demanded silence from the students.

explanations.title: Suggest: предлага́ть
explanations.body: Предлага́ть takes a dative person and an infinitive: Я предлага́ю тебе́ пойти́. With что́бы it works like проси́ть: Я предлага́ю, что́бы мы пошли́.

examples.translation: I suggest going to the park.

examples.text: Она́ предложи́ла, что́бы мы пошли́ в кино́.
examples.translation: She suggested that we go to the cinema.

exercises.promptTranslation: Mom asked me to buy bread.
The doctor advised me to rest.
He ordered us to leave.
I demand that you be quiet.
The doctor advised me to rest.
Mom asked me to buy bread.

exercises.prompt: Ма́ма сказа́ла, ___ мы шли домо́й. (so that: a command)
exercises.promptTranslation: Mom said that we should go home.

exercises.prompt: Which verb takes the dative of the person?
Which verb takes the accusative of the person?

lessons.title: 241. In order to: что́бы for purpose
lessons.subtitle: Я иду́ в магази́н, что́бы купи́ть хлеб.

explanations.title: Why? In order to...
explanations.body: Что́бы also answers the question Заче́м? (what for?). When the subject of both parts is the same, it is followed by the infinitive, exactly like English ‘in order to’.

examples.text: Я иду́ в магази́н, что́бы купи́ть хлеб.
examples.translation: I am going to the store to buy bread.

examples.text: Мы вста́ли ра́но, что́бы успе́ть на по́езд.
examples.translation: We got up early to catch the train.

explanations.title: A different subject: past tense
explanations.body: When the second part has its own subject, the verb is in the past tense, as after verbs of wanting.

examples.text: Я оста́влю запи́ску, что́бы он знал.
examples.translation: I will leave a note so that he knows.
Speak loudly so that everyone can hear.

explanations.title: Purpose at the start
explanations.body: The что́бы part may come first. In formal Russian you may also hear для того́ что́бы, which means the same.

examples.text: Что́бы хорошо́ говори́ть по-ру́сски, на́до мно́го чита́ть.
examples.translation: To speak Russian well, you have to read a lot.

examples.text: Для того́ что́бы успе́ть на по́езд, мы взя́ли такси́.
examples.translation: To catch the train we took a taxi.

exercises.prompt: Я иду́ в магази́н, что́бы ___ хлеб. (buy)
exercises.promptTranslation: I am going to the store to buy bread.

exercises.prompt: Мы вста́ли ра́но, что́бы ___ на по́езд. (catch)
exercises.promptTranslation: We got up early to catch the train.

exercises.prompt: Я оста́влю запи́ску, что́бы он ___. (would know)
exercises.explanation: Different subject: что́бы + past; он is masculine.
exercises.promptTranslation: I will leave a note so that he knows.
Speak loudly so that everyone can hear.
We went to the park to take a walk.

exercises.prompt: ___ хорошо́ говори́ть по-ру́сски, на́до мно́го чита́ть. (to)
exercises.explanation: Что́бы at the start of a purpose clause.
exercises.promptTranslation: To speak Russian well, you have to read a lot.

exercises.prompt: What follows что́бы when the subject stays the same?

lessons.title: 242. Someone, something, somewhere: кто́-то, что́-то, где́-то
lessons.subtitle: Кто́-то звони́л, но я не зна́ю кто.

explanations.title: The particle -то
explanations.body: Add -то to a question word and you get ‘some...’: someone, something, somewhere. The particle -то is used when you know that the person, thing or place exists, but you cannot or do not want to say which. The particle itself never changes.

examples.text: Кто́-то звони́л, но я не зна́ю кто.
examples.translation: Someone called, but I don't know who.
He went off somewhere.
For some reason she is not answering.

explanations.title: Something happened, but details are missing
explanations.body: With -то the action or the object is real. You just cannot give more details: perhaps you forgot, perhaps you do not know, perhaps it does not matter.

examples.translation: I have seen this person somewhere.
Once there was a park here.
Something is lying in the room.

explanations.title: Spelling
explanations.body: Always use a hyphen: кто-то, где-то, куда-то. Where the question word has a stress, it stays the same: кто́-то, что́-то, куда́-то. Note that ка́к-то has the stress on the first word.

examples.translation: Some man is waiting for you.

exercises.prompt: ___ звони́л, но я не зна́ю кто. (someone)
exercises.promptTranslation: Someone called, but I don't know who.
He went off somewhere.
I have seen this person somewhere.
For some reason she is not answering.
Once there was a park here.
Something is lying in the room.

options: it exists, but details are unknown

exercises.prompt: Which spelling is right for ‘to somewhere’?

lessons.title: 243. Anyone, anything, ever: кто́-нибудь, что́-нибудь, когда́-нибудь
lessons.subtitle: Ты когда́-нибудь был в Росси́и?

explanations.title: The particle -нибудь
explanations.body: Add -нибудь to a question word when you do not know whether the person, thing or event even exists: anyone, anything, anywhere, ever. It is typical of questions, conditions, requests and the future.

examples.translation: Have you ever been to Russia?
Did anyone call?

explanations.title: -то or -нибудь?
explanations.body: -то: it exists, but you cannot say which. -нибудь: perhaps it exists, perhaps not. Compare a question and its answer.

examples.text: Е́сли кто́-нибудь придёт, скажи́, что меня́ нет.
examples.translation: If anyone comes, say that I am out.
Buy something to eat.
Call me sometime.

explanations.title: Where -нибудь appears
explanations.body: Think of -нибудь as ‘any’. It is natural in these places:

examples.translation: I will go somewhere in the summer.

exercises.promptTranslation: Have you ever been to Russia?
Did anyone call?
Yes, someone called.

exercises.prompt: Е́сли ___ придёт, скажи́, что меня́ нет. (anyone)
exercises.promptTranslation: If anyone comes, say that I am out.
Buy something to eat.
I will go somewhere in the summer.

exercises.prompt: In which sentence is -нибудь used correctly?
options: Вчера́ кто́-нибудь звони́л, но я не зна́ю кто.

exercises.prompt: What does когда́-нибудь often mean in questions?

lessons.title: 244. To someone, with something: the cases of кто́-то and что́-нибудь
lessons.subtitle: Я с кем-то говори́л о чём-то ва́жном.

explanations.title: The question word declines, the particle does not
explanations.body: Put the question word in the case it needs and add the particle at the end. The preposition goes in front of the whole word.

examples.text: Я с ке́м-то говори́л о чём-то ва́жном.
examples.translation: I was speaking with someone about something important.
He called someone.
Does anyone have a pen?

explanations.title: The same with -нибудь
explanations.body: The forms of -нибудь are built in exactly the same way.

examples.text: Ты говори́л об э́том с ке́м-нибудь?
examples.translation: Did you talk about this with anyone?
Do you know anything about him?

explanations.title: Whose? Which?
explanations.body: Како́й declines like an adjective. The particle again stays unchanged.

examples.translation: This letter is from some stranger.

explanations.title: Do not confuse with ни-
explanations.body: Words with ни- mean ‘no one, nothing’ and need не before the verb. Compare:

examples.translation: I did not call anyone.

exercises.prompt: Я с ___ говори́л о чём-то ва́жном. (someone)
exercises.promptTranslation: I was speaking with someone about something important.
He called someone.
Does anyone have a pen?
Did you talk about this with anyone?
I did not call anyone.
I saw no one.

exercises.prompt: Does the particle -то change with the case?
options: no, only the question word does
before the whole word: с кем-то

lessons.title: 245. Review: bring, take, want, in order to, someone
lessons.subtitle: Я хочу́, что́бы ты кому́-нибудь отвёз э́ти кни́ги.

explanations.title: What you now know
explanations.body: Prefixed carrying and leading verbs make an aspect pair (the perfective uses the one-way stem). Вы- is stressed in the perfective. Что́бы + past tense joins a wish, a request or a command to a different subject. Что́бы + infinitive gives a purpose. -То means ‘someone I cannot name’; -нибудь means ‘anyone, if any’.

rows: Я иду́ в магази́н, что́бы купи́ть хлеб.

examples.text: Я хочу́, что́бы ты отвёз э́ти кни́ги кому́-нибудь из друзе́й.
examples.translation: I want you to take these books to one of your friends.

exercises.promptTranslation: Please bring some water.
I want you to come.

exercises.prompt: Я иду́ в магази́н, что́бы ___ хлеб. (buy)
exercises.promptTranslation: I am going to the store to buy bread.

lessons.title: 250. Adjectives made from verbs: what is a participle?
lessons.subtitle: Э́то мой люби́мый писа́тель.

explanations.title: You already know some
explanations.body: Look at these words you have met: люби́мый (favorite), бы́вший (former), закры́тый (closed), за́нятый (busy). They look like adjectives, because they have adjective endings. But each one is built from a verb: люби́мый from люби́ть, бы́вший from быть, закры́тый from закры́ть. Such a word is a participle (прича́стие in Russian; the root is the same as in часть, ‘part’, because it takes part in both a verb and an adjective).

examples.translation: This is my favorite writer.
The former president lives in Moscow.
The door is closed, but the window is open.

explanations.title: Two things a participle shows
explanations.body: A participle says what the action is, and it also tells you two more things. Is the action happening now (present) or was it earlier (past)? Is the noun doing the action (active) or is something being done to the noun (passive)? English has participles too: ‘the stolen money’ is past passive, ‘a fire-breathing dragon’ is present active.

examples.translation: The sleeping child does not hear the noise.

explanations.title: Where do you meet them?
explanations.body: Participles are common in news, books, signs and official language, and less common in everyday speech. In this unit you will learn to recognise them; you do not need to build them yet.

examples.translation: Here is a letter written yesterday.

exercises.prompt: Which verb does люби́мый come from?
Which verb does бы́вший come from?
exercises.explanation: Бы́вший = one who used to be.

exercises.promptTranslation: This is my favorite writer.
The former president lives in Moscow.

options: an adjective formed from a verb
a verb formed from a noun
a short form of a noun
exercises.explanation: It shows an action and a tense.

lessons.title: 251. Four types: present or past, active or passive
lessons.subtitle: Чита́ющий, чита́емый, чита́вший, прочи́танный.

explanations.title: Two questions, four types
explanations.body: Ask two questions about any participle. When did the action happen: now (present) or earlier (past)? Who does the action: the noun itself (active) or somebody else (passive)? The answers give four types.

examples.text: Студе́нт, чита́ющий кни́гу, сиди́т у окна́.
examples.translation: The student who is reading a book is sitting by the window.

examples.text: Кни́га, прочи́танная студе́нтом, лежи́т на столе́.
examples.translation: The book read by the student is lying on the table.

explanations.title: How to recognise them
explanations.body: Look at the suffix just before the ending:

examples.translation: The former president lives in Moscow.

explanations.title: English translations
explanations.body: Literal translations show the type well.

examples.translation: This is my favorite writer.

exercises.prompt: Which suffix signals an active participle?
Which suffix signals a passive participle?
‘A book that has been read’ is:
exercises.explanation: The book is acted on, and the action is finished: past passive.
The student acts, now: present active.

lessons.title: 252. Present active: чита́ющий, пи́шущий, говоря́щий
lessons.subtitle: Студе́нты, изуча́ющие ру́сский, живу́т в общежи́тии.

explanations.title: From the они́-form
explanations.body: A present active participle describes a noun that is doing the action right now. Take the они́-form of the verb, drop -т, and add -щий. First conjugation gives -ущий / -ющий; second conjugation gives -ащий / -ящий. The stress usually stays where it is in the они́-form.

examples.translation: The girl reading a book is my sister.

examples.text: Лю́ди, живу́щие в э́том до́ме, о́чень до́брые.
examples.translation: The people who live in this building are very kind.

explanations.title: Reflexive verbs keep -ся
explanations.body: A reflexive verb keeps -ся at the end of the participle, even after a vowel: занима́ющийся, ча́сто встреча́ющийся. The ending is always -ся here, never -сь.

examples.translation: A child who does sports rarely gets sick.

explanations.title: In a sentence
explanations.body: A present active participle can replace кото́рый + a present-tense verb. The two sentences below mean the same.

rows: Студе́нт, кото́рый чита́ет кни́гу, сиди́т у окна́.
Студе́нт, чита́ющий кни́гу, сиди́т у окна́.

examples.text: Вот челове́к, рабо́тающий в на́шем ба́нке.
examples.translation: Here is a person who works in our bank.

lessons.title: 253. Past active: чита́вший, прочита́вший, уше́дший
lessons.subtitle: Студе́нт, прочита́вший кни́гу, отве́тил на вопро́с.

explanations.title: From the past tense
explanations.body: A past active participle describes a noun that did the action earlier. Take the masculine past tense, drop -л and add -вший. If the masculine past does not end in -л, add -ший: ушёл → уше́дший. The stress stays close to the stress of the infinitive; Wiktionary shows the exact form.

examples.text: Студе́нт, прочита́вший кни́гу, отве́тил на вопро́с.
examples.translation: The student who had read the book answered the question.

examples.text: Лю́ди, прише́дшие на конце́рт, жда́ли на у́лице.
examples.translation: The people who had come to the concert were waiting on the street.

explanations.title: Imperfective or perfective
explanations.body: Past active participles can be made from both aspects. From an imperfective verb the participle shows an action in progress or a repeated one in the past: чита́вший = who was reading. From a perfective verb it shows a finished action: прочита́вший = who had read.

examples.translation: The man who had sent the parcel left.

explanations.title: In a sentence
explanations.body: A past active participle can replace кото́рый + a past-tense verb.

examples.text: Ма́льчик, уста́вший по́сле дня, лёг спать.
examples.translation: The boy, tired after the day, went to bed.

lessons.title: 254. Present passive: чита́емый, люби́мый, изуча́емый
lessons.subtitle: Вот кни́га, люби́мая детьми́.

explanations.title: From the мы-form
explanations.body: A present passive participle describes a noun that is being acted on right now. Take the мы-form of the verb and add -ый. First conjugation gives -емый; second conjugation gives -имый. Only imperfective verbs that take an object have this participle.

examples.translation: This is a language studied at school.
Dear students! The lesson is beginning.

explanations.title: The agent
explanations.body: If you say who does the action, put them in the instrumental case. The participle is passive, so the doer goes in the instrumental: чита́емая детьми́ кни́га = a book read by children.

examples.translation: This is a book loved by children.

examples.text: Вот това́ры, продава́емые в на́шем магази́не.
examples.translation: Here are the goods sold in our shop.

explanations.title: A few have become ordinary adjectives
explanations.body: Some present passive participles are now just adjectives. Люби́мый (favorite), ви́димый (visible), уважа́емый (respected, dear) are everyday words. Elsewhere this participle is mostly found in writing.

examples.translation: This is my favorite city.

lessons.title: 255. Past passive: прочи́танный, закры́тый, переведённый
lessons.subtitle: Письмо́, напи́санное вчера́, уже́ на по́чте.

explanations.title: From the infinitive of a perfective verb
explanations.body: The past passive participle describes a noun that something has been done to. It is usually made from perfective verbs. The three suffixes are -нн-, -енн- and -т-.

examples.text: Письмо́, напи́санное вчера́, уже́ на по́чте.
examples.translation: The letter written yesterday is already at the post office.
The shoppers found the umbrella that had been bought yesterday.

explanations.title: Which suffix?
explanations.body: Roughly: verbs in -ать, -ять, -еть add -нный (написанный). Verbs in -ить change the consonant and add -енный (полученный, купленный). A few short verbs add -тый (закрытый, забытый, взятый).

examples.translation: The open door leads into the garden.

explanations.title: The agent
explanations.body: The doer, if mentioned, goes in the instrumental case.

examples.translation: This is a letter written by my grandmother.
Here is an umbrella forgotten by someone.

lessons.title: 256. A participle agrees with its noun: in every case
lessons.subtitle: Я ви́жу де́вочку, чита́ющую кни́гу.

explanations.title: Like any adjective
explanations.body: A participle has adjective endings, so it agrees with its noun in gender, number and case. The verb part of the participle stays the same. Compare the endings of чита́ющий with хоро́ший:

examples.translation: I see a girl reading a book.

examples.text: Мы говори́м о де́вочке, чита́ющей кни́гу.
examples.translation: We are talking about the girl who is reading a book.

explanations.title: The object keeps its own case
explanations.body: The words that depend on the verb part keep the case the verb needs. Чита́ть takes the accusative, so кни́гу stays in the accusative however the participle changes.

examples.translation: He is helping the boy who is reading aloud.
We are pleased with the students who are studying Russian.

explanations.title: Passive and past participles
explanations.body: Passive and past participles agree in the same way. Their endings are the ordinary adjective endings.

examples.text: Я чита́ю статью́, напи́санную мои́м дру́гом.
examples.translation: I am reading an article written by my friend.

lessons.title: 257. Word order: noun + participle, or participle + noun
lessons.subtitle: Письмо́, напи́санное вчера́, лежи́т на столе́.

explanations.title: Construction 1: noun, then participle
explanations.body: The participle follows the noun and is set off by commas, together with the words that depend on it. This is the easiest order to read, because the noun comes first.

examples.text: Письмо́, напи́санное вчера́, лежи́т на столе́.
examples.translation: The letter written yesterday is lying on the table.

examples.text: Де́вочка, стоя́щая у окна́, — моя́ сестра́.
examples.translation: The girl standing by the window is my sister.

explanations.title: Construction 2: participle first, noun last
explanations.body: The participle can also stand before the noun, like an ordinary adjective. But its dependent words come with it, so the participle and its noun may be separated by a whole phrase. There is no comma before the participle.

rows: Письмо́, напи́санное вчера́, лежи́т на столе́.
Напи́санное вчера́ письмо́ лежи́т на столе́.

examples.translation: The girl standing by the window smiled.

explanations.title: How to untangle it
explanations.body: If you meet a participle without a comma before it, note its gender, number and case. Then read on until you find a noun with the same features. Everything between them belongs to the participle.

rows: Откры́тая учи́телем дверь ведёт в сад.

examples.translation: I am reading a letter written by my brother.

exercises.explanation: Instrumental: the doer of a passive participle.

exercises.promptTranslation: The student reading a newspaper is silent.
The door opened by the teacher leads into the garden.
The girl standing by the window is my sister.

exercises.prompt: Is there a comma before the participle in Construction 2?
exercises.explanation: No comma before the participle in front of the noun.

lessons.title: 264. Short past passive: закры́то, сде́лано, переведён

explanations.title: Making the short form
explanations.body: A past passive participle also has a short form, used in the nominative only and always connected to the verb быть. To make it, drop the long ending. For -тый participles, drop -ый. For -нный, drop the ending and one н. For -ённый, drop the ending and one н; the stress moves to the last syllable.

examples.text: Магази́н закры́т. Дверь закры́та. Окно́ закры́то.
examples.translation: The shop is closed. The door is closed. The window is closed.
The question has already been settled.

explanations.title: They agree with the noun
explanations.body: The short form agrees with its noun in gender and number. It has no cases: it is always the predicate (‘the door is closed’), never a description (‘the closed door’).

examples.text: Музе́й откры́т с десяти́ до шести́.
examples.translation: The museum is open from ten till six.
Everything is done.

explanations.title: Past and future
explanations.body: Present tense uses no verb: Дверь закры́та. Past tense adds была́: Дверь была́ закры́та. Future adds бу́дет: Дверь бу́дет закры́та.

examples.text: Дверь была́ закры́та, когда́ мы пришли́.
examples.translation: The door was closed when we arrived.
The question will be settled tomorrow.

lessons.title: 265. Long or short? Describes the noun, or states the result

explanations.title: Two jobs, two forms
explanations.body: A long form describes the noun and can replace кото́рый + a verb. A short form states that something has been done and is always linked with быть. The short form with its noun is a full sentence; the long form is not.

examples.translation: The parcel sent yesterday arrived today.
The parcel was sent yesterday.

explanations.title: A quick test
explanations.body: Try to replace the participle with кото́рый + a verb. If it works, use the long form. If the participle is the main information and the sentence would not be complete without it, use the short form.

explanations.title: English translations
explanations.body: The short form is often translated by ‘has been’ or ‘was’. The long form is translated by ‘that’, ‘which’ or an English participle phrase.

explanations.title: Short participles without быть
explanations.body: News headlines use short past participles and drop the verb быть. The participle usually comes first and agrees in gender and number with the noun that follows. It has the sense ‘has been done’.

explanations.body: Choose the ending to match the noun, as in a normal short participle. Masculine: no ending. Feminine: -а. Neuter: -о. Plural: -ы.

explanations.body: In normal speech you would write the sentence with the verb: Аэропо́рт закры́т. A headline is a compressed form of this: the participle is moved forward and the noun follows.

explanations.title: Three groups, three patterns
explanations.body: The noun follows the usual rule: 1 takes the nominative singular, 2–4 take the genitive singular, 5+ take the genitive plural. The adjective follows the noun.

explanations.title: Feminine nouns and 2–4
explanations.body: With feminine nouns the adjective may be in the nominative plural or in the genitive plural. The genitive plural is always safe. With masculine and neuter nouns use the genitive plural only.

explanations.body: With large numbers the last word decides the pattern. О́ба (both) and о́бе (both, f.) follow the 2–4 pattern.

explanations.title: Оди́н is an adjective
explanations.body: The number 1 agrees with its noun in gender, number and case. Its endings are those of э́тот.

explanations.title: Accusative: animate or inanimate
explanations.body: In the accusative, masculine singular and the plural look like the nominative for inanimate nouns and like the genitive for animate nouns.

examples.translation: I know only one doctor.

examples.text: Я иду́ к одному́ ста́рому дру́гу.
examples.translation: I am going to see an old friend.

explanations.title: Plural одни́
explanations.body: The plural одни́ is used with nouns that only exist in the plural. It can often be translated as ‘one pair of’.

examples.translation: He has one pair of blue trousers.

examples.text: Он пое́хал в о́тпуск с одни́м ста́рым дру́гом.

explanations.title: Two, three, four
explanations.body: These numbers change by case. The two-form два / две is only for the nominative.

examples.translation: They are satisfied with the two cars.
We talked about four students.

explanations.title: О́ба and о́бе
explanations.body: ‘Both’ has two forms. The stress is on the first syllable in the nominative and on the middle -о- (in о́ба) or -е- (in о́бе) in the other cases.

examples.text: Ле́на звони́т обо́им сыновья́м и обе́им дочеря́м ка́ждую неде́лю.
examples.translation: Lena calls both sons and both daughters every week.
I love both daughters.

explanations.title: The basic-form rule
explanations.body: The rule ‘2–4 + genitive singular’ only works when the number is in its basic (counting) form: the nominative, or the accusative of an inanimate noun. In any other case the noun takes the same case as the number. With animate nouns the accusative of 2–4 is the genitive.

examples.translation: Three students passed the exam.

lessons.title: 270. Declension of 5–20 and 30: like дверь
lessons.subtitle: Мы познако́мились с пятна́дцатью но́выми студе́нтами.

explanations.title: Only three forms
explanations.body: Numerals from 5 to 20 and 30 end in -ь and decline like дверь. The accusative is the same as the nominative, so animate and inanimate nouns behave alike.

examples.translation: He called five friends.

examples.text: Я хочу́ поговори́ть с пятью́ друзья́ми.
examples.translation: I want to talk to five friends.

explanations.title: Stress
explanations.body: In the short numerals the stress moves to the end of the word when the number is not in its basic form. In 11–19 the stress does not move.

examples.text: Э́та кни́га о восьми́ ста́рых города́х.

explanations.title: Not the basic form: no special rule
explanations.body: As with 2–4, the noun and the adjective copy the case of the number. There is no genitive plural unless the number is nominative or accusative.

examples.text: Мы познако́мились с пятна́дцатью но́выми студе́нтами.

explanations.title: Every part has its own case
explanations.body: In a number such as 25 or 36 each word takes the case ending. The last word decides whether the noun is singular or plural.

explanations.title: The last digit
explanations.body: The nominative and inanimate accusative follow the last digit: 21 → nominative singular, 22–24 → genitive singular, 25–30 → genitive plural.

explanations.body: The animate-accusative rule is used for simple 2, 3 and 4. It does not apply to 22, 23 or 24. It does apply to 21, because one is an adjective.

explanations.body: Remember the three patterns: оди́н + nominative; два, три, четы́ре + genitive singular; пять and more + genitive plural. If the number is not in its basic form, the noun takes the case of the number.

explanations.body: A short participle agrees in gender and number with its noun: закры́т, закры́та, закры́то, закры́ты. In headlines the verb быть is dropped.

explanations.title: Ожида́ется and возмо́жен
explanations.body: Forecasts say what is expected. The verb ожида́ться (to be expected) and the short adjective возмо́жен (is possible) agree with the thing that is expected, in number and gender.

examples.translation: Heavy rains are expected.
Thunderstorms are possible.

explanations.title: Предупрежда́ть о чём?
explanations.body: To warn someone about something: предупрежда́ть / предупреди́ть кого́ о чём. The warning itself is предупрежде́ние.

examples.translation: We were warned about the ice.

examples.text: Предупрежде́ние о непого́де де́йствует кру́глые су́тки.
examples.translation: The bad-weather warning is in force around the clock.

exercises.promptTranslation: A heavy downpour is expected.
Heavy downpours are expected.
Because of the ice there are many accidents on the roads.
Forecasters warned us about the strong wind.

Heavy rains are expected.
Thunderstorms are possible.

exercises.prompt: Which word means a low-pressure system?
exercises.explanation: Цикло́н = low pressure, антицикло́н = high pressure.

lessons.subtitle: Из-за ли́вней в реке́ поднялся́ у́ровень воды́.

explanations.title: Natural disasters
explanations.body: A стихи́я is a force of nature. These are the names of the most common ones.

rows: rising water from snowmelt or rain (a minor flood)

examples.translation: A flood is expected in the area of the river.
A mudflow blocked the road.
The inhabitants of three cities felt the earthquake.

explanations.title: Verbs of water and earth
explanations.body: Reports use a few typical verbs.

rows: to strike, hit (a place); to collapse

examples.translation: The water level in the river is rising.
Several streets were flooded.
An avalanche came down in the mountains.

explanations.title: A line from a news report
explanations.body: Some set phrases appear in almost every report.

examples.translation: A hurricane struck the coast.

exercises.promptTranslation: An avalanche came down in the mountains.
The water level in the river is rising.

exercises.explanation: Три + genitive, but трёх: genitive plural.

lessons.title: 275. Fire and rescue: пожа́р, туши́ть, спаса́тель, эвакуа́ция
lessons.subtitle: Спаса́тели потуши́ли пожа́р и эвакуи́ровали жи́телей.

explanations.title: Fire and rescue words
explanations.body: A basic vocabulary for reports about fires and rescue work.

examples.text: Из-за ды́ма в до́ме бы́ло тру́дно дыша́ть.
examples.translation: Because of the smoke it was hard to breathe in the house.
The house burned all night.

explanations.title: Verbs
explanations.body: The actions of the fire service and rescuers.

examples.text: Спаса́тели потуши́ли пожа́р за три часа́.
examples.translation: The rescuers put out the fire in three hours.
The fire spread to the neighboring house.
The rescuers evacuated the residents of the building.

explanations.title: They: the impersonal plural
explanations.body: News reports often leave out who is doing the work and use the plural ‘they’ in the past tense. You know this from the indefinite-personal sentences.

examples.translation: They were putting out the fire for almost six hours.

examples.text: Люде́й спасли́ с кры́ши на вертолёте.
examples.translation: People were rescued from the roof by helicopter.

The fire spread to the neighboring house.

lessons.title: 276. Damage and aftermath: после́дствия, уще́рб, разруше́ния, убы́тки
lessons.subtitle: Уще́рб от наводне́ния соста́вил не́сколько миллио́нов рубле́й.

explanations.title: Nouns for damage
explanations.body: Most of these appear in the plural in reports.

examples.translation: The scale of the destruction is very large.
People were left homeless.

explanations.title: Verbs
explanations.body: What the damage amounts to, and what is done about it.

examples.translation: The damage amounted to several million rubles.

explanations.title: According to preliminary data
explanations.body: Reports start with sources and estimates: по + Dative plural.

rows: according to the report of the emergency services

People were left homeless.

explanations.title: Time words in reports
explanations.body: A few time expressions that appear again and again.

examples.text: Накану́не в о́бласти объяви́ли режи́м ЧС.
examples.translation: The day before, a state of emergency was declared in the region.
Two hours later the fire was put out.
The rescuers work around the clock.

explanations.title: Verbs that report events
explanations.body: Verbs for what happened to people.

rows: to have to (impersonal; the person is in the dative)
to find oneself, to turn out

examples.translation: The residents had to leave their homes.
Many found themselves without electricity.
The river remains high.

explanations.title: Reporting the source
explanations.body: Reports often name the source in an introductory phrase.

rows: According to a report by the emergency services, …

examples.text: Как сообща́ют в МЧС, пострада́вших нет.
examples.translation: As the emergency services report, there are no casualties.

exercises.explanation: Накану́не + genitive: on the eve of.

Two hours later the fire was put out.
The residents had to leave their homes.
