lessons.title: 278. Collective numerals: дво́е, тро́е, че́тверо, пя́теро
lessons.subtitle: Дво́е пострада́ли, а че́тверо оста́лись без кро́ва.

explanations.title: The collective numerals
explanations.body: Besides the ordinary numerals, Russian has a set of collective numerals, mostly used in news about groups of people. Above ten they do not exist, and from six upward they are rare.

examples.text: На вечери́нке нас бы́ло всего́ че́тверо.
examples.translation: There were only four of us at the party.
Three tourists went missing in the mountains.

explanations.title: Case endings
explanations.body: The endings are always stressed. Дво́е and тро́е decline like soft adjectives, че́тверо and higher like hard ones. In the accusative, animate objects use the genitive.

examples.translation: The rescuers found all four.
Nothing is known about the two.

explanations.title: In news reports
explanations.body: A collective numeral is often used without a noun, in the sense ‘people’. The verb is plural.

examples.translation: Two died and four were injured.

exercises.promptTranslation: There were four of us.

exercises.prompt: Дво́е пострада́ли, а че́тверо ___ без кро́ва. (were left)
exercises.explanation: Plural verb with a collective numeral.
exercises.promptTranslation: Two were injured and four were left homeless.
Three tourists went missing in the mountains.
The rescuers found all four.
Nothing is known about the two.
They have three children.

exercises.explanation: Collective numeral + genitive plural; not for girls only.

options: are the same as ordinary numerals

lessons.title: 279. дво́е часо́в or два часа́? When to use collective numerals
lessons.subtitle: Ва́ня купи́л дво́е часо́в: одни́ себе́, одни́ бра́ту.

explanations.title: When the collective numeral is used
explanations.body: Where both a collective and an ordinary numeral are possible, the collective one is preferred in these cases.

rows: дво́е часо́в, тро́е су́ток, че́тверо кани́кул

examples.text: Ва́ня купи́л дво́е часо́в: одни́ себе́, одни́ бра́ту.
examples.translation: Vanya bought two watches: one for himself, one for his brother.
Two men were sitting in the park.
They have three children.

explanations.title: Ordinary or collective?
explanations.body: Compare the meanings. Часы́ (watch) is a plural-only noun, so it needs the collective numeral; часы́ as ‘hours’ is the ordinary noun час.

examples.translation: We waited for three days and nights.
I have three sisters.

explanations.title: Not for women
explanations.body: The collective numeral is for males, or for mixed groups. For women only, use the ordinary numeral. A mixed group can use the collective numeral without a noun.

examples.text: Нас бы́ло тро́е: сестра́, брат и я.
examples.translation: There were three of us: my sister, my brother and I.

examples.text: Нам нужны́ че́тверо кани́кул в год.
examples.translation: We need four vacations a year.

exercises.promptTranslation: Vanya bought two watches.
They have three children.
Two men were sitting in the room.
We waited for three days and nights.

exercises.explanation: Women: ordinary numeral three + genitive singular.
exercises.promptTranslation: I have three sisters.
We need four vacations a year.

exercises.prompt: Which noun cannot take a collective numeral?

lessons.title: 280. Together as a group: вдвоём, втроём, вчетвером, впятером
lessons.subtitle: Мы пое́хали в го́ры вчетверо́м.

explanations.title: Collective adverbs
explanations.body: To say that an action is done by a small group together, put в in front of the collective numeral and use the ending -ом (-ём for 2 and 3). These adverbs do not change.

examples.translation: My friend and I traveled as a pair.
Trips for two are more fun.
The four of us went to the mountains.

explanations.title: Using them with verbs
explanations.body: The adverb tells you how many people act together. It often replaces вме́сте in a sentence about a small group.

rows: to come as a group of three
to live, the four of us
to be left alone together, the two of us
to have lunch, the two of us

examples.text: Мы жи́ли впятеро́м в одно́й ко́мнате.
examples.translation: The five of us lived in one room.
The three of them came to visit.

explanations.title: Fitting in
explanations.body: Collective adverbs are common when you speak about whether a group fits, travels or sits together.

examples.text: Впятеро́м мы не помести́мся в маши́не.
examples.translation: The five of us won't fit in the car.

examples.text: Вчетверо́м мы сиде́ли за одни́м сто́ликом.
examples.translation: The four of us sat at one table.

exercises.prompt: Мы с дру́гом путеше́ствовали ___. (as a pair)
exercises.promptTranslation: My friend and I traveled together.

exercises.prompt: Нас бы́ло тро́е, и мы пошли́ в кино́ ___. (as a group of three)
exercises.explanation: Adverb for a group of three.
exercises.promptTranslation: There were three of us and we went to the cinema together.

exercises.prompt: В маши́не мы помести́мся то́лько ___. (the four of us)
exercises.promptTranslation: We will only fit in the car as four.

exercises.prompt: Мы жи́ли ___ в одно́й ко́мнате. (the five of us)
exercises.promptTranslation: The five of us lived in one room.

exercises.prompt: Which adverb means ‘as a group of three’?

exercises.explanation: A small set of fixed adverbs.

lessons.title: 281. Telling time (1): пять мину́т седьмо́го, полови́на пе́рвого
lessons.subtitle: Сейча́с пять мину́т седьмо́го.

explanations.title: Digital time
explanations.body: In everyday speech you will often hear the digital style. Say the hour and then the minutes, one after another.

examples.translation: It is eight twenty-five now.

explanations.title: Russian-style time: minutes of the next hour
explanations.body: The day starts at midnight, so 12:05 a.m. is five minutes into the first hour. Russians say ‘five minutes of the first’: the number of minutes, then the hour that has begun, as an ordinal in the genitive. This is used for 1–29 minutes.

examples.translation: It is ten past three.
It is a quarter past seven.

explanations.title: Half past
explanations.body: For 30 minutes say полови́на + the next hour in the genitive. In speech полови́на is often shortened to пол-: полседьмо́го.

examples.translation: It is half past six.
It is a quarter past seven.

exercises.promptTranslation: It is ten past three.
It is a quarter past seven.
It is half past six.
It is five past twelve.
It is one minute past one.
It is twenty-nine minutes past eleven.

exercises.explanation: The sixth hour has ended; five minutes of the seventh.

lessons.title: 282. Telling time (2): без двадцати́ три, без че́тверти во́семь
lessons.subtitle: Сейча́с без десяти́ во́семь.

explanations.title: After half past: ‘without’
explanations.body: From 31 to 59 minutes Russians look ahead and say how many minutes are missing: без + genitive of the number + the next hour as an ordinary number. The word мину́та is usually left out, except for amounts under five.

examples.translation: It is ten to eight.
It is twenty-five to eight.

explanations.title: A quarter and one o'clock
explanations.body: Че́тверть (a quarter) is used as in English. One o'clock is simply час.

examples.translation: It is a quarter to six.
It is twenty to one.

explanations.title: The 24-hour clock
explanations.body: Timetables, television guides and announcements use the 24-hour clock. The hour and the minutes are read as ordinary numbers.

examples.text: По расписа́нию по́езд отправля́ется в четы́рнадцать три́дцать.
examples.translation: According to the timetable the train leaves at fourteen thirty.

exercises.promptTranslation: It is twenty to three.
It is a quarter to eight.
It is ten to four.
It is one minute to two.
It is two minutes to ten.
It is twenty to one.
It is fourteen thirty.

exercises.prompt: From 31 to 59 minutes you count towards:

lessons.title: 283. At what time? Кото́рый час? В кото́ром часу́? Во ско́лько?
lessons.subtitle: — Во ско́лько нача́ло? — В полови́не седьмо́го.

explanations.title: Two different questions
explanations.body: To ask what the time is now, use Кото́рый час? or Ско́лько вре́мени?. To ask when something happens, use В кото́ром часу́? or Во ско́лько?.

examples.translation: What time is it now?
At what time does the film start?

explanations.title: The preposition в
explanations.body: For ‘at’ with the time: after 1–29 minutes, use в + accusative. For half past use в + prepositional. For the ‘without’ forms use no preposition at all. The short пол- forms never change.

examples.text: Мы пришли́ домо́й в пять мину́т восьмо́го.
examples.translation: We came home at five past seven.
The film starts at half past six.
The bus arrives at five to ten.

explanations.title: Putting it together
explanations.body: A short conversation using both questions.

examples.text: — Во ско́лько вы пришли́ домо́й? — Без двадцати́ пяти́ де́вять.
examples.translation: — What time did you get home? — At twenty-five to nine.
— What time is it? — Half past nine.

exercises.prompt: — ___ вы пришли́ домо́й? — Без двадцати́ пяти́ де́вять. (At what time)
exercises.promptTranslation: — What time did you get home? — At twenty-five to nine.
The film starts at half past six.

exercises.prompt: Мы пришли́ домо́й ___ пять мину́т восьмо́го. (at)
exercises.promptTranslation: We came home at five past seven.

exercises.prompt: По́езд отправля́ется ___ че́тверти шесть. (at a quarter to)
exercises.promptTranslation: The train leaves at a quarter to six.
The film starts at half past seven.

exercises.prompt: Мы встре́тились в ___. (at half past nine, short form)
exercises.explanation: The short form does not change.
exercises.promptTranslation: We met at half past nine.

exercises.prompt: Which question means ‘What time is it?’

lessons.title: 284. Word-building: -рух-, -выс-, под-, воз-/вос-, вз-/вс-
lessons.subtitle: Высота́ зда́ния превыша́ет де́сять этаже́й.

explanations.title: The roots -рух- and -выс-
explanations.body: Roots carry meaning across many words. -Рух- is about collapse and destruction; -выс- is about height.

examples.translation: The height of the building exceeds ten floors.
Prices rose in September.

explanations.title: The prefix под-
explanations.body: Под- means ‘under’ or ‘from below’ in many words. It can also mean ‘secretly’ or ‘in addition’.

examples.translation: He found a side job for the weekends.
Don't eavesdrop on other people's conversations.

explanations.title: воз- / вос-, вз- / вс-
explanations.body: Воз-/вос- often means ‘again’ or an abstract ‘up’. Вз-/вс- means ‘up’ in a physical sense.

examples.translation: The shop has resumed work on Sundays.

examples.text: Взро́слые и де́ти пришли́ на пра́здник.
examples.translation: Adults and children came to the party.

exercises.promptTranslation: The shop resumed work on Sundays.
Prices rose in September.
He violated the rules.

lessons.title: 285. Review: weather, disasters, collective numerals, telling time
lessons.subtitle: Накану́не в полови́не седьмо́го в го́роде начался́ ли́вень.

explanations.title: Collective numerals and adverbs
explanations.body: Collective numerals stand for groups of people or plural-only nouns and take the genitive plural. The adverbs вдвоём, втроём, вчетверо́м say that the group acts together.

examples.translation: Four tourists were found alive.

explanations.title: Telling time
explanations.body: Minutes 1–29: minutes + the next hour in the genitive. Half: полови́на + hour. Minutes 31–59: без + minutes + the next hour. For ‘at’: в for the first two kinds, no preposition for без.

explanations.body: Words for those who commit crimes and for the crimes themselves.

explanations.body: The people and procedures of an investigation.

examples.translation: The police carried out a search in the apartment.

explanations.body: Typical verbs in a police report.

rows: to put on the wanted list

explanations.title: Verbs with prepositions
explanations.body: Verbs of crime and justice have fixed patterns. Learn the preposition and the case together.

examples.translation: He is accused of theft.
The man is suspected of murder.
The court sentenced him to a fine.

explanations.title: Nouns and adjectives with the same pattern
explanations.body: The nouns and adjectives from these verbs keep the preposition.

examples.translation: He was charged with theft.

examples.text: Суд приговори́л вора́ к трём года́м заключе́ния.
examples.translation: The court sentenced the thief to three years of imprisonment.

explanations.title: Aspect pairs
explanations.body: Most of the verbs come in pairs.

examples.translation: He broke the law.

exercises.promptTranslation: He is accused of theft.
The man is suspected of murder.
The court sentenced him to a fine.
He is accused of theft.

exercises.prompt: Суд приговори́л вора́ к трём ___ заключе́ния. (years)
exercises.promptTranslation: The court sentenced the thief to three years of imprisonment.
The criminal admitted his guilt.
He broke the law.

lessons.title: 290. Verbal adverbs: чита́я and прочита́в
lessons.subtitle: Он за́втракает, проверя́я по́чту.

explanations.title: What is a verbal adverb?
explanations.body: A verbal adverb (дееприча́стие) is a verb form that works as an adverb. It has no tense, gender or case: it only adds a second action to the main verb. It comes in two kinds.

rows: at the same time as the main action

examples.translation: He eats breakfast while checking his mail.
Having checked his mail, he goes to have breakfast.

explanations.title: The same person does both actions
explanations.body: The verbal adverb always belongs to the subject of the main verb. The tense is set only by the main verb.

examples.translation: While walking home, I met a friend.
Having read the letter, she phoned home.

explanations.title: Mostly written Russian
explanations.body: Verbal adverbs are typical of written and formal Russian. In speech you use a clause with пока́ or по́сле того́ как.

rows: Пока́ он чита́л кни́гу, он пил чай.
По́сле того́ как он прочита́л кни́гу, он лёг спать.

examples.translation: While reading the book he drank tea.

exercises.promptTranslation: He drinks tea while reading the news.
Having read the letter, she phoned home.
He walks along the street listening to music.

exercises.prompt: ___ дома́шнюю рабо́ту, Ди́ма пошёл в кино́. (having done)
exercises.promptTranslation: Having done his homework, Dima went to the cinema.
She eats supper while watching television.

exercises.prompt: Which verbal adverb shows an action before the main action?
Who performs both actions in a sentence with a verbal adverb?

lessons.title: 291. Imperfective verbal adverbs: чита́я, говоря́, слу́жа, сидя́
lessons.subtitle: Мы пьём чай, разгова́ривая.

explanations.title: The rule
explanations.body: Take the они́ form, drop the last two letters (-ут, -ют, -ат, -ят) and add -я. After ж, ч, ш and щ write -а instead.

examples.translation: While walking home I met a friend.

examples.text: Рабо́тая в рестора́не, она́ про́бовала мно́го блюд.
examples.translation: While working in a restaurant she tried many dishes.

explanations.title: Stress and special cases
explanations.body: In a few verbs the stress is different from the они́ form. Verbs in -ся end in -ясь. Verbs in -давать, -знавать, -ставать keep -ва-.

examples.text: Лёжа на дива́не, он чита́л кни́гу.
examples.translation: Lying on the sofa, he read a book.

examples.text: Бу́дучи вегетариа́нцем, Ле́на не ест мя́со.
examples.translation: Being a vegetarian, Lena does not eat meat.

explanations.title: No imperfective verbal adverb
explanations.body: Some common verbs do not form an imperfective verbal adverb at all: есть, пить, е́хать, спать, хоте́ть, ждать, мочь, писа́ть. Use a clause with пока́ instead.

examples.text: Пока́ он пил чай, он чита́л газе́ту.
examples.translation: While he drank tea he read the newspaper.

exercises.promptTranslation: Walking along the street, he listened to music.
She answers, smiling.

exercises.prompt: ___ в рестора́не, Та́ня про́бовала мно́го блюд. (working)
exercises.promptTranslation: While working in a restaurant, Tanya tried many dishes.

exercises.explanation: The adverb of лежа́ть is лёжа.
exercises.promptTranslation: Lying on the sofa, he read a book.
We drink tea, chatting.

exercises.explanation: The adverb of быть is бу́дучи.
exercises.promptTranslation: Being a vegetarian, Lena does not eat meat.

exercises.prompt: Form the verbal adverb from говоря́т:
Which verb has no imperfective verbal adverb?
The verbal adverb from занима́ться ends in:

lessons.title: 292. Perfective verbal adverbs: прочита́в, получи́в, придя́
lessons.subtitle: Прочита́в письмо́, он позвони́л домо́й.

explanations.title: The rule: -л → -в
explanations.body: Take the masculine past tense and replace the final -л with -в.

examples.translation: Having read the letter, he phoned home.

examples.text: Сде́лав дома́шнюю рабо́ту, Ди́ма пошёл в кино́.
examples.translation: Having done his homework, Dima went to the cinema.

explanations.title: When the masculine past does not end in -л
explanations.body: Add -ши. Verbs with -ся always take -вшись.

examples.text: Вы́росши в дере́вне, наш сосе́д не лю́бит жить в большо́м го́роде.
examples.translation: Having grown up in the country, our neighbor doesn't like living in a big city.

examples.text: Познако́мившись с Ле́ной, он позвони́л ей на сле́дующий день.
examples.translation: Having met Lena, he called her the next day.

explanations.title: Motion verbs: like the imperfective rule
explanations.body: Verbs in -йти, -вести, -везти, -нести form the perfective adverb the way the imperfective is formed: the они́ form minus the ending plus -я. So one letter can be the only difference between the two aspects.

examples.translation: Having come home, he turned on the TV.

examples.text: Вы́йдя из до́ма, он закры́л дверь.
examples.translation: Having gone out of the house, he closed the door.

exercises.promptTranslation: Having read the letter, he phoned home.

exercises.prompt: ___ биле́ты, мы пошли́ в аэропо́рт. (having bought)
exercises.promptTranslation: Having bought the tickets, we went to the airport.
Having come home, he turned on the TV.

exercises.prompt: ___ пла́вать, он с удово́льствием хо́дит в бассе́йн. (having learned)
exercises.promptTranslation: Having learned to swim, he goes to the pool with pleasure.

exercises.prompt: Вы́йдя из до́ма, он закры́л ___. (the door)
exercises.promptTranslation: Having left the house, he closed the door.

exercises.prompt: ___ в дере́вне, наш сосе́д не лю́бит жить в большо́м го́роде. (having grown up)
exercises.promptTranslation: Having grown up in the country, our neighbor doesn't like living in a big city.

exercises.prompt: The perfective adverb of прийти́ is:
-ся verbs form perfective verbal adverbs ending in:

lessons.title: 293. Without doing: не ду́мая, не сказа́в; adverb or participle?
lessons.subtitle: Он ушёл, не сказа́в ни сло́ва.

explanations.title: Не + verbal adverb = ‘without’
explanations.body: A verbal adverb with не often means ‘without doing’. It can be imperfective or perfective.

examples.text: Он ушёл, не сказа́в ни сло́ва.
examples.translation: He left without saying a word.

examples.text: Не ду́мая о после́дствиях, он вы́шел на у́лицу без пальто́.
examples.translation: Without thinking about the consequences, he went outside without a coat.

examples.text: Она́ рабо́тает, не теря́я ни мину́ты.
examples.translation: She works without losing a minute.

explanations.title: Verbal adverb or participle?
explanations.body: A verbal adverb has no endings and belongs to the subject. A participle agrees with a noun. Compare:

rows: Вы́росши в дере́вне, наш сосе́д не лю́бит го́род.
verbal adverb: the neighbor, having grown up in the country, …
Наш сосе́д, вы́росший в дере́вне, не лю́бит го́род.
participle: our neighbor, who grew up in the country, …

examples.text: Вы́росши в дере́вне, наш сосе́д не лю́бит го́род.
examples.translation: Having grown up in the country, our neighbor does not like cities.

examples.text: Наш сосе́д, вы́росший в дере́вне, не лю́бит го́род.
examples.translation: Our neighbor, who grew up in the country, does not like cities.

explanations.title: Commas
explanations.body: A phrase with a verbal adverb is separated by commas from the rest of the sentence.

examples.translation: Having come home, he went to bed.

examples.text: Он рассказа́л об э́том, не поду́мав о после́дствиях.
examples.translation: He told about it without thinking of the consequences.

exercises.promptTranslation: He left without saying a word.

exercises.prompt: ___ о после́дствиях, он вы́шел на у́лицу. (without thinking)
exercises.promptTranslation: Without thinking about the consequences, he went outside.
She works without losing a minute.

exercises.prompt: Наш сосе́д, ___ в дере́вне, не лю́бит го́род. (who grew up)
exercises.promptTranslation: Our neighbor, who grew up in the country, does not like cities.

exercises.prompt: ___ в дере́вне, наш сосе́д не лю́бит го́род. (having grown up)
exercises.promptTranslation: Having grown up in the country, our neighbor does not like cities.

exercises.prompt: A participle differs from a verbal adverb because it:
A phrase with a verbal adverb is set off by:

lessons.title: 294. Verbal adverb or clause? в то вре́мя как, по́сле того́ как, как то́лько
lessons.subtitle: Придя́ домо́й, он лёг спать = Когда́ он пришёл домо́й, он лёг спать.

explanations.title: Imperfective: while
explanations.body: Replace an imperfective verbal adverb with в то вре́мя как, пока́ or когда́. Add the subject and put the verb in the same tense as the main verb.

rows: Рабо́тая над перево́дом, Ма́ша слу́шала му́зыку.
В то вре́мя как Ма́ша рабо́тала над перево́дом, она́ слу́шала му́зыку.
Когда́ я шёл домо́й, я встре́тил дру́га.

examples.text: Рабо́тая над перево́дом, Ма́ша слу́шала му́зыку.
examples.translation: While working on a translation, Masha listened to music.

explanations.title: Perfective: after
explanations.body: Replace a perfective verbal adverb with по́сле того́ как, когда́ or как то́лько.

rows: Как то́лько соба́ка услы́шала шаги́, она́ сра́зу подбежа́ла.
Проведя́ два го́да в Герма́нии, Бо́ря стал хорошо́ говори́ть по-неме́цки.
По́сле того́ как Бо́ря провёл два го́да в Герма́нии, он стал хорошо́ говори́ть по-неме́цки.

examples.translation: Hearing steps, the dog ran up at once.

explanations.title: Steps for rewriting
explanations.body: 1. Find the verbal adverb. 2. Decide: same time (imperfective) or earlier (perfective). 3. Choose the conjunction. 4. Turn the adverb into a finite verb that agrees with the subject. 5. Put it in the same tense as the main verb.

rows: в то вре́мя как, пока́, когда́
по́сле того́ как, как то́лько, когда́

examples.translation: Having finished the work, he went home.

examples.text: По́сле того́ как он сде́лал рабо́ту, он пошёл домо́й.
examples.translation: After he finished the work, he went home.

exercises.prompt: Рабо́тая над перево́дом = ___ она́ рабо́тала над перево́дом. (while)
exercises.promptTranslation: While she was working on a translation.

exercises.prompt: ___ он прочита́л письмо́, он позвони́л домо́й. (after)
exercises.promptTranslation: After he read the letter, he phoned home.

exercises.prompt: ___ соба́ка услы́шала шаги́, она́ сра́зу подбежа́ла. (as soon as)
exercises.promptTranslation: As soon as the dog heard steps, it ran up at once.

exercises.prompt: Идя́ домо́й = ___ я шёл домо́й, я встре́тил дру́га. (when)
exercises.promptTranslation: While I was walking home, I met a friend.

exercises.prompt: Проведя́ два го́да в Герма́нии = По́сле того́ как он ___ два го́да в Герма́нии. (spent)
exercises.promptTranslation: After he spent two years in Germany.

exercises.prompt: Which conjunction replaces an imperfective verbal adverb?
Which replaces a perfective verbal adverb?
When you rewrite an adverb as a clause you must add:
exercises.explanation: The clause needs its own subject and finite verb.

lessons.title: 295. Case conflicts: Мы ве́рим тому́, что они́ сказа́ли
lessons.subtitle: Мы ве́рим тому́, что они́ сказа́ли.

explanations.title: Two verbs, two cases
explanations.body: Sometimes one verb takes the dative and the other the accusative, and the same word ‘what’ has to join them. Russian solves this with a buffer word то (the neuter of тот). It takes the case of the first verb.

rows: Мы не слы́шали, что они́ сказа́ли.
Мы ве́рим тому́, что они́ сказа́ли.
Мы ду́мали о том, что они́ сказа́ли.

examples.text: Мы ве́рим тому́, что они́ сказа́ли.
examples.translation: We believe what they said.

examples.text: Мы ду́мали о том, что они́ сказа́ли.
examples.translation: We thought about what they said.

explanations.title: Forms of то
explanations.body: The buffer word to use depends on the case the first verb needs.

rows: Мы бои́мся того́, что он ска́жет.
Мы ве́рим тому́, что она́ сказа́ла.
Мы говори́м о том, что случи́лось.

examples.translation: He does what he loves.

examples.text: Мы говори́м о том, что случи́лось.
examples.translation: We are talking about what happened.

explanations.title: Nouns, accusative and exceptions
explanations.body: When a noun joins the clauses, use кото́рый instead of то. If the first verb takes the accusative, то is usually left out. But if the first verb needs any other case, то is needed even when there is no real conflict.

rows: Мы ве́рим лю́дям, кото́рые э́то сказа́ли.
Подро́стки не ве́рят тому́, чему́ роди́тели их у́чат.

examples.text: Мы ве́рим лю́дям, кото́рые э́то сказа́ли.
examples.translation: We believe the people who said it.

examples.text: Подро́стки не ве́рят тому́, чему́ роди́тели стара́ются их учи́ть.
examples.translation: Teenagers do not believe what their parents try to teach them.

exercises.promptTranslation: We believe what they said.

exercises.prompt: Мы ду́мали о ___, что они́ сказа́ли.
exercises.promptTranslation: We thought about what they said.
He does what he loves.

exercises.explanation: Both verbs take the accusative: no buffer.
exercises.promptTranslation: We know what they said.

exercises.prompt: Подро́стки не ве́рят ___, чему́ роди́тели стара́ются их учи́ть.
exercises.promptTranslation: Teenagers do not believe what their parents try to teach them.

exercises.explanation: A noun links the clauses: кото́рый.
exercises.promptTranslation: We believe the people who said it.

exercises.prompt: Why is то needed in ‘Мы ве́рим тому́, что они́ сказа́ли’?
options: the two verbs need different cases

exercises.prompt: If the first verb takes the accusative, то is:

lessons.title: 296. то after prepositions: из-за того́, что; по́сле того́ как; о том, как
lessons.subtitle: Ава́рия произошла́ из-за того́, что води́тель не уви́дел знак.

explanations.title: Conjunctions made of preposition + то
explanations.body: Many conjunctions are formed from a preposition, a form of то and что or как. The preposition decides the form of то.

examples.text: Ава́рия произошла́ из-за того́, что води́тель не уви́дел знак.
examples.translation: The accident happened because the driver did not see the sign.

examples.text: По́сле того́ как Ле́на око́нчила рабо́ту, она́ пошла́ спать.
examples.translation: After Lena finished her work, she went to bed.

examples.text: Мы верну́лись домо́й как раз пе́ред тем как пошёл дождь.
examples.translation: We got home just before it started to rain.

explanations.title: Verb + preposition + то
explanations.body: After a verb with a preposition, то often introduces an indirect question.

rows: Цена́ зави́сит от того́, куда́ вы лети́те.
Мы ду́мали о том, почему́ мы проигра́ли.
Они́ говори́ли о том, где жить.

examples.text: Цена́ биле́тов зави́сит от того́, куда́ вы лети́те.
examples.translation: The price of the tickets depends on where you are flying.

explanations.title: Noun + preposition + то
explanations.body: Nouns and short adjectives also use то.

examples.text: Вот статья́ о том, как стать миллионе́ром.
examples.translation: Here is an article about how to become a millionaire.

examples.text: Пробле́ма в том, что вре́мени ма́ло.
examples.translation: The problem is that there is little time.

examples.text: Он смог прийти́, несмотря́ на то, что бо́лен.
examples.translation: He managed to come in spite of being ill.

exercises.prompt: Ава́рия произошла́ из-за ___, что води́тель не уви́дел знак.
exercises.promptTranslation: The accident happened because the driver did not see the sign.

exercises.prompt: Цена́ биле́тов зави́сит ___ того́, куда́ вы лети́те.
exercises.promptTranslation: The price of the tickets depends on where you are flying.

exercises.prompt: ___ того́ как Ле́на око́нчила рабо́ту, она́ пошла́ спать. (After)
exercises.promptTranslation: After Lena finished work, she went to bed.

exercises.prompt: Мы верну́лись домо́й как раз ___ тем как пошёл дождь. (just before)
exercises.promptTranslation: We got home just before it started to rain.

exercises.prompt: Пробле́ма ___ том, что вре́мени ма́ло. (is in)
exercises.promptTranslation: The problem is that there is little time.

exercises.prompt: Вот статья́ ___ том, как стать миллионе́ром. (about)
exercises.promptTranslation: Here is an article about how to become a millionaire.

exercises.prompt: Он смог прийти́, несмотря́ ___ то, что бо́лен. (despite)
exercises.promptTranslation: He managed to come in spite of being ill.

lessons.title: 297. дово́лен тем, что; тот, кто; те, кто
lessons.subtitle: Тот, кто придёт пе́рвым, полу́чит приз.

explanations.title: Short adjectives with то
explanations.body: Short-form adjectives govern a case, so they also need то before что or an indirect question.

rows: уве́рен в том, что он прав
согла́сен с тем, что вы сказа́ли

examples.text: И́горь недово́лен тем, ско́лько ему́ пла́тят.
examples.translation: Igor is dissatisfied with how much he is paid.

examples.text: Э́та доро́га опа́сна тем, что на ней мало́ освеще́ния.
examples.translation: This road is dangerous because there is little lighting on it.

examples.text: Я рад тому́, что вы пришли́.
examples.translation: I am glad that you came.

explanations.title: Тот, кто and те, кто
explanations.body: To speak about people in general, use тот with кто (singular) or те with кто (plural). Each part takes its own case.

rows: Тот, кто придёт пе́рвым, полу́чит приз.
Те, у кого́ есть соба́ка, ча́сто гуля́ют.
Всегда́ говори́те пра́вду тому́, кого́ вы лю́бите.
У тех, кто говори́т на иностра́нном языке́, лу́чше па́мять.

examples.text: Тот, кто придёт пе́рвым, полу́чит приз.
examples.translation: The one who comes first will get a prize.

examples.text: Те, у кого́ есть соба́ка, ча́сто гуля́ют.
examples.translation: Those who have a dog walk often.

explanations.title: Agreement
explanations.body: After те the main verb is plural. After кто the verb in the second clause is usually singular, but the plural is also heard.

examples.text: Всегда́ говори́те пра́вду тому́, кого́ вы лю́бите.
examples.translation: Always tell the truth to the one you love.

exercises.promptTranslation: Igor is dissatisfied with how much he is paid.
I am glad that you came.

exercises.prompt: Я уве́рен в ___, что он прав.
exercises.promptTranslation: I am sure that he is right.

exercises.prompt: ___, кто придёт пе́рвым, полу́чит приз. (The one)
exercises.promptTranslation: The one who comes first will get a prize.

exercises.prompt: Всегда́ говори́те пра́вду ___, кого́ вы лю́бите. (to the one)
exercises.promptTranslation: Always tell the truth to the one you love.

exercises.prompt: ___, у кого́ есть соба́ка, ча́сто гуля́ют. (Those)
exercises.explanation: Plural, nominative; the verb is plural.
exercises.promptTranslation: Those who have a dog walk often.

exercises.prompt: Э́та доро́га опа́сна ___, что на ней мало́ освеще́ния.
exercises.promptTranslation: This road is dangerous because there is little lighting on it.

lessons.title: 298. Word-building: -вин-, -след-, под-
lessons.subtitle: Суд призна́л подсуди́мого вино́вным.

explanations.title: The root -вин-
explanations.body: -Вин- is about guilt and blame.

examples.translation: Who is to blame?
The court found the defendant guilty.

explanations.title: The root -след-
explanations.body: -След- is about a trace and following.

rows: to watch, to keep an eye on

examples.translation: The mother is watching the children.
The police got onto the criminal's trail.
He received an inheritance from his grandfather.

explanations.title: The prefix под- in legal words
explanations.body: Под- can mean ‘under’: a person under someone's protection or authority.

examples.translation: My client does not admit guilt.

exercises.promptTranslation: Who is to blame for this?
The investigator is conducting an investigation.
The mother is watching the children.
The police got onto the criminal's trail.
He received an inheritance from his grandfather.

lessons.title: 299. Review: crime, verbal adverbs and case conflicts
lessons.subtitle: Прочита́в пригово́р, он не ве́рил тому́, что слы́шит.

explanations.title: Verbal adverbs: a reminder
explanations.body: Imperfective (at the same time): они́ form minus the ending + -я (чита́ют → чита́я). Perfective (before): masculine past −л + в (прочита́л → прочита́в); -ся verbs: -вшись; -йти, -вести, -везти, -нести: they-form + -я (придя́). Не + adverb = ‘without’.

rows: Он ушёл, не сказа́в ни сло́ва.

examples.text: Прочита́в пригово́р, он не ве́рил тому́, что слы́шит.
examples.translation: Having read the verdict, he did not believe what he was hearing.

explanations.title: The buffer word то
explanations.body: Use то in the case required by the first verb, adjective, noun or preposition. Use тот, кто and те, кто for people.

rows: Мы ве́рим тому́, что они́ сказа́ли.
Мы говори́м о том, что случи́лось.
Те, кто нару́шил зако́н, отвеча́ют пе́ред судо́м.

examples.text: Те, кто нару́шил зако́н, отвеча́ют пе́ред судо́м.
examples.translation: Those who broke the law answer before the court.

exercises.prompt: ___ пригово́р, он не ве́рил тому́, что слы́шит. (having read)
exercises.promptTranslation: Having read the verdict, he did not believe what he was hearing.
He did not believe what he heard.
Walking home, I listened to music.
He left without saying a word.

exercises.prompt: Ава́рия произошла́ из-за ___, что дождь шёл це́лый день. (the fact)
exercises.promptTranslation: The accident happened because it rained all day.

exercises.prompt: ___, кто нару́шил зако́н, отвеча́ют пе́ред судо́м. (Those)
exercises.promptTranslation: Those who broke the law answer before the court.
He accuses her of theft.

exercises.prompt: Which word is the buffer in ‘Мы говори́м ___ том, что случи́лось’?

units.title: Unit 30: Education and negation

lessons.title: 300. The education system: шко́ла, учени́к, университе́т, вы́сшее образова́ние
lessons.subtitle: Шко́льники у́чатся одиннадцать лет, а студе́нты — в университе́те.

explanations.title: Stages of education
explanations.body: Russian general education runs through eleven school grades. After that come vocational colleges and higher education.

examples.translation: Schoolchildren study for eleven years.
She received a higher education.

explanations.title: People in education
explanations.body: Pupils in grades 1–11 are ученики́ or шко́льники. People at a university are студе́нты. The one who has finished is a выпускни́к.

examples.translation: There are many pupils in our class.
The school's graduates received their certificates.

explanations.title: Places at a university
explanations.body: A university has факульте́ты (departments). Studying at a university is described with на for a faculty and a year, and в for the institution.

examples.text: Мой брат у́чится на второ́м ку́рсе.
examples.translation: My brother is in his second year.
She studies in the journalism department.

exercises.promptTranslation: My son studies at school.

exercises.prompt: Она́ у́чится на пе́рвом ___. (year of university)
exercises.promptTranslation: She is in her first year.
My brother studies in our department.
After school she went to university.
There are many pupils in our class.
Every graduate received a diploma.

exercises.explanation: На пе́рвом ку́рсе = in the first year.

lessons.title: 301. Applying to university: поступа́ть, заявле́ние, ко́нкурс, экза́мен
lessons.subtitle: Она́ подала́ докуме́нты и поступи́ла на бюдже́т.

explanations.title: To apply, to be accepted
explanations.body: Поступа́ть (imperfective) means to apply, or to be going through the admissions process. Поступи́ть (perfective) means you got in.

rows: to be accepted to a university

examples.text: Она́ поступа́ла в МГУ три го́да.
examples.translation: She tried to get into MSU for three years.
He got into MSU.

explanations.title: The admissions process
explanations.body: Applicants submit a заявле́ние and documents, take exams, and compete in a ко́нкурс. A successful applicant may get a бюдже́тное ме́сто, a place with no tuition.

examples.translation: There is a big competition for this department.
He got a tuition-free place.

explanations.title: Aspect: process or result
explanations.body: Поступа́ть describes the effort; поступи́ть reports success. In the past you can say the first about a try, the second about the result.

examples.translation: Have you got into university yet?

exercises.promptTranslation: She submitted her documents to the university.

exercises.prompt: Он ___ в университе́т три го́да, но не попа́л. (kept applying)
exercises.promptTranslation: He applied to university for three years but did not get in.
At last he got into university!
There is a big competition for this department.
Tomorrow I take my last exam.
She wrote an application and collected her documents.

exercises.prompt: Which verb means ‘to pass an exam’?

lessons.title: 302. Knowledge and skills: зна́ния, на́вык, о́пыт, спосо́бность
lessons.subtitle: У неё хоро́шие зна́ния и большо́й о́пыт.

explanations.title: What you know and can do
explanations.body: A few nouns describe what a person brings to study or work.

examples.translation: She has good knowledge.
This skill develops over the years.

explanations.title: Subjects and sciences
explanations.body: A предме́т is a school subject. Нау́ка is science, and the adjective is нау́чный.

examples.translation: My favorite subject is history.
He is busy with scientific work.

explanations.title: Capable people
explanations.body: Спосо́бный means capable or gifted. It can stand alone or take a verb: спосо́бен + infinitive.

rows: He has a talent for languages.

examples.translation: This is a very gifted pupil.

exercises.promptTranslation: She has good knowledge.
This skill develops over the years.
My favorite subject is history.
He has a lot of work experience.
This is a very gifted pupil.
She does scientific work.

lessons.title: 303. Developing and achieving: развива́ть, достига́ть, добива́ться, относи́ться к
lessons.subtitle: Она́ доби́лась успе́ха и дости́гла свое́й це́ли.

explanations.title: Reaching a goal: two verbs with the genitive
explanations.body: Both достига́ть / дости́чь and добива́ться / доби́ться take the genitive. The second stresses effort and persistence.

examples.translation: We reached our goal.
She achieved success.
He worked a long time for this result.

explanations.title: Developing
explanations.body: Развива́ть is transitive: you develop something. Развива́ться is intransitive: something develops by itself. The noun is разви́тие.

examples.translation: The school develops children's abilities.
The business is developing quickly.

explanations.title: Discuss, consider, attitude
explanations.body: Several useful verbs and nouns of thinking go with particular cases.

examples.translation: She treats her colleagues well.

exercises.promptTranslation: She achieved success.
We reached our goal.
The school pays attention to foreign languages.

exercises.prompt: Вчера́ мы це́лый час ___ э́тот вопро́с. (discussed)
exercises.promptTranslation: Yesterday we discussed this question for a whole hour.
She treats her colleagues well.
The business is developing quickly.
The school develops children's abilities.
He thinks that this is important.

exercises.prompt: In ‘Я счита́ю его́ хоро́шим учи́телем’ the noun учи́телем is in the:

lessons.title: 304. Prospects and demand: перспекти́вный, спрос, ры́нок труда́
lessons.subtitle: На ры́нке труда́ большо́й спрос на специали́стов.

explanations.title: The labor market
explanations.body: Ры́нок труда́ is the job market. Спрос на + accusative is demand for something, and a востре́бованный specialist is one in demand.

examples.text: На ры́нке труда́ большо́й спрос на специали́стов.
examples.translation: On the job market there is great demand for specialists.
This major is in high demand.

explanations.title: Prospects
explanations.body: Перспекти́вы is usually plural. The adjective перспекти́вный describes something with potential.

examples.translation: A young specialist has good prospects.

explanations.title: Size, difficulty and extras
explanations.body: Four adjectives help you describe situations in reports.

examples.translation: The government allocated additional funds.
This figure is very significant.

exercises.prompt: На ры́нке труда́ большо́й ___ на специали́стов. (demand)
exercises.promptTranslation: There is great demand for specialists on the job market.
These specialists are in high demand.
A young specialist has good prospects.
This is a very promising project.
The government allocated additional funds.
This figure is very significant.

exercises.prompt: What follows спрос when you name the product?

lessons.title: 305. Nobody, nothing: ни- words with prepositions (ни о чём не, ни с кем не)
lessons.subtitle: Мы ни о чём не говори́ли и ни с кем не спо́рили.

explanations.title: One не, many ни-
explanations.body: A Russian sentence normally has one не, right before the verb. Any other negative words are built with ни-, and the verb must still be negated.

examples.translation: The children have never worked anywhere.

explanations.title: When there is a preposition
explanations.body: If кто or что needs a preposition, the preposition goes between ни and the pronoun. The preposition always wins its place: ни о чём, ни с кем.

rows: Я ни о чём не пишу́.
Мы ни с кем не рабо́таем.
Он ни у кого́ не спроси́л.
Она́ ни к кому́ не идёт.
Он ни на что не жа́луется.
Мы ни о како́м фи́льме не говори́м.

examples.text: Я ни о чём не пишу́.
examples.translation: I am not writing about anything.

examples.text: Мы ни с кем не рабо́таем.
examples.translation: We don't work with anyone.

explanations.title: Case and writing
explanations.body: Write ни and the preposition as separate words. The pronoun still takes the case that the preposition requires.

rows: ни у кого́, ни от кого́, ни для кого́
ни от чего́, ни для чего́

examples.text: Он ни от кого́ не зави́сит.
examples.translation: He doesn't depend on anyone.

exercises.explanation: The preposition splits ни and что.
exercises.promptTranslation: I am not writing about anything.
We don't work with anyone.
He doesn't depend on anyone.
She isn't going to see anyone.
He doesn't complain about anything.
We aren't talking about any movie.
She never reads.

options: Я ни о ком не ду́маю.
Я не ни о ком ду́маю.
exercises.explanation: Ни + preposition + pronoun, and не before the verb.

exercises.prompt: How many words does ‘with nobody’ take here?

lessons.title: 306. Not a single one: ни оди́н, ни ра́зу, ни сло́ва, ни за что
lessons.subtitle: Он ни ра́зу не опозда́л и ни сло́ва не сказа́л.

explanations.title: Emphatic ни: not even one
explanations.body: Ни before a noun gives the idea ‘not even one’. The verb is still negative.

examples.translation: He was not late even once.
She did not say a word.

examples.text: У меня́ нет ни одно́й свобо́дной мину́ты.
examples.translation: I don't have a single free minute.

explanations.title: Ни … ни … and fixed phrases
explanations.body: The pair ни … ни … means ‘neither … nor …’. Some fixed phrases with ни are worth learning whole.

examples.text: Ни Бо́ря, ни Ле́на не пришли́.
examples.translation: Neither Borya nor Lena came.

examples.text: Ни за что не пойду́ туда́!
examples.translation: No way I'm going there!

explanations.title: Genitive after ни одного
explanations.body: After ни оди́н the noun is in the singular and agrees in gender. In the genitive after нет, use ни одного́ / ни одно́й.

examples.translation: Not a single female student came.

exercises.promptTranslation: He was not late even once.
She didn't say a word.

exercises.prompt: У меня́ нет ни одно́й ___ мину́ты. (free)
exercises.promptTranslation: I don't have a single free minute.
Not a single student came.
Not a single female student came.
There is not a single pupil in the class.

exercises.prompt: ‘Ни Бо́ря, ни Ле́на не пришли́’ means:
In ‘Он ни ра́зу не опозда́л’ the не is needed because:
exercises.explanation: Ни words need не before the verb.

lessons.title: 307. Nowhere to go: Мне не́где рабо́тать, нам не́куда идти́
lessons.subtitle: Ему́ не́когда, а нам не́куда идти́.

explanations.title: A negative idea with a positive verb
explanations.body: Compare: ‘I don't work anywhere’ (Я нигде́ не рабо́таю) and ‘there is nowhere for me to work’ (Мне не́где рабо́тать). In the second sentence the verb is positive, so the word is built with не instead of ни.

examples.translation: I have nowhere to work.
We have nowhere to go.
She has no time.

explanations.title: The pattern
explanations.body: The person is in the dative. The не́- word comes next, then an infinitive. There is no nominative subject. The не is always stressed.

examples.translation: He has nothing to do.

explanations.title: Past and future
explanations.body: Because there is no subject, the past tense is always бы́ло and the future is always бу́дет.

examples.translation: Yesterday we had nowhere to go.

exercises.prompt: Мне ___ рабо́тать в э́том го́роде. (nowhere to)
exercises.promptTranslation: I have nowhere to work in this town.
We have nowhere to go.
He had nothing to do.

exercises.prompt: За́втра у меня́ экза́мен, и мне ___ гуля́ть. (no time to)
exercises.promptTranslation: Tomorrow I have an exam and have no time to walk.
Yesterday we had nowhere to go.
Tomorrow we will have nowhere to go.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means ‘there is nowhere for me to work’?
In ‘Нам не́куда идти́’ the word нам is in the:
exercises.explanation: The person is in the dative.

exercises.prompt: Where does the stress fall in не́куда?
exercises.explanation: A stressed не marks the positive negative.

lessons.title: 308. Nothing to read, no one to ask: не́чего, не́кого, не́кому, не́ с кем
lessons.subtitle: Мне не́ с кем бы́ло говори́ть, и не́кому бы́ло помо́чь.

explanations.title: The forms of не́чего and не́кого
explanations.body: These words decline like что and кто, but with a stressed не in front. The case shows what the infinitive needs.

examples.translation: I have nothing to read.
He has no one to ask.
We have nothing to write with.

explanations.title: With prepositions
explanations.body: A preposition splits the word into two, exactly as with ни-, and the stress stays on не.

examples.text: Мне не́ с кем бы́ло говори́ть.
examples.translation: I had no one to talk to.
We have nothing to tell about.

examples.text: — Спаси́бо за кни́гу! — Не́ за что.
examples.translation: “Thanks for the book!” “You're welcome.”

explanations.title: не́кому: no one who can
explanations.body: Не́кому with an infinitive means that there is nobody around to do something. The missing person is the one who would do it.

rows: There is no one to work.
There was no one to help.
There will be no one to answer.

examples.translation: In the daytime there is no one to play with the dog.

exercises.promptTranslation: I have nothing to read.
He has no one to ask.
We have nothing to write with.

exercises.prompt: Мне ___ бы́ло говори́ть. (no one to talk to)
exercises.promptTranslation: I had no one to talk to.
We have nothing to tell about.

exercises.prompt: Днём ___ игра́ть с соба́кой. (no one to)
exercises.explanation: The missing player is the subject: dative не́кому.
exercises.promptTranslation: In the daytime there is no one to play with the dog.
“Thanks for the gift!” “You're welcome.”

exercises.prompt: Which means ‘nothing to be surprised at’?
In ‘Мне не́ с кем бы́ло говори́ть’ which part carries the stress?

lessons.title: 309. Ни- or не́-? Мы никуда́ не идём, потому́ что нам не́куда идти́
lessons.subtitle: Он нигде́ не рабо́тает: ему́ не́где рабо́тать.

explanations.title: Two patterns, one idea
explanations.body: The ни- pattern describes what happens: negative verb, ни- word. The не́- pattern explains why: positive infinitive, не́- word.

examples.text: Мы никуда́ не идём: нам не́куда идти́.
examples.translation: We aren't going anywhere: we have nowhere to go.

explanations.title: Choosing
explanations.body: If you can say ‘there is nowhere / nothing / no one to …’, use не́-. If you can say ‘does not … anywhere / anything / anyone’, use ни- with не.

rows: I have no one to ask here.

examples.text: Он ничего́ не чита́ет, потому́ что ему́ не́чего чита́ть.
examples.translation: He reads nothing because he has nothing to read.

explanations.title: Mini-dialogue
explanations.body: Ask with a question word, answer with ни-, explain with не́-.

examples.text: — Что ты чита́ешь? — Я ничего́ не чита́ю: мне не́когда.
examples.translation: “What are you reading?” “Nothing: I have no time.”

exercises.promptTranslation: We aren't going anywhere.
We have nowhere to go.
He doesn't read anything.
He has nothing to read.
I don't know anyone here.
I have no one to ask here.

exercises.prompt: Она́ ___ не смо́трит телеви́зор, потому́ что ей не́когда. (never)
exercises.promptTranslation: She never watches TV because she has no time.

exercises.prompt: ‘He works nowhere, because there's nowhere to work.’
options: Он нигде́ не рабо́тает, потому́ что ему́ не́где рабо́тать.
Он не́где не рабо́тает, потому́ что ему́ нигде́ рабо́тать.
Он нигде́ рабо́тает, потому́ что ему́ не́где рабо́тать.
Он не рабо́тает нигде́, потому́ что не́где ему́ не рабо́тать.
exercises.explanation: ни- with a negated verb, then не́- with an infinitive.

lessons.title: 310. Review: education, applying and negation
lessons.subtitle: Он поступи́л на бюдже́т и ни о чём не жале́ет.

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: Study vocabulary: поступа́ть / поступи́ть, подава́ть докуме́нты, сдава́ть экза́мен, зна́ния, на́вык, спрос на. Negation: ни- with не and a preposition between; не́- with a dative and an infinitive.

rows: Я ни о чём не пишу́.

examples.text: Ей не́ с кем бы́ло говори́ть.
examples.translation: She had no one to talk to.

exercises.promptTranslation: He got a tuition-free place.
She submitted her documents to the university.

exercises.prompt: На ры́нке труда́ большо́й ___ на программи́стов. (demand)
exercises.promptTranslation: There is great demand for programmers.
He doesn't regret anything.
We don't work with anyone.
We have nowhere to go.
Yesterday he had nothing to do.
She achieved success.

options: Я ничего́ не де́лаю: мне не́чего де́лать.
Я не́чего не де́лаю: мне ничего́ де́лать.
Я ничего́ де́лаю: мне не́чего не де́лать.
Я не́чего де́лаю: мне ничего́ не де́лать.
exercises.explanation: Ни- with не, then не́- with infinitive.

units.title: Unit 31: Reflexive verbs, себя' and word-building

lessons.title: 311. What -ся does: умыва́ться, встреча́ться, боя́ться
lessons.subtitle: Мы ча́сто встреча́емся, и она́ всегда́ улыба́ется.

explanations.title: Reflexive: the action returns to the subject
explanations.body: The ending -ся is a short form of себя́. In reflexive verbs the doer and the receiver are the same person.

examples.translation: The little boy already washes up by himself.
She is preparing for the exam.

explanations.title: Reciprocal: each other
explanations.body: In reciprocal verbs the people act on each other. The -ся here could be replaced by друг дру́га.

rows: to get to know each other

examples.translation: We often meet at a café.
They met at university.

explanations.title: Verbs that exist only with -ся
explanations.body: Many common verbs have no form without -ся. You simply learn them as they are.

examples.translation: The shop is located in the center.
I am afraid of dogs.

exercises.promptTranslation: The little boy already washes up by himself.
We often meet at a café.
She is preparing for the exam.
I am afraid of dogs.
She always smiles when she sees us.
The shop is located in the center.

exercises.prompt: Они́ ___ в университе́те. (got to know each other)
exercises.promptTranslation: They met at university.

exercises.explanation: Себя́ is the full reflexive pronoun.

lessons.title: 312. Things get done: Рейс отменя́ется, це́ны поднима́ются
lessons.subtitle: Авиакомпа́ния отменя́ет рейс. — Рейс отменя́ется.

explanations.title: The object becomes the subject
explanations.body: To describe an action without saying who does it, take a transitive verb, make its object the subject, and add -ся. The verb agrees with the new subject.

examples.translation: The flight is being cancelled because of the weather.
Gas prices are rising.

explanations.title: Naming the doer
explanations.body: If you still want to mention who does it, put the doer in the instrumental case.

rows: The house is being built by workers.
The flight is cancelled by the airline.

examples.translation: The house is being built by workers.

explanations.title: Only imperfective, only with objects
explanations.body: This construction is normally imperfective: it describes a process or a general rule. Verbs that cannot take an object do not add -ся: рейс прилета́ет, пла́мя бушу́ет.

rows: has a direct object, so -ся is possible

examples.translation: The flight arrives on time.

exercises.promptTranslation: The airline cancels the flight.
The flight is being cancelled because of the weather.
The authorities are raising gas prices.
Gas prices are rising.
The workers are building a new house.
The new house is being built by workers.

exercises.prompt: Э́ти услу́ги ___ по ни́зким це́нам. (are offered)
exercises.promptTranslation: These services are offered at low prices.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence has the doer in the instrumental?

lessons.title: 313. With or without -ся: меня́ть / меня́ться, продолжа́ть / продолжа́ться
lessons.subtitle: Компа́ния меня́ет це́ны, и це́ны меня́ются.

explanations.title: A simple test
explanations.body: If there is a direct object in the accusative, use the verb without -ся. If the subject is itself what changes, starts or ends, use -ся.

examples.translation: The company is changing its prices.
Prices are changing.

explanations.title: More pairs
explanations.body: These pairs often appear in news and reports.

examples.translation: The government lowered the tax.
The tax went down.

explanations.title: People vs. things
explanations.body: -Ся also appears when a person does something to themselves: остановиться (stop), измениться (change). The test is still the same: no direct object.

examples.translation: The lesson ended at three o'clock.

exercises.promptTranslation: The company changes its prices.
Prices are changing.
The government lowered the tax.
The tax went down.
The driver stopped the car.
The car stopped.
The lesson ended at three o'clock.
The teacher finished the lesson at three o'clock.

lessons.title: 314. Three ways to say it: отменя́ется, отменя́ют, отменён
lessons.subtitle: Рейс отменя́ется. Рейс отменя́ют. Рейс отменён.

explanations.title: Same idea, three tools
explanations.body: When the doer is unknown or unimportant, Russian offers three constructions.

rows: someone does it, we don't know who

examples.translation: Prices are rising. — They are raising the prices.

explanations.title: Past and future
explanations.body: In the past and the future, the third option adds a form of быть.

examples.translation: The problem will not be resolved.
The concert was cancelled.

explanations.title: Choosing
explanations.body: The participle fits official reports and finished results. The they-form is natural in speech. The -ся form describes what is happening to the subject.

examples.translation: The flight is cancelled.

exercises.promptTranslation: They cancelled the flight because of the snowfall.
The flight has been cancelled because of the snowfall.
The concert was cancelled because of the rain.
The problem will not be resolved.
The problem will not be resolved.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence has no stated doer and uses the они́-form?
Which suits an official airport announcement?
Convert to the past with a participle: ‘Прое́кт не реши́тся’.

lessons.title: 315. The pronoun себя́: себя́, себе́, собо́й, о себе́
lessons.subtitle: Он ду́мает то́лько о себе́, а она́ ре́дко покупа́ет себе́ что́-то.

explanations.title: Forms of себя́
explanations.body: Себя́ reflects the subject back: ‘myself, himself, themselves’ and so on. Its forms are those of ты, with с instead of т.

examples.translation: He thinks only of himself.

explanations.title: No nominative
explanations.body: Себя́ always refers back to the subject of the sentence, so it has no nominative form and can never be a subject.

examples.translation: Masha rarely buys herself anything.
They see themselves in the mirror.

explanations.title: Ме́жду собо́й
explanations.body: With plural subjects ме́жду собо́й means ‘among themselves’, ‘with each other’.

rows: They speak German to each other.

examples.translation: They speak German to each other.

exercises.promptTranslation: He thinks only of himself.
She sees herself in the mirror.
He bought himself a new car.
We are pleased with ourselves.
They speak German to each other.
She doesn't believe in herself.

exercises.prompt: Себя́ has no form in the:
exercises.explanation: It can never be a subject.

exercises.prompt: Which pronoun matches Он ду́мает о ___?
exercises.explanation: The subject and the one thought about are the same person.

lessons.title: 316. To my place, with me, to myself: к себе́, у себя́, с собо́й, про себя́
lessons.subtitle: Приходи́ ко мне — нет, к себе́ я не приглашу́.

explanations.title: Home and ownership
explanations.body: Себя́ with a preposition often points to ‘my own place’. The subject decides whose.

rows: I'm going home / to my room.

examples.text: Я приглашу́ вас к себе́ на вечери́нку.
examples.translation: I'll invite you to my place for a party.
Is the manager in his office?

explanations.title: With me, to myself
explanations.body: С собо́й is used for what a person takes or carries with them.

examples.text: Он берёт дете́й с собо́й на рабо́ту.
examples.translation: He takes his kids to work with him.
The cyclone will bring rain with it.

explanations.title: Doors: на себя́ and от себя́
explanations.body: On doors, на себя́ means pull and от себя́ means push. The direction is relative to the person acting.

examples.translation: On the door it says ‘pull’.

exercises.prompt: Я приглашу́ вас ___ на вечери́нку. (to my place)
exercises.promptTranslation: I'll invite you to my place for a party.

“For here or to go?”

The door says ‘pull’.

exercises.promptTranslation: He said it to himself so that nobody would hear.

options: I'm going home / to my room.
exercises.explanation: К себе́ = to one's own place.

lessons.title: 317. Verb phrases with себя́: чу́вствовать себя́, вести́ себя́, позво́лить себе́
lessons.subtitle: Она́ хорошо́ себя́ чу́вствует и взяла́ на себя́ отве́тственность.

explanations.title: Feeling and behaving
explanations.body: Two phrases you already know take себя́ in the accusative.

examples.translation: How are you feeling?

explanations.title: Taking, allowing, imagining
explanations.body: Other fixed phrases use себя́ or себе́.

examples.translation: She took responsibility upon herself.

examples.text: Я не могу́ позво́лить себе́ тако́й тур.

explanations.title: Seeing and thinking of oneself
explanations.body: Several verbs of perception and thought take себя́ as an object.

rows: I don't see myself as a coach.

examples.translation: He considers himself a specialist.

exercises.promptTranslation: How are you feeling?

lessons.title: 318. Word-building: крат / корот, пуск / пуст, прав, ступ
lessons.subtitle: Выпускни́к, упуще́ние, исправля́ть, поступа́ть — одни́ и те же ко́рни.

explanations.title: КРАТ – КОРОТ: short
explanations.body: Both roots mean ‘short’. Прекраща́ть is to make something stop (cut it short), and сокраща́ть is to shorten.

examples.translation: They shortened the working day.
Give a brief answer.

explanations.title: ПУСК – ПУСТ: let go
explanations.body: The root means ‘let go, release, allow’.

examples.translation: He missed the opportunity.

explanations.title: ПРАВ and СТУП
explanations.body: Прав means ‘right, direct’. Ступ means ‘step, act’.

examples.translation: He corrected the mistake.
This is a good deed.
She gave up her seat on the bus.

lessons.title: 319. Review: -ся, себя́ and word roots
lessons.subtitle: Це́ны поднима́ются, а она́ ве́дёт себя́ споко́йно.

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: The ending -ся can mean reflexive, reciprocal, or passive-like. Use it when there is no direct object. Себя́ has no nominative; its forms are себя́, себе́, собо́й, о себе́.

rows: к себе́, у себя́, с собо́й, про себя́
чу́вствовать себя́, вести́ себя́, позво́лить себе́

examples.text: Це́ны поднима́ются, а она́ ве́дёт себя́ споко́йно.

units.title: Unit 32: Work, pay and the job market

lessons.title: 320. Jobs and employers: работода́тель, рабо́тник, руководи́тель, предприя́тие
lessons.subtitle: Рабо́тник пришёл к руководи́телю предприя́тия.

explanations.title: People at work
explanations.body: Russian has several words for the people in a workplace. Рабо́тник and сотру́дник can both mean ‘employee’; the second also means ‘colleague’.

examples.translation: The employer is looking for a new employee.
The owner of the firm is a young woman.

explanations.title: Places of work
explanations.body: Use на with предприя́тие (an enterprise, factory) and в with компа́ния and фи́рма.

examples.translation: She works at an enterprise.
He works in a small firm.

explanations.title: Positions
explanations.body: До́лжность (f.) is a position or job title. Штат, in the sense of workforce, is a collective noun.

examples.translation: He holds the position of manager.

exercises.promptTranslation: The employer is looking for a new employee.

lessons.title: 321. Finding work: вака́нсия, резюме́, собесе́дование, стаж, устро́иться на рабо́ту
lessons.subtitle: Она́ пошла́ на собесе́дование и устро́илась на рабо́ту.

explanations.title: Vacancies and interviews
explanations.body: These words appear in every job advertisement.

examples.translation: We have an opening.

examples.text: На собесе́довании её спроси́ли об о́пыте.
examples.translation: At the interview they asked her about her experience.

explanations.title: Who hires, who gets hired
explanations.body: The employer нанима́ет / нанял. The candidate устра́ивается / устро́ился на рабо́ту. Use на + accusative with рабо́ту, and в + accusative with a company.

rows: Анна устро́илась на рабо́ту в компа́нию.

examples.text: Анна устро́илась на рабо́ту в компа́нию.

The company hired a new employee.

explanations.title: Contract and conditions
explanations.body: Once hired, the employee signs a контра́кт and discusses усло́вия (conditions).

examples.translation: The working conditions are good.

lessons.title: 322. Pay and expenses: зарпла́та, дохо́д, расхо́ды, нало́г, посо́бие
lessons.subtitle: Дохо́ды ра́стут, но и расхо́ды то́же.

explanations.title: Money coming in
explanations.body: Several words describe money received. Дохо́д is the broadest.

examples.translation: She has a good salary.
The family's income rose.

explanations.title: To earn and to save
explanations.body: Зараба́тывать / зарабо́тать is to earn by working. Эконо́мить / сэконо́мить is to save, with на and the prepositional case.

examples.translation: He earns well.
We save on transport.

explanations.title: Salary talk
explanations.body: Questions about pay are common in job interviews and surveys.

rows: What expenses does the family have?

examples.translation: What taxes do you pay?

exercises.promptTranslation: She has a good salary.
The family's income rose.

lessons.title: 323. Raising and lowering: повыша́ть, снижа́ть, увели́чивать, уменьша́ть
lessons.subtitle: Зарпла́та повы́силась на пять проце́нтов.

explanations.title: Four pairs of verbs
explanations.body: Each pair has an imperfective and a perfective form. All of them take an object. Add -ся to get ‘goes up’ or ‘goes down’.

examples.translation: The government raised pensions.
Pensions rose.

explanations.title: The nouns
explanations.body: The nouns are повыше́ние, сниже́ние, увеличе́ние, уменьше́ние. Повыше́ние can also mean promotion.

examples.translation: She got a promotion.
The tax reduction helped business.

explanations.title: By how much?
explanations.body: Use на + accusative for the amount of change, в + genitive for ‘times’, and с … до for ‘from … to’.

examples.translation: Expenses fell by five percent.
Income increased twofold.

lessons.subtitle: В э́той о́трасли высо́кая конкуре́нция, и мно́гих уво́лили.

explanations.title: Employment and unemployment
explanations.body: Reports on the economy use a small set of nouns.

examples.translation: Unemployment is growing in the region.
The unemployed receive benefits.

explanations.title: Branches of the economy
explanations.body: A branch of the economy is an о́трасль or a сфе́ра. Use в + prepositional.

examples.translation: She works in the retail trade.
There is little work in this sector.

explanations.title: Hiring and firing
explanations.body: Two aspect pairs describe the employer's decisions.

examples.translation: The company fired fifty workers.
The dismissal was unexpected.

lessons.subtitle: Он стреми́тся к успе́ху и уве́рен в себе́.

explanations.title: Verbs and the cases they need
explanations.body: Many verbs of this lesson take a particular preposition or case. Learn each verb with its partner.

examples.translation: The weather influences mood.
This concerns everyone.

explanations.title: Nouns: влия́ние and потре́бность
explanations.body: The related nouns take the same prepositions: влия́ние на and потре́бность в.

examples.translation: There is a need for new specialists.

explanations.title: Small but useful
explanations.body: Four words that appear often in reports.

examples.text: В тече́ние ме́сяца мы жда́ли отве́та.

lessons.title: 326. Word-building: им / ём, треб, влад, раб
lessons.subtitle: Заём, приём, наём — один корень; владеть и обладать — другой.

explanations.title: ИМ / ЁМ / ЕМ / ЙМ / Я: take, have
explanations.body: This root changes shape. You have already seen it in взять, занять and снять.

examples.translation: Document admission starts in July.
We have an advantage.

explanations.title: ТРЕБ and ВЛАД
explanations.body: Треб means ‘require, need’. Влад means ‘possess, control’.

explanations.title: РАБ: work
explanations.body: The root work forms many verbs with prefixes.

examples.translation: The engineers developed a new program.

lessons.subtitle: Компа́ния наняла́ но́вого сотру́дника и повы́сила зарпла́ту.

explanations.title: What to remember
explanations.body: Hiring: нанима́ть / наня́ть (employer), устро́иться на рабо́ту (candidate). Money: зарпла́та, дохо́д, расхо́ды, нало́г. Change: повыша́ть / повы́сить, снижа́ть / сни́зить with -ся when there is no object. Cases: влия́ть на + acc., стреми́ться к + dat., уве́рен в + prep., каса́ться + gen.
